ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಮರುದ್ಭಿಃ ಸಹ ಮಂದಸಾನಃ ಸನ್ ಸೋಮಂ ಪಿಬ । ಕೀದೃಶೈರ್ಮರುದ್ಭಿಃ ।

ಶುಭಯದ್ಭಿಃ ಶೋಭಮಾನೈರನ್ಯಾನ್ ಶೋಭಯದ್ಭಿರ್ವಾ ಋಕ್ವಭಿಃ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯೈರ್ಗಣಶ್ರಿಭಿರ್ಗಣಭಾವಮಾಶ್ರಯದ್ಭಿಃ ಪಾವಕೇಭಿಃ ಶೋಧಕೈರ್ವಿಶ್ವಮಿನ್ವೇಭಿರ್ವಿಶ್ವಂ ವೃಷ್ಟಾ ಪ್ರೀಣಯದ್ಧಿರಾಯುಭಿರಾಯುಷ್ಮದ್ಭಿಃ । ಹೇ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ವಿಶ್ವನರಹಿತಾಗ್ನೇ ಪ್ರದಿವಾ ಪುರಾಣೇನ ಕೇತುನಾ ಜ್ವಾಲಾಪುಂಜೇನ ಸಜೂಃ
ಗಣಶ್ರಿಭಿಃ-ಸಂಘರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿಕೊಂಡಿರುವವರೂ । ಪಾವಕೇಭಿಃ-ಶುದ್ಧಿಕಾರಕರೂ । ವಿಶ್ವಮಿನ್ವೇಭಿಃವೃಷ್ಟಿಯಿಂದ ಜಗತ್ತಿಗೆ ತೃಪ್ತಿಕಾರಕರೂ । ಆಯುಭಿಃ-ಚಿರಾಯುಗಳೂ ಆದ । ಮರುದ್ಭಿಃ-ಮರುತ್ತುಗಳೊಡನೆ ।
ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನರೂ, ಸ್ತುತ್ಯರೂ, ಸಂಘರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿಕೊಂಡಿರುವವರೂ, ಶುದ್ಧಿಕಾರ
ಕರೂ, ವೃಷ್ಟಿಯಿಂದ ಜಗತ್ತಿಗೆ ತೃಪ್ತಿಕಾರಕರೂ, ಚಿರಾಯುಗಳೂ ಆದ ಮರುತ್ತುಗಳೊಡನೆ ಸಂತೋಷವನ್ನನುಭವಿ
ಸುತ್ತಾ ಸೋಮವನ್ನು ಪಾನಮಾಡು. ವೈಶ್ವಾನರರೂಪಿಯಾದ ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಪುರಾತನವಾದ ನಿನ್ನ ಜ್ವಾಲಾರೂಪ
Agni, drink the Soma-juice, rejoicing, along with the Maruts,
resplendent, adorable, associated in troops, purifying all, animating
and long-lived : drink, Vaiswanara, who are identified with the ancient
ಆಗ್ನಿಮಾರುತದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವಾಗ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಮರುದ್ಭಿಃ ಎಂಬ ಈ ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನು
ಯಾಜ್ಯಾಮಂತ್ರವನ್ನಾಗಿ ಪಠಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನ ಶ್ರೌತಸೂತ್ರದ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಮರುದ್ಭಿಃ ಶುಭಯದ್ಭಿರ್ಯುಕ್ವಭಿಃ
ಈ ಯುಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಮರುದ್ದೇವತೆಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹರ್ಷಯುಕ್ತನಾಗಿ ಸೋಮಪಾನಮಾಡ
ಭಾಷ್ಯಕಾರರು ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಪೂರ್ವೇತಿಹಾಸವನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿರುವರು—
ಆರ್ತ್ವಿಜ್ಯಾಯ ವೃತೋ ಯಜ್ಞೇ ವಿತತೇ ಹೌತ್ರ ಆಸ್ಥಿತಃ ।
ಯಯಾಚೇ ಸ್ವಕುಮಾರಾಯ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವಾಯ ಚ ತಾಂ ಸುತಾಂ ।
ಇತಿ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾ ಪುನಃ ಪ್ರಾಹ ಕಥಮಸ್ಮೈ ಪ್ರದಾಸ್ಯಸಿ ।
ಇತಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ಸುತಾ ದತ್ತಾ ನಾಸೀದನೃಷಯೇ ಕ್ವಚಿತ್ ॥
ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವಃ ಸಂಸ್ಥಿತೇ ಯಜ್ಞೇ ತೇನ ರಾಜ್ಞಾ ನಿರಾಕೃತಃ ॥
ತಥೇತಿ ರಾಜ್ಯೋ ವಚನಂ ನಿಶಮ್ಯ ತದ್ಭಾರ್ಯಯಾ ದರ್ಶಿತಸರ್ವಮಾರ್ಗಃ ॥
ವಿಲೋಕ್ಯ ವಿಪ್ರಃ ಸಭಯಃ ಪ್ರಣಮ್ಯ ಕೃತಾಂಜಲಿಃ ಕಂಟಕಿತಾಂಗಸಂಘಃ ॥
ಸಂಪ್ರಾಸ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸ್ವಮನೀಷಿತಂ ತದಾ ಮರುದ್ಧಣೇಭ್ಯೋ ಮುದಿತಾತ್ಮವದ್ಧ್ಯಃ ॥
ಪಶ್ಚಾತ್ಸುನರ್ಗೃಹಂ ಗತ್ವಾ ಭೂಯೋ ಲಬ್ಧ್ವಾ ಗವಾಂ ಶತಂ ॥
ದಾರ್ಭ್ಯೋ ಮಂತ್ರದೃಶೇ ರಾಜ್ಞಾ ಚೋದಿತಃ ಸ್ವಸುತಾಂ ದದೌ ।
ದಾರ್ಭ್ಯೋ ಯೋ ರಥವೀತ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಃ ಸಪ್ತ ಯೇ ಮರುತಾಂ ಗಣಾಃ ।
ಆಗಮಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಪಾರಂಗತರಾದ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸರು ಅತ್ಯಾಶ್ಚರ್ಯಕರವಾದ ಒಂದು ಪೂರ್ವೇತಿಹಾಸವನ್ನು ಈ ರೀತಿ
ಹೇಳಿರುವರು—ಪೂರ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ಅತ್ರಿವಂಶೋತ್ಪನ್ನನಾದ ಅರ್ಚನಾನಾಃ ಎಂಬ ಋಷಿಯನ್ನು ರಥವೀತಿದಾರ್ಭ್ಯನೆಂಬ
ರಾಜರ್ಷಿಯು ತಾನು ಮಾಡುವ ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಪೌರೋಹಿತ್ಯವನ್ನು ವಹಿಸಿ ಯಜ್ಞವನ್ನು ನೆರವೇರಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಿ
ದನು. ರಾಜನ ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥನೆಯನ್ನಂಗೀಕರಿಸಿ ಅರ್ಚನಾನಸನು ತನ್ನ ಪುತ್ರನಾದ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನೊಂದಿಗೆ ರಾಜನ ಯಜ್ಞ
ಗೃಹಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಿ ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋತೃವೆಂಬ ಋತ್ವಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಪಾತ್ರವನ್ನು ವಹಿಸಿ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರತನಾಗಿದ್ದನು. ಹೀಗಿರು
ವಾಗ ಆ ರಥವೀತಿರಾಜನ ಸಮೀಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಕುಳಿತಿದ್ದ ರಾಜಪುತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ ಈ ಕನೈಯನ್ನು ತನ್ನ ಪುತ್ರನಾದ
ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ ಮದುವೆಮಾಡಿಕೊಡಬೇಕೆಂದು ರಾಜನನ್ನು ಕೇಳಿದನು. ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಆ ರಾಜನು ಸಮ್ಮಿತಿಸಿದರೂ ತನ್ನ
ಭಾರ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಈ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇಳಿ ಅವಳ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಯುವುದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಅಂತಃಪುರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಿ ತನ್ನ

ಪುತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು ಅರ್ಚನಾನಸಪುತ್ರನಾದ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ ಕೊಡುವ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿನ್ನ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವೇನೆಂದು ಕೇಳಿದನು. ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಅವನ ಭಾರ್ಯೆಯು ಎಲೈ ಭರ್ತೃವೇ, ನಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು ಈ ಶ್ವಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ ಕೊಡಲು ಹೇಗೆ ಸಾಧ್ಯ ? ಇವನು ಋಷಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಇದುವರೆಗೂ ನಮ್ಮ ವಂಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಋಷಿಯಲ್ಲದವರಿಗೆ ನಾವು ಕನ್ಯಾದಾನವನ್ನು ಮಾಡಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ ನಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು ವಿವಾಹಮಾಡಿಕೊಡಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ತನ್ನ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿದಳು. ರಾಜನೂ ಅದನ್ನೇ ಅನುಮೋದಿಸಿ ಅರ್ಚನಾನಸನಿಗೆ ಈ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಿದನು. ಈ ರೀತಿ ರಾಜನು ತನ್ನ ಮಾತನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸಲು ಯಜ್ಞ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವಾಗಲೇ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನು ಅಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಹೊರಟು ತನ್ನ ಆಶ್ರಮಕ್ಕೆ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿ ತೀವ್ರವಾದ ತಪಸ್ಸನ್ನಾಚರಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದನು. ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯವ್ರತವನ್ನು ನಿಯಮದಿಂದ ಪಾಲಿ ಸುತ್ತಾ ಶಾಂತಮನಸ್ಕನಾಗಿ ತಪಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದನು. ಒಂದು ದಿನಸ ಈ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನು ಭಿಕ್ಷಾಟನಮಾಡುತ್ತಿರು ವಾಗ ತರಂತನೆಂಬ ರಾಜನ ಪತ್ನಿಯೂ ಸಾಧ್ವಿಯೂ ಆದ ಶಶೀಯಸೀ ಎಂಬ ರಾಜಮಹಿಷಿಯನ್ನು ಭಿಕ್ಷಾರ್ಥವಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಿದನು. ಅದನ್ನು ಕೇಳಿ ರಾಜಪತ್ನಿಯು ತನ್ನ ಪತಿಯ ಬಳಿಗೆ ಹೋಗಿ ಭಿಕ್ಷಾರ್ಥವಾಗಿ ಋಷಿಯು ಬಂದಿರು ವುದನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಲು ರಾಜನು ಆ ಋಷಿಯನ್ನು ಉಚಿತವಾದ ಅತಿಥಿಸತ್ಕಾರಗಳಿಂದ ಪೂಜಿಸೆಂದು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ರಾಜನ ಅನುಜ್ಞೆಯಿಂದ ರಾಜಪತ್ನಿಯು ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವಋಷಿಗೆ ಅನೇಕ ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನೂ, ದಿವ್ಯಾಭರಣಗಳನ್ನೂ ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಸತ್ಕರಿಸಿ ದಳು. ತರಂತರಾಜನೂ ಸಹ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ ಬೇಕಾದಷ್ಟು ಧನಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಉಪಚರಿಸಿ ತನ್ನ ತಮ್ಮನಾದ ಪುರುಮೀಳನೆಂಬ ರಾಜನ ಬಳಿಗೆ ಹೋದಲ್ಲಿ ಅವನೂ ಸಹ ನಿನಗೆ ಯಥೇಚ್ಛವಾಗಿ ಧನಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಡುವನೆಂದು ಹೇಳಿ ಆವನ ಬಳಿಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿಕೊಟ್ಟನು. ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನು ರಾಜನ ಮಾತಿಗೆ ಸಮ್ಮತಿಸಿ ರಾಜಪತ್ನಿಯು ತೋರಿಸಿದ ಮಾರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಿರುವಾಗ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ತನಗೆ ಅಭಿಮುಖವಾಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತಿರುವ ಮರುದ್ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕಂಡನು. ಅವರೆಲ್ಲರೂ ಸಮಾನರೂಪ ಮತ್ತು ಆಕಾರವುಳ್ಳವರಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವುದನ್ನು ಈ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನು ನೋಡಿ ಭಯ ಭಕ್ತಿಯಿಂದ ಕೈ ಮುಗಿದುಕೊಂಡು ಪ್ರಸನ್ನಚಿತ್ತದಿಂದ ಆ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥಗರ್ಭಿತವಾದ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಿಂದ ನಾನಾ ವಿಧವಾಗಿ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರ ಮಾಡಿದನು. ಆ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರದಿಂದ ಆ ಮರುದ್ದೇವತೆಗಳು ತೃಪ್ತರಾಗಿ ಆ ಋಷಿಯ ಇಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥವು ಸಿದ್ಧಿಸಲೆಂದು ಅನುಗ್ರಹಿಸಿದರು. ಮತ್ತು ಮರುದ್ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸ್ತುತಿಸಿದ್ದರಿಂದ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನು ಸೂಕ್ತದ್ರಷ್ಟವಾದ ಋಷಿಯಾದನು. ಈ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿದು ರಥವೀತಿರಾಜನು ಅವನ ಪತ್ನಿಯೂ ಸಹ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನ ಗೃಹಕ್ಕೆ ಬಂದು ಮಂತ್ರದ್ರಷ್ಟವಾದ ಅವನಿಗೆ ನೂರು ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಸತ್ಕರಿಸಿ ತಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು ವಿವಾಹಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟರು. ಈ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ ಎಂದರೆ—ಪುರುಮಿಳ, ತರಂತ, ಅವನ ಪತ್ನಿಶಶೀಯಸೀ, ದಾರ್ಭರಥವೀತಿ ರಾಜನು, ಸಪ್ತಮರುದ್ಧಣಗಳು ಇವರೆಲ್ಲರೂ ತನಗೆ (ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವನಿಗೆ) ಏನೇನನ್ನು ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಉಪಚರಿಸಿದರೋ ಅದೆಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ಶ್ಯಾವಾಶ್ವಋಷಿಯು ಕೇ ಷ್ಠಾ ನರಃ ಎಂಬ ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಣಿಸಿದ್ದಾನೆ.

ಒಬ್ಬರಲ್ಲೊಬ್ಬರಿಗಿರುವ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದಳು. ರಾಜನು ತನ್ನ ಪತ್ನಿಯಾದ ಈ ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅತ್ಯಂತ

ವಾಗುವುದು. ಪತಿಯ ಅನುರಾಗಸೂಚಕವಾದ ಆಲಿಂಗನಾದಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಇವನ ಪತ್ನಿಯು ಪಾತ್ರಳಾಗಿದ್ದಳು ಎಂದು
ಮುಖ್ಯಾಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವು. ಪತಿಯ ಪ್ರೀತ್ಯಾದರಗಳಿಗೆ ಪಾತ್ರಳಾದ ಇಂತಹ ಈ ರಾಜಮಹಿಷಿಯು ರಾಜನ ಅನುಜ್ಞೆ
ಯಿಂದ ತನಗೆ ಅನೇಕ ಅಶ್ವಗಳನ್ನೂ, ಪಶುಗಳನ್ನೂ, ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನೂ ಆಡುಗಳನ್ನೂ ನೂರುಗಟ್ಟಲೆಯಾಗಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ
ಉತ ತ್ವಾ ಸ್ತ್ರೀ ಶಶೀಯಸೀ ಪುಂಸೋ ಭವತಿ ವಸ್ಯಸೀ ।
ಉತ । ತ್ವಾ । ಸ್ತ್ರೀ । ಶಶೀಯಸೀ । ಪುಂಸಃ । ಭವತಿ । ವಸ್ಯಸೀ ।
ಉತಾಪಿ ಚ ತ್ವೈಕಾ ಶಶೀಯಸೀ । ಶಶೀಯಸೀತ್ಯೇತನಮಹಿಷ್ಯಾ ನಾಮ । ಸೈವ ಸ್ತ್ರೀ । ಯದ್ವಾ।
ವಚನಾತ್ ತ್ವೇತಿ ನಿಘಾತಃ ॥ ಸೈವ ಪುಂಸಃ ಪುರುಷಾದ್ವಸ್ಯಸೀ ವಸೀಯಸೀ ಭವತಿ । ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪುಂಸ
ಇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ । ಆದೇವತ್ರಾತ್ । ದೇವಾ ನ ಯೇನ ತ್ರಾಯಂತೇ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ಸೋಽದೇವತ್ರಃ ।
ಅದೇವತ್ರಾತ್—ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂಜಿಸದೇ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ಅವರ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಗೆ ಪಾತ್ರನಾಗದವನೂ
ಉತ ತ್ವಾ ಶಶೀಯಸೀ—ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯೊಬ್ಬಳೇ । ಸ್ತ್ರೀ—ಹೆಂಗಸಾಗಿದ್ದರೂ ಸಹ । ವಸ್ಯಸೀ—ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟಳಾಗಿ
ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂಜಿಸದೇ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ಅವರ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಗೆ ಪಾತ್ರನಾಗದವನೂ, ದಾನಕ್ಕೆ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತವಾದ
ಧನವಿಲ್ಲದವನೂ ಆದ ಪುರುಷನಿಗಿಂತಲೂ, ಹೆಂಗಸಾಗಿದ್ದರೂ ಸಹ ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯೇ ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟಳು.
Sasiyasi, though a female, is more excellent than a man who
reverences not the gods, nor bestows wealth.
ಸಾಧಾರಣವಾಗಿ ಪುರುಷರು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಾದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ, ಪರಾಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ, ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ
ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯರಿಗಿಂತ ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟರು ಎಂಬ ಭಾವನೆಯು ರೂಢಿಯಲ್ಲಿದೆ. ಪುರುಷರಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಸಹ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂಜಿಸದೆ
ಎಂದರೆ ಯಜ್ಞಯಾಗಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡದೆ, ದಾನ ಧರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಆಚರಿಸದೆ, ಜನರಿಗೆ ಯಾವ ವಿಧವಾದ ಉಪಕಾರ
ವನ್ನೂ ಮಾಡದೆ ಕೇವಲ ಲೋಭಿತನದಿಂದ ವರ್ತಿಸುವ ಪುರುಷರು, ಪುರುಷವರ್ಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರಿದ್ದರೂ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠರಲ್ಲ.
ಜನರಿಗೆ ಇವರಲ್ಲಿ ಗೌರವಾದರಗಳಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಇಂತಹ ಕೆಟ್ಟ ಸ್ವಭಾವದ ಪುರುಷರಿಗಿಂತ ದಾನ ಧರ್ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ
ಪರೋಪಕಾರದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಮನಸ್ಸುಳ್ಳ ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯೇ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಳು. ಶಶಿಯಸೀ ಎಂಬ ತರಂತರಾಜನ ಪತ್ನಿಯು
ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯಾಗಿದ್ದರೂ ಇಂತಹ ಸುಗುಣವಿಶಿಷ್ಟಳಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಹೆಸರಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಪುರುಷರೆನಿಸಿದವರೂ ದೇವಯಜನ ದಾನ
ಧರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡದವರೂ ಆದ ಅನೇಕ ಪುರುಷರಿಗಿಂತ ಎಷ್ಟೋಪಾಲು ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟಳಾಗಿರುವಳು ಎಂದು ಋಷಿಯು
ವರ್ಣಿಸಿದ್ದಾನೆ. ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯರಿಗಿಂತ ಪುರುಷರು ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠರು ಎಂಬ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ನಿಯಮಕ್ಕೆ ವಿರುದ್ಧವಾಗಿ ತರಂತರಾಜನ
ಮಹಿಷಿಯು ಅನೇಕ ಪುರುಷರಿಗಿಂತ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಳು ಎಂಬ ವಿಶೇಷೋಕ್ತಿಯು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ವಿವೃತವಾಗಿದೆ.
ಉತ-ಅಪಿ ಚ । ಉತ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದವು ಸಮುಚ್ಚಯಾರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ (ಮತ್ತು ಎಂಬರ್ಥ)
ಅವಧಾರಣಾರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಉಪಯೋಗಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವುದು. ಪ್ರಕೃತ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನಾದರೂ ಹೇಳಬಹುದು.
ವಿ ಯಾ ಜಾನಾತಿ ಜಸುರಿಂ ವಿ ತೃಷ್ಯಂತಂ ವಿ ಕಾಮಿನಂ ।
ವಿ । ಯಾ । ಜ್ಞಾನಾತಿ । ಜಸುರಿಂ । ವಿ । ತೃಷ್ಣಂತಂ । ವಿ । ಕಾಮಿನಂ ।
ಯಾ ಶಶೀಯಸೀ ಜಸುರಿಂ ವ್ಯಥಿತಂ ॥ ಜಸಿಸ್ತಾಡನಕರ್ಮೋಪಕ್ಷೇಪಣಕರ್ಮಾ ನಾ ॥ ತಂ ವಿ
ಜಾನಾತಿ । ತಥಾ ತೃಷ್ಯಂತಂ ವಿ ಜಾನಾತಿ । ಕಾಮಿನಂ ಧನಾದ್ಯಭಿಲಾಷವಂತಂ ವಿ ಜಾನಾತಿ । ಅನುಕಂಪಯಾಭಿಮತಂ ದತ್ತವತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ದೇವತ್ರಾ ದೇವೇಷು ಮನಃ ಕೃಣತೇ ಕುರುತೇ ದೇವಪ್ರೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ
ಪ್ರದಾನಬುದ್ಧಿಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಯಾ ಸೈವ ಸ್ತ್ರೀತಿ ಪೂರ್ವತ್ರ ಸಂಬಂಧಃ ॥
ಯಾ—ಯಾವ ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯು । ಜಸುರಿಂ-ದುಃಖಿತನಾದವನ ಕಷ್ಟವನ್ನು । ವಿ ಜಾನಾತಿ—ಅರಿಯಲು
ಯಾವ ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯು ದುಃಖಿತನಾದವನ ಕಷ್ಟವನ್ನು ಅರಿಯಲು ಶಕ್ತಳೋ, ಯಾವಳು ಧನಾಪೇಕ್ಷಿಯಾದ
ಪುರುಷನ ಆವಶ್ಯಕತೆಯನ್ನರಿತು ಅವನ ಇತರ ಅಪೇಕ್ಷೆಗಳೂ ಪೂರೈಸುವಂತೆ ಸಹಾಯಮಾಡಬಲ್ಲಳೋ ಮತ್ತು
ಯಾವಳ ಮನಸ್ಸು ದೇವಪೂಜೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರತವಾಗಿದೆಯೋ ಅವಳೇ ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟಳು.
For she discerns one who suffers pain, one who is in want, or one desirous (of any thing), and directs her mind towards the gods.
ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ತರಂತಮಹಿಷಿಯಾದ ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯ ಗುಣವರ್ಣನೆ ಇದೆ. ಈ ರಾಜಪತ್ನಿಯು
ಉದಾರಮತಿಯಿಂದ ದಾನಮಾಡುವ ಸ್ವಭಾವವುಳ್ಳವಳು ಮಾತ್ರವೇ ಅಲ್ಲ. ಇತರರ ಕಷ್ಟಗಳನ್ನು ಎಂದರೆ ಕಷ್ಟ
ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಜನರ ದುಃಖವನ್ನು ಅರಿತು ಅವರ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಮರುಕವನ್ನು ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಪಡಿಸಿ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಮಾಡುವ
ಸ್ವಭಾವದವಳು : ಧನಹೀನರಾದವರಿಗೆ ಧನವನ್ನೂ, ಸಹಾಯಾಪೇಕ್ಷಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಇತರವಿಧ ಸಹಾಯವನ್ನೂ ನೀಡಿ
ಪರೋಪಕಾರಮಾಡುವವಳು ; ಧನಾದಿಗಳ ಅಭಾವದಿಂದ ಕಷ್ಟಪಡುತ್ತಿರುವ ಬಡಜನರಿಗೆ ಅವರಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನರಿತು
ಧನಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಸಹಾಯಮಾಡುವವಳು. ಈ ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲದೆ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂಜಿಸುವುದರಲ್ಲಿಯೂ
ಇವಳ ಮನಸ್ಸು ಪ್ರವರ್ತಿಸುವುದು. ಎಂದರೆ ದೇವಪೂಜಾದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ಯಜ್ಞಾದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ)ಯೂ ಇವಳಿಗೆ ಆಸಕ್ತಿ
ಯಿರುವುದು ಎಂದು ಶಶೀಯಸಿಯ ಗುಣವರ್ಣನೆಯನ್ನು ಋಷಿಯು ಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
ಜಸುರಿಂ—ಜಸುರಿ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಯಾಸ್ಕರು ನಿರ್ವಚನವನ್ನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾಉತ ಸ್ಮೈನಂ ವಸ್ತ್ರಮಥಿಂ ನ ತಾಯುಮನು ಕ್ರೋಶಂತಿ ಕ್ಷಿತಯೋ ಭರೇಷು ।
ನೀಚಾಯಮಾನಂ ಜಸುರಿಂ ಶ್ಯೇನಂ ಶ್ರವಶ್ಚಾಚ್ಛಾ ಪಶುಮಚ್ಚ ಯೂಥಂ ॥
ಎಂಬ ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನುದಾಹರಿಸಿ ಈ ಶಬ್ದದ ಅರ್ಥವಿವರಣೆಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಜಸುರಿಂ ಎಂದರೆ ಕ್ಷುದ್ಬಾಧೆಗೆ ಒಳಗಾದ,
ಹಸಿದ ಎಂದರ್ಥವಿರುವುದು. ಪ್ರಕೃತ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಆ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನೂ ಬಾಧೆಗೆ ಒಳಗಾದ, ಕಷ್ಟಪಡುತ್ತಿರುವ ಎಂಬ
ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಾರ್ಥವನ್ನೂ ಹೇಳಬಹುದು. ಎಂದರೆ ಆಹಾರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಕ್ಷುದ್ಬಾಧೆಯಿಂದ ಸಂಕಟಡುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅಥವಾ
ಇತರ ವಿಧವಾದ ಕಷ್ಟಕ್ಕೊಳಗಾಗಿ ದುಃಖಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವ ಎಂಬರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಹೇಳಬಹುದು.
ಉತ ಘಾ ನೇಮೋ ಅಸ್ತುತಃ ಪುಮಾ ಇತಿ ಬ್ರುವೇ ಪಣಿಃ ।
ಉತ । ಘ । ನೇಮಃ । ಅಸ್ತುತಃ । ಪುಮಾನ್ । ಇತಿ । ಬುವೇ । ಪಣಿಃ ।
ಉತ ಘಾಪಿ ಚ । ಫೇತಿ ಪೂರಣಃ । ನೇಮಃ । ತ್ವೋ ನೇಮ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಸ್ಯೆತಿ ನಿರುಕ್ತಂ ।
ಅರ್ಧಂ ಶರೀರಸ್ಯ ಭಾರ್ಯೇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಸ್ಮೃತೇಃ । ಶಶೀಯಸ್ಯಾ ಅರ್ಧಭೂತಸ್ತರಂತಃ ಪುಮಾನಸ್ತುತ ಇತಿ
ಬ್ರುವೇ । ಬಹುಧಾ ಸ್ತುತೋಽಪಿ ಗುಣಸ್ಯಾತಿಬಾಹುಲ್ಯಾದಸ್ತುತ ಏವೇತಿ ಬ್ರುವೇ ಪಣಿಃ ಸ್ತೋತಾಹಂ ।
ಸ ಚ ತರಂತೋ ವೈರದೇಯೇ । ವೀರಾ ಧನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರೇರಯಿತಾರೋ ದಾನಶೀಲಾಃ । ತೈರ್ದಾತವ್ಯಂ
ಧನಂ ದೇಯಂ । ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ಥನೇ ಸಮಃ । ಸರ್ವೇಭ್ಯೋ ದಾತೇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ಇದಿತಿ ಪೂರಣಃ ॥
ಅಸ್ತುತ ಇತಿ—(ಅನೇಕವಾಗಿ ಸ್ತುತನಾಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೂ ಸಹ) ಅಸ್ತುತನೆಂದೇ । ಪಣಿಃ—ಸ್ತೋತೃವಾದ ನಾನು ।
ಬ್ರುವೇ—ಹೇಳುತ್ತೇನೆ । ಸಃ—ಆ ತರಂತನು । ವೈರದೇಯೇ—ಪ್ರಭೂತವಾದ ಧನದ ದಾನದ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ।

ಸುವರ್ಣರೂಪವುಳ್ಳದ್ದೂ, ಉಕ್ಕಿನಸ್ತಂಭಗಳುಳ್ಳದ್ದೂ ಆದ ರಥವನ್ನು ಹತ್ತುತ್ತೀರಿ. ಅನಂತರ ಅಖಂಡಳಾದ
At the break of dawn, at the rising of the sun, ascend, Mitra and Varuna, your golden-bodied, iron-pillared car, and thence behold theearth and its inhabitants
ಉಷಸೋ ವ್ಯುಷ್ಟೌ ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಉದಿತಾ-ಉಷಸ್ಸಿನ ಆವಿರ್ಭಾವಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸೂರ್ಯನು
ಉದಯಿಸಿದಾಗ ಎಂಬ ಎರಡು ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಿಗೂ ಪ್ರಾತಃಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಂಬ ಒಂದೇ ಅರ್ಥವು ಸೂಚಿತವಾಗುವುದು.

ಯಜ್ಞಭೂಮಿಗೆ ಬರುವುದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸುವರ್ಣಮಯವಾದ ಮತ್ತು ಉಕ್ಕಿನ ಸ್ಥಂಭಗಳುಳ್ಳ ರಥವನ್ನೇರುತ್ತೀರಿ

ತೇನ ನೋ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣಾವವಿಷ್ಟಂ ಸಿಷಾಸಂತೋ ಜಿಗೀವಾಂಸಃ ಸ್ಯಾಮ॥
ಯತ್ । ಬಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ । ನ । ಅಽವಿಧೇ । ಸುದಾನೂ ಇತಿ ಸುದಾನೂ । ಅಚ್ಛಿದ್ರಂ । ಶರ್ಮ ।
ತೇನ । ನಃ । ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣೌ । ಅವಿಷ್ಟಂ । ಸಿಸಾಸಂತಃ । ಜಿಗೀವಾಂಸಃ । ಸ್ಯಾಮ ॥ ೯ ॥
ದಾಕ್ಷಾಯಣಯಜ್ಞೇ ಯದ್ವಂಹಿಷ್ಠಮಿತಿ ನವಮೀ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಸ್ಯಾಮಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾಯಾಂ ಮೈತ್ರಾವರುಣಸ್ಯ ಹವಿಷೋ ಯಾಜ್ಯಾ । ಸೂತ್ರಿತಂ ಚ । ಆ ನೋ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣಾ ಯದ್ವಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ ನಾತಿವಿಧೇ
ಸುದಾನೂ । ಆ. ೨.೧೪ । ಇತಿ ॥ ಮೈತ್ರಾವರುಣೇ ಪಶೌ ಹವಿಷ ಏಷ್ಯನ ಯಾಜ್ಯಾ । ಸೂತ್ರಿತಂ ಚ ।
ಯದ್ವಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ ನಾತಿವಿಧೇ ಸುದಾನೂ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ ಸಮವರ್ತತಾಗ್ರೇ । ಅ. ೩-೮ । ಇತಿ ॥
ಹೇ ಸುದಾನೂ ಶೋಭನದಾನೌ ಹೇ ಭುವನಸ್ಯ ಗೋಪಾ ಯುವಾಂ ಬಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ ಬಹುತವತಿ
ಯದಚ್ಛಿದ್ರಮನವಚ್ಚಿನ್ನಂ ಶರ್ಮ ಸುಖಂ ಗೃಹಂ ವಾ ನಾತಿವಿಧೇಽತಿವೇದ್ದುಮಶಕ್ಯಂ ಶರ್ಮೇಂ
ಶರ್ಮವಿಶೇಷಣಂ ॥ ವ್ಯಧ ತಾಡನ ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಮಾದತ್ಯುಪಪದೇ ಕೃತ್ಯಾರ್ಥೇ ಕೇನ್ ಸಂಪ್ರಸಾರಣಂ ಚ ॥
ತಾದೃಶಂ ಶರ್ಮ ಧಾರಯಥಃ ತೇನ ಶರ್ಮಣಾ ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾನವಿಷ್ಟಂ । ರಕ್ಷತಂ । ಹೇ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣೌ
ಸಿಷಾಸಂತೋ ಧನಾನಿ ಸಂಭಕ್ತುಮಿಚ್ಛಂತೋ ವಯಂ ಜಿಗೀವಾಂಸಃ ಶತ್ರೂಣಾಂ ಧನಾನಿ ಜೇತುಮಿಚ್ಛಂತಃ ಸ್ಯಾಮ । ಭವೇಮ ॥
ರಕ್ಷಕರಾದ ನೀವು । ಬಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ-ಅತಿ ಪ್ರಭೂತವಾದುದೂ । ಅಚ್ಚಿದ್ರಂ—ಭಂಗರಹಿತವಾದುದೂ । ನಾತಿವಿಧೇ—
ಇತರರಿಂದ ಛೇದಮಾಡಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲದುದೂ ಆದ। ಯತ್-ಯಾವ ಸುಖವನ್ನೂರಕ್ಷಣೆಯನ್ನೂ ಹೊಂದಿದ್ದೀರೋ।
ಸಿಷಾಸಂತಃ—ಧನವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಲು ಇಚ್ಛೆಯುಳ್ಳ ನಾವು । ಜಿಗೀವಾಂಸಃ—ಶತ್ರುಗಳನ್ನು ಜಯಿಸಿ ಅವರ
ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠರಾದ ದಾನಿಗಳಾದ ಎಲೈ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣರೇ, ವಿಶ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ರಕ್ಷಕರಾದ ನೀವು ಅತಿ ಪ್ರಭೂತವಾದುದೂ,
ಭಂಗರಹಿತವಾದುದೂ, ಇತರರಿಂದ ಛೇದಮಾಡಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲದುದೂ ಆದ ಯಾವ ಸುಖವನ್ನೂ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಯನ್ನೂ
ಹೊಂದಿದ್ದೀರೋ, ಅದರಿಂದ ನಮ್ಮನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಿ. ಎಲೈ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣರೇ, ಧನವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಲು ಇಚ್ಛೆಯುಳ್ಳ ನಾವು
ಶತ್ರುಗಳನ್ನು ಜಯಿಸಿ ಅವರ ಧನಗಳನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯುಳ್ಳವರಾಗಿ ಆಗುವಂತೆ ಅನುಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ.

Munificent Mitra and Varuna, protectors of the universe, (it is yours to grant) exceeding and perfect felicity, such as it is impossible to disturb: bless us with that (felicity), and may we ever be (possessed) of the riches we desire, and be confident of victory (over our enemies.)

ಯೋಗಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂತ್ರದ-ಆ ನೋ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣಾ ಯದ್ವಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ ನಾತಿವಿಧೇ ಸುದಾನೂ ಎಂಬ ಸೂತ್ರದಿಂದ (ಆ. ೨-೧೪) ವಿವೃತವಾಗಿರುವುದು. ಮತ್ತು ಮೈತ್ರಾವರುಣ ಸಂಬಂಧವಾದ ಪಶುಯಾಗ

ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನ ಶೌತಸೂತ್ರದ-ಯದ್ವಂಹಿಷ್ಠಂ ನಾತಿವಿಧೇ ಸುದಾನೂ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ ಸಮವರ್ತತಾಗ್ರೇ

en: O Agni, mortals who have the materials for the oblation glorify you, the shining god. I too praise you, Jātavedas. He is Jātavedas because he knows all that is born, the moving and the unmoving beings; or because all that is born, the immovable and the movable, knows him; or else, "veda" being a name for wealth, because all that is born is his wealth. Such as you are, I praise you; the root "mani" is used here in the sense of praising, since roots have many meanings. You, thus, convey the oblations, the means of sacrifice, continuously (to the gods).

notes: ಗಾ printed in the Pratipadārtha, evidently for ಸಃ; gloss "ಅತಹ ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞನಾದ ನೀನು"

en: O Agni, the sacrificers, men who possess oblations, praise you, the shining one. I also praise you, who are Jātavedas in form. Such an omniscient you carry the oblations to the gods continuously.
Mortals bearing oblations glorify you, Agni, the divine: I praise you, Jatavedas, for that you convey successively oblations (to the gods)

हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—होमसाधनद्रव्यसमेताः । (*homasādhanadravyasametāḥ |*) The meaning is: sacrificers who have made ready the materials for the oblation, such as the oblation (cooked rice), ghee and kindling sticks, in order to offer them in the fire for the sake of the gods.

जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—जातमुत्पन्नं चराचरं भूतजातं वेत्तीति जातवेदाः । अथवा जातानि स्थावरजंगमात्मकानि एनं विदुरिति जातवेदाः । यद्वा वेद इति धननाम । जातं सर्वं वेदो धनं यस्यासौ जातवेदाः । (*jātamutpannaṃ carācaraṃ bhūtajātaṃ vettīti jātavedāḥ | athavā jātāni sthāvarajaṃgamātmakāni enaṃ viduriti jātavedāḥ | yadvā veda iti dhananāma | jātaṃ sarvaṃ vedo dhanaṃ yasyāsau jātavedāḥ |*) For the word Jātavedasam Sāyaṇa has given three kinds of meaning. Since this Agni knows all the moving and unmoving things that are born in the world, he is called Jātavedas; or, since the whole class of beings, moving and unmoving, born in the world knows this Agni, Agni is called Jātavedas; or, the word Veda having the meaning of wealth (Ni. 3-9), since he possesses wealth to give to the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, Agni is called Jātavedas: thus he has given the explanation in three ways. Besides this, मम नाम प्रथमं जातवेदः पिता माता च दधतुर्यदग्रे । (*mama nāma prathamaṃ jātavedaḥ pitā mātā ca dadhaturyadagre |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-10-1): that is, Agni himself declares, "My father and mother first gave me the name Jātavedas."
मन्ये (*manye*)-स्तौमि । (*staumi |*) I praise. Here the commentator has explained that the root mani is used in the sense of praising.

The Agni to whom all the sacrifices come together, and to whom the oblations, which win abundant fame for the sacrificer, resort: such an Agni is the Hotā, the invoker of the gods, for the sake of the sacrifice of that man, the donor of the oblation by casting it and the like, by whom the sacred grass has been cut, and who is the abode in which the means and fruits of heaven dwell.
- सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)—come together and serve
- दास्वतः (*dāsvataḥ*)—to the one who offers the oblation
- वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)—and offers a seat of cut darbha grass
- होता (*hotā*)—becomes the Hotā (who calls the gods in the sacrifice)

The Agni whom all the sacrifices serve together, and to whom the oblations, intended to win fame for the sacrificer, resort: such an Agni becomes the Hotā, who calls the gods for the sake of the sacrifice, for the man who offers the oblation and offers a seat of cut darbha grass.

Agni is the invoker of the gods (on behalf of) him, the donor (of the oblation), the abode (of the fruit of good works) by whom the sacred grass has been strewn; (he) in whom congregate all sacrifices securing food and fame.

Moreover, Agni, whom the two araṇīs (kindling sticks) generated like a new child, is the upholder of the human race, of the descendants of Manu: the viś are those who enter the womb, that is, the people. He nourishes the bodily elements of those people by way of the cooking of food and the like, and he is the one of good sacrifice. The meaning is that the two araṇīs created this Agni for the nourishment of the people.
- मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*)—born in the line of Manu
- अरणी (*araṇī*)—the two pieces of wood also
- शिशुं यथा (*śiśuṃ yathā*)—as one gives birth to a child
The two pieces of wood also brought forth that very Agni, the nourisher of all the people born in the line of Manu and possessor of an excellent sacrifice, as one gives birth to a new child.
He (it is) whom the two stieks have engendered like a new-born babe ; the supporter of men the descendants of Manu, the fit object of sacrifice.

And you, O Agni, are laid hold of with difficulty, like the young of the crooked-moving ones (hvāryāṇām): of serpents; or else, of horses whose gait is crooked by special paces such as the leap, that is, like a young snake or an untrained young horse. You who burn many forests (vanā) are a consumer, as an animal (is a consumer) of fodder (yavase). The meaning is: as an animal that is extremely hungry, when let loose in a meadow, eats everything, so you do.
- पुत्रो न (*putro na*)—as their young are caught with great effort
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who are that very one
- पशुर्न (*paśurna*)—as an animal eats up the grass entirely

O Agni, as difficult as it is to catch the young of serpents of crooked movements, so difficult it is to reach you. As an animal, hungry and eager for grass, eats the whole meadow entirely as soon as it is let loose, you too burn up many forests entirely.
You are laid hold of with difficulty like the young of tortuously-twining (snakes) ; you who are the consumer of many forests, as an animal is of fodder.

And of that smoky Agni, whose flames (arcayaḥ) go well, that is, spread on every side; Trita, that is, pervading in the three places, or one who goes to the three places; when in heaven, that is, in the atmosphere, he fans himself up (upa dhamati), that is, increases himself, then the flames go out in all directions. How? Like a blower: as a smith increases fire with bellows and the like, so he increases himself. And further, "as in the blower": as the fire that is near a blower, being blown by him, sharpens itself, that is, makes itself keen, so he makes himself keen of his own accord. The word "aha" is a mere filler of the verse-quarter.
- ध्मातेव (*dhmāteva*)—as a smith blows up fire and makes it grow
- ध्मातरी यथा (*dhmātarī yathā*)—as the fire in the smith's furnace
- शिशीते (*śiśīte*)—when the smith blows with the bellows, increases its own form

As a smith blows up fire and makes it grow, and as the fire in a smith's furnace, when the smith blows with the bellows, increases its own form, so when Agni surpasses the three places and makes his own form grow in the atmosphere, then the flames of that smoky Agni spread everywhere beautifully.

Of whom smoke-emitting, the flames intensely collect ; then, when diffused in the three regions Agni inflates himself in the firmament, like the blower of a bellowes, and sharpens (his flames), as (the fire blazes from the blast) of the blower.

O Agni, friend of all, by your protections, the acts of protecting done by you, and by the praises of you made by us, may we pass over the evil deeds, the sin-producing acts, done by mortals who are our enemies, as one passes over enemies who are full of hatred (dveṣoyutaḥ). The meaning is: by your protections and by praises connected with you may I overcome the outer and the inner enemies.
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—who are the friend of all
- प्रशस्तिभिश्च (*praśastibhiśca*)—and with the help of hymns addressed to you
- द्वेषोयुतो न (*dveṣoyuto na*)—as one conquers enemies full of hatred

O Agni, by your protections, you who are the friend of all, and with the help of hymns addressed to you, may I cross over the sins natural to men. May I be freed from those sins as one conquers enemies full of hatred.
By the protections of you, Agni, the friend (of all), and by our praises (of you), may we pass safe from the evil acts of men, as if from malignant (enemies).

O Agni, mighty one (sahasvaḥ), leader (naraḥ) of the oblations, bring to us (abhi ā bhara), that is, bring towards us, that wealth (rayim) well known in the world, having the form of cattle and the like. May that Agni mentioned before cast down (kṣepayat) our enemies; may that Agni nourish us; may he be (bhuvat) for the gain of food (vāja). And, O Agni, in battles (pṛtsu, from pṛtanā) be (edhi) for our prosperity: so you, for victory over the enemy in war, make us prosper.
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—you, the leader of the oblations
- क्षेपयत् (*kṣepayat*)—may he cast down our enemies

O powerful Agni, you, the leader of the oblations, bring towards us that well-known wealth. May that well-known Agni cast down our enemies. May that same Agni nourish us. May he bring us the gain of food. O Agni, be a helper to us in battles, for our victory and for the growth of our wealth.

Powerful Agni, bestow upon us the institutors (of pious rites), that wealth (which we desire) : may he discomfit (our foes) : may he cherish us : may he be ever ready to bestow upon us food : and Agni, be present in battles for our success.

O Agni, bring to us the most powerful (ojiṣṭham) dyumna, that is, wealth; it is called dyumna because it shines everywhere in the form of bracelets, crowns and the like. "Adhrigu" is a form of address: O you whose going is unobstructed, unrestrained; or else, one whose cows, that is, rays, are unrestrained. Join us (naḥ) with wealth (rāyā) that extends on every side (parīṇasā). For the gain of food (vājāya) make (ratsi, cut out) a path (panthām), a road that is the means of reaching food near us: such is the meaning.
- अध्रिगो (*adhrigo*)—having an unobstructed power of going
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for the gain of food for us

O Agni, whose power of going is unobstructed, bring us the most powerful and shining wealth. Make us full, possessed of wealth that extends everywhere. Construct for us the right path for the gain of food.
Agni, of irresistible prowess, bring to us most powerful treasure; (invest us) with surrounding wealth ; mark out the paths to abundance.

O Agni, marvellous (adbhuta), a wonder to all through the excess of your power: you, pleased by our work (kratvā), our sacrificial activity and the like, grant (kuru is to be supplied) the gift called mamhana of strength or of wealth (dakṣasya). Since the strength that slays the asuras has risen (ārohat) in you, therefore, being worthy of sacrifice (yajñiyaḥ) like Mitra, that is, like the Sun, be a doer (kraṇā) of deeds that consist in driving away the rākṣasas who destroy the sacrifice.⟨NOTE:4⟩
notes: ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ: ಮಂಹನಾ—ಆಧಿಕ್ಯವನ್ನು (ನಮ್ಮಲ್ಲಿ) ಉಂಟುಮಾಡು; ಮಿತ್ರೋ ನ—ಮಿತ್ರದೇವನಂತೆ; ಅಸುರಂ; Sāyaṇa: ದಾನಂ ಕುರು, ಸೂರ್ಯ ಇವ, ಅಸುರ್ಯಂ

en: - मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like the god Mitra
- यज्ञियः (*yajñiyaḥ*)—you who are worthy of worship
- क्राणा (*krāṇā*)—are a doer of wonderful deeds

O Agni, possessed of supernatural power, you, pleased by our sacrifices and other works, produce for us strength that is most abundant and great. In you the strength that destroys enemies has spread. You, worthy of worship like the god Mitra, are a doer of wonderful deeds.

Marvellous Agní, (gratified) by our acts, (produce) in us greatness of vigour : in you abides the strength destroying evil spirits : you who are to be worshipped, like Mitra, are the doer (of great deeds).

O Agni, make us, these your worshippers, reach increase of gaya, that is, a house (that to which one goes, for dwelling), or wealth (that which is praised), and of prosperity in cattle and the like. As the famous sūris, the men who are praisers and have obtained renown, have by their stomas, their hymns, obtained praiseworthy riches such as cattle, so may we also: such is the meaning.
- ये (*ye*)—who were famed in the past, and
- पुष्टिं च (*puṣṭiṃ ca*)—and the prosperity of wealth such as cattle

O Agni, the men, priests and others, who were famed in the past and composed excellent praise addressed to you, obtained praiseworthy riches as the fruit of their hymns. Even so, you, praised by us, make grow the wealth such as house, and the prosperity of wealth such as cattle, of us who praise you.
Augment, Agni, our dwelling and prosperity, for the devout men (who have propitiated you) by their praises have acquired riches.

O Agni, delighting (candra) all beings: the men whose words, hymns that are connected with you, adorn you, make beautiful, they become possessors of horse-wealth (aśvarādhasaḥ); by this prosperity is indicated. And further, being mighty, they become destroyers of enemies by their own strengths (śuṣmebhiḥ). For those who make praise connected with you, a great and fair renown arises, greater even than that of heaven: it is a renown that abides in all directions. Such as you are, ⟨NOTE:5⟩ he himself of his own accord awakens (bodhati, causes to know).
notes: ಏವಂವಿಧು ತ್ವಾಂ ಗಯಸ್ತ್ಮನಾತ್ಮನಾ ಸ್ವಯಮೇವ ಬೋಧತಿ ಬೋಧಯತಿ: damaged text; subject of ಬೋಧತಿ unclear (ಗಯ?)

en: - ये नरः (*ye naraḥ*)—which men, priests and others
- ते गिरः (*te giraḥ*)—reciting speech in the form of praise of you
- अश्वराधसः (*aśvarādhasaḥ*)—are possessed of wealth in the form of horses
- शुष्मेभिः (*śuṣmebhiḥ*)—become destroyers of enemies by their strengths

O delightful Agni, the men, priests and others, who recite speech in the form of praise of you and extol your greatness become possessed of wealth in the form of horses; and, being powerful, they become destroyers of enemies by their strengths. The very great and excellent fame of those who praise you, spreading all over the atmosphere, awakens you of its own impulse.

Delightful Agni, those men who glorify you with hymns become rich in horses, and are invigorated with (foe-destroying) energies ; and their great renown, spread through the firmament, arouses (you) of your own accord.

O Agni, those famous rays (arcis) of yours, extremely bold and shining, go forth, that is, move in all directions. How? Like lightnings that pervade all around: by this the excess of their brilliance is stated. They are noisy like a chariot: by this the greater sound of the flames is stated. And as one who longs for food sets out in battles for victory over enemies for the sake of food, so do they; by this the longing for the oblation is stated.
The remainder of the block consists only of grammatical derivations of the words yaṃti, dhṛṣṇuyā, parijmānaḥ and vājayuḥ.
- विद्युतः न (*vidyutaḥ na*)—like the radiance of lightning (the flash)
notes: ಶಾಂತಿಯುತವೂ printed in the Pratipadārtha; the Bhāvārtha has ಕಾಂತಿಯುತವೂ "radiant"; translated as radiant

en: O Agni, your famous rays, possessing power that checks enemies and radiant, spread in all directions like the all-pervading radiance of lightning, and like a chariot that makes a noise and rushes forward into battle for food.
These your bright and fierce flames, Agni, spread around like the circumambient lightnings, and are like a rattling chariot rushing (into battle) for booty.

O Agni, be quick for our protection; and be for the giving of wealth to us who are accompanied by the affliction caused by poverty. Further, may our sons, friends and others, the praisers, be capable of crossing, that is, of attaining, all the quarters (āśāḥ). Or else āśāḥ means desires; the meaning then is: accomplish for us all the excellent things we desire.
- सबाधसः च (*sabādhasaḥ ca*)—and (be) the giver of wealth that brings about the destruction of harmful poverty
- तरीषणि (*tarīṣaṇi*)—let them be capable of attaining (or: capable of pervading all the quarters)
O Agni, be always for our protection. Be the giver of wealth that destroys harmful poverty. May our sons, friends and others, your praisers, be capable of attaining all their desired objects.
Be prompt, Agni, for our protection, and for the gift of poverty-repelling (riches) ; and may our pious (descendants be able to) compass all their desires-

O Agni, Aṅgiras: by the figure of non-distinction between cause and effect, Agni, though the source of the Aṅgirases, is called Aṅgiras. O Aṅgiras, praised by the ancient great seers and praised also by those of the present day, bring to us wealth that overcomes even the mighty; wealth is called "overcoming" because it is the cause of overcoming. O Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, give to us, your praisers, the power to praise. And in battles be for our prosperity, that is, be present for it.
- स्तवानः (*stavānaḥ*)—and being praised by those of the present day
- विभ्वासहं (*vibhvāsahaṃ*)—giving the power to face an adversary of great strength
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O Agni, in the form of the Hotṛ
- स्तवसे (*stavase*)—give the capacity to praise you

O Agni, in the form of Aṅgiras, you who were praised by the earlier seers and are praised by those of the present day, give us wealth that gives the power to face an adversary of great strength. O Agni, in the form of the Hotṛ, give to us who praise you the capacity to praise you, and be the cause of our prosperity in battles.

Agni, you are Angiras ; glorified in the past, glorified (at present), invoker (of the gods), bring unto us riches (enabling us) to overcome the mighty : give to your praisers (ability) to praise you, and be (at hand) for our suceess in battles.

Agni is the protector of the people, ever wakeful, of good strength, that is, of strength praised by all. He was born for the newer welfare of the worlds. With limbs blazing with ghee ⟨NOTE:8⟩, endowed with great, sky-touching, that is, cloud-licking, splendour, pure: such is Agni; he shines brilliantly, in a radiant manner, for the Bharatas, the priests and sacrificers ⟨NOTE:9⟩. The rest of the block, as far as it stands in this window, gives the grammar of the words gopāḥ and jāgṛviḥ.
The remainder of the block consists only of grammatical derivations of the words jāgṛviḥ, sudakṣaḥ, suvitāya, navyase, divispṛśā and dyumat.
notes: ಧೃತಪ್ರತೀಕೋ ಧೃತೇನ printed with dh; the Saṃhitā has ಘೃತಪ್ರತೀಕಃ
ಋತ್ವಿಗ್ಯಸ್ತಧರ್ಥಂ damaged in the machine-read text; read as "for the priests"

en: - सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—for the welfare of the world
- धृतप्रतीकः (*dhṛtapratīkaḥ*)—having a body blazing with ghee ⟨NOTE:10⟩
- दिविस्पृशा (*divispṛśā*)—touching the sky; endowed with such splendour
- भरतेभ्यः (*bharatebhyaḥ*)—for the Kṣatriyas of the Bharata family
notes: ಧೃತದಿಂದ printed with dh; read as ghee, as the Saṃhitā has ಘೃತಪ್ರತೀಕಃ

en: Agni, who has excellent strength, is the protector of all men and is ever wakeful, has been born for the new welfare of the world. Having a body blazing with ghee, endowed with great splendour that touches the atmosphere, and pure, Agni shines in the atmosphere for the Kṣatriyas of the Bharata family.

The vigilant, the powerful Agni, the protector of man, has been engendered for the present prosperity (of the world): fed with butter, (blazing) with intense (radiance) reaching to the sky, the pure Agni shines brilliantly for the Bharatas

The men, that is, the priests, first kindled Agni, who is the banner, the making-known, of the sacrifice, and the purohita, set in front by the sacrificer. He shares a chariot with Indra and the gods, since they honour him. They kindled him in the threefold place, the area of the sacrificial enclosure, that is, in the three places of the fires. That Agni, performer of excellent rites, the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, has sat down on the sacred grass, at that place furnished with grass, for the sacrifice; that is, he has become established there.
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the one who makes it known
- पुरोहितं (*purohitaṃ*)—the one who occupies the place of honour
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—who sits in the same chariot
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seats of darbha grass
- यजथाय (*yajathāya*)—for the conduct of the sacrifice

The priests and others first made to blaze, in the three places, the Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya and Dakṣiṇāgni, Agni, who makes the sacrifice known, who occupies the place of honour, and who sits in the same chariot with Indra and the other gods. Agni, the performer of excellent rites and the invoker of the gods, has sat down on the seats of darbha grass for the conduct of the sacrifice.

The priests have first kindled, in three places, Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the family priest, (riding) in the same car with Indra and the gods : he, the performer of pious acts, the invoker (of the gods) has sat down on the sacred grass for the (celebration of the) rite.

O Agni, from the two mothers, the two fire-sticks (the two aranis are called "mothers" because they are the cause of his birth), you are born unobstructed, that is, you appear. Mandra means praised by all.

Kavi means pervading everywhere; or else wise. You, pure, have risen up from the sacrificer who dwells specially in the house for the Agnihotra and other rites. The ancient great seers made you grow with ghee. O Ahuta, offered with oblations, your smoke, spread in the atmosphere, became your banner, your sign, since smoke is what makes fire inferable. The rest of the block gives the grammar of mātroḥ, mandraḥ, kaviḥ, udatiṣṭhaḥ and vivasvataḥ.
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—with the help of the performer of the sacrifice
- अवर्धयन् (*avardhayan*)—(the priests and others) have made you grow
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—like a banner that makes known
notes: ಉದ್ಯೂತನಾಗಿದ್ದೀಯೆ printed; read as "have risen up"
ಧೃತದಿಂದ printed with dh; read as ghee

en: O Agni, you are born unobstructed from your mothers, the fire-sticks. You, worthy of praise, wise and pure, have risen up with the help of the performer of the sacrifice. The priests and others have made you grow with ghee. O Agni, honoured with oblations, the smoke spread in the atmosphere has become for you like a banner that makes you known.

You are born unobstructed of two mothers: pure, adorable, wise, you have sprung up from (the devotion of) the householder : they have augmented you with butter : Agni, to whom burnt-offerings are made, the smoke is your banner spread abroad in the sky-

मात्रोः (*mātroḥ*)—अरण्योः । (*araṇyoḥ |*) स्वजनननिमित्तत्वात् अरणी मातरावित्युच्येते । (*svajanananimittatvāt araṇī mātarāvityucyete |*) In the sacrifice two pieces of wood are used to bring forth Agni. A broad piece of wood is laid below on the ground and a small hollow is made in it; in that hollow they put well-dried things that catch fire easily, such as cotton, coconut fibre and dry leaves. Another piece of wood, long like a stick, is placed over the hollow, and they churn it as one churns curds. After churning in this way for a little while, a spark of fire arises from the friction, touches the dry material nearby, such as cotton, and catches. Then, making it burn well with firewood and the like, they carry it in due form to the place in the sacrificial hall called the Uttaravedi and establish it there. This rite is called Agni-mathana (the churning of fire). Among the proceedings that must be carried out at the beginning of a sacrifice this act of churning is an important one. The carrying of the fire from the place of churning to the Uttaravedi is called Agni-praṇayana. This rite also must be performed with mantras and according to rule. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes the rites of agni-mathana and agni-praṇayana at length. They can be learnt from what we have written at length on pages 384 and 541 of Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 12.

May Agni, the accomplisher of all human aims, come to our sacrifice, that is, approach. Men, human beings, carry Agni about in every house; that is, they perform the carrying about. Agni, bearer of the oblations to the gods, has become the messenger of the gods. Those who adore him, choosing him, choose Agni as the one whose sacrifice is accomplished (kavikratu); that is, they worship him. The remainder of the block gives the grammar of sādhuyā.
- उप वेतु (*upa vetu*)—may he graciously come
- वि भरंते (*vi bharaṃte*)—honour in a special manner
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—as the messenger of the gods
- कविक्रतुं (*kavikratuṃ*)—as the one who accomplishes the sacrifice

May Agni, the accomplisher of desired aims, graciously come to our sacrifice. The sacrificers honour Agni in a special manner in every sacrificial house. Agni, the bearer of the oblation, has become the messenger of the gods. All who honour Agni worship him as the accomplisher of the sacrifice.

May Agni, the fulfiller (of all desires), come to our sacrifice : men cherish Agni in every dwelling : Agni, the bearer of oblations, has become the messenger (of the gods) : those adoring Agni adore him as the accomplisher of the sacrifice.

O Agni, this most sweet speech is made for you, for your sake. May this praise (manīṣā), which brings happiness to the heart, be for you. Words in the form of praise fill you, that is, make you full, and make you grow with strength, just as the great streams, the rivers carrying water, fill the sea.
- वर्धयंति च (*vardhayaṃti ca*)—and also make you grow

O Agni, this praise, endowed with the utmost sweetness, is composed with you as its object. May this praise bring joy to your heart. As great rivers fill the ocean with water, these praises fill you with delight and make you grow with strength.
To you, Agni, this most sweet speech (is addressed); may this praise be gratification to your heart : pious hymns fill you, and augment you with vigour, as large rivers (replenish) the sea.

O Agni, the Aṅgirasa seers found you, hidden in the cave, taking refuge in every single tree. You, endowed with great strength, are born when you are churned. O Aṅgiras, you who are the source of the Aṅgirases, they call the son of strength.
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—O Agni, who are Aṅgiras yourself
- सहसः पुत्रं (*sahasaḥ putraṃ*)—as the son of strength

O Agni, you who were hidden within the cave and had taken refuge in every tree, the Aṅgirasa seers found as the fruit of their effort. You, endowed with very great strength, are born by the act of churning. O Agni, who are Aṅgiras yourself, they call you the son of strength.

The Angirasas discovered you, Agni, hidden in secret, and taking refuge from wood to wood : you are generated, being churned with great force; therefore they have called you, Angiras, the son of strength.

त्वां सहसः पुत्रं आहुः (*tvāṃ sahasaḥ putraṃ āhuḥ*)—When fire is produced by churning in the fire-sticks, great force has to be used for the churning. Since Agni is produced in this way by the application of force, it is a usage particularly common in the Ṛgveda to call Agni सहसः पुत्रं (*sahasaḥ putraṃ*), the son of strength, that is, one produced by the application of force. On the matter of agni-mathana see what is written in the Special Topics of the 3rd Ṛk of this sūkta (page 37).

To great Agni, great through excess of ability, worthy of sacrifice, the showerer of ṛta (ṛta is water, as it is read among the names of water), the strong (asura means mighty), the showerer of desires, I bring forward an utterance in the form of praise, a means of knowledge, directed to him. How? As ghee, well purified, poured into the mouth at the sacrifice is pleasing to him, so I bring a praise that is pleasing.
- यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—at the time of the sacrifice
- आस्येन (*āsyena*)—as one offers it into the mouth of Agni
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—to him who has the nature of greatness
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—the causer of rain (the one who pours down rain)
- प्रतीचीं (*pratīcīṃ*)—that which comes to meet him
notes: ಧೃತಂ printed with dh; the Saṃhitā has ಘೃತಂ; read as ghee

en: As, at the time of the sacrifice, a stream of well-purified ghee is offered into the mouth of Agni, so I offer, to Agni, who has the nature of greatness, is worthy of sacrifice, causes rain, is endowed with strength and showers desires, a praise that brings about reflection and comes to meet him.
I offer to the great, the adorable Agni. the rainer of water, the vigorous, the showerer (of benefits), the present acceptable praise, like well-purified butter (poured) at sacrifices into his mouth.

बृहते—सामर्थ्यातिशयेन महते । (*bṛhate—sāmarthyātiśayena mahate |*) The abilities of Agni are many: the power to give the desired objects to those who worship him, the power to destroy enemies, the power to carry the oblations and other materials that the sacrificers offer in him to the gods for whom they are intended, and many other kinds of power and ability. Because Agni has these, he is possessed of excess of ability, and so the great nature of Agni is set out here.
असुराय (*asurāya*)—The word asura has many meanings. Here असुराय—बलवते । (*asurāya—balavate |*) the word is used in the sense of strength.
प्रतीचीं (*pratīcīṃ*)—This word is an adjective of the word गिरं (*giraṃ*). The main purport is: I stand facing Agni and recite the words of praise.

सुपूतं धृतं आस्स्येन (*supūtaṃ dhṛtaṃ āssyena*)—Here an illustration is given for reciting the hymn while standing facing Agni. It is a matter of experience that when ghee (ghṛta) is offered in Agni it burns blazing and shining; that is, the idea is suggested that Agni is pleased by a stream of ghee. Therefore, in the way in which Agni is pleased when ghee is offered in the mouth of Agni, that is, in the Agni blazing with flames, in that way the seer describes: may Agni be pleased with the words of praise that I, the seer, recite standing facing Agni.

ṛta here means praise. O Agni, who know (cikitvaḥ), know this praise made by me. Further, to nourish the world, to bring about the abundant streams of ṛta, that is, of water, pierce (tṛndhi) the clouds. I, endowed with strength, do not touch (sapāmi), that is, I do not practise, the violence that destroys sacrificial rites; and with the two, truth and untruth, I do not do any act that is not Vedic. But I address only praise to you, the radiant one, the showerer of desires.
- अनु त्वंधि (*anu tvaṃdhi*)—cause (from the cloud) to pour down
- यातुं (*yātuṃ*)—the act that obstructs the rite
- न सपामि (*na sapāmi*)—I do not practise
- द्वयेन (*dvayena*)—either by truth or by untruth
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of you who have a radiant colour
O Agni, you who know the excellence of my praise, praise this hymn composed by me. Cause streams of water to pour abundantly from the cloud. I, from pride in my strength,
do not practise obstruction of the rite. Either by truth or by untruth, I do not trouble the rite. But I compose and recite praise of you, who have a radiant colour and shower desires.

Agni, who know (the purpose of) the sacrifice, assent to this rite: be favourable to the copious showers of water : (endowed) with strength, (I undertake) not (to obstruct) sacred acts, nor adjure the rite with both (truth and untruth), but (repeat the praise) of the resplendent showerer (of benefits).

The meaning of this Ṛk is not so clear. To make the meaning clear, many words have been supplied, and an effort has been made so that a definite sense becomes evident. Only some of them are explained here.

ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—In this Ṛk this word is read three times. For this word ṛta Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "this hymn made by me (the seer)". For the word ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*) he gives the meaning उदकस्य (*udakasya*), "of the waters". For the use of the word dhārāḥ, "streams of water", in ऋतस्य धाराः (*ṛtasya dhārāḥ*) indicates that the word ṛtasya means water (or ghee?).
यातुं—कर्मणां नाशकरीं हिंसां । (*yātuṃ—karmaṇāṃ nāśakarīṃ hiṃsāṃ |*) He has fitted the meaning: the violence that causes obstruction to the sacrificial rite.
द्वयेन (*dvayena*)—Here also an explanation is given that the two are two kinds of rite, truth and untruth.

O Agni, who make water, the means of life of all beings, by what rite performed with truth do you become the knower of our praise? The praiseworthy one, the guardian of the seasons (the second word for "season" is only a repetition), the shining Agni, may he know me. Of me, the one who serves him, whose wealth consists of cattle and the like, I do not know that Agni, the lord. He explains नवेदाः (*navedāḥ*) as having the sense "he knows" (not "he does not know"), which is obtained by an irregular formation; he adopts the view of Skandasvāmin, while Pāṇini by the sūtra नभ्राण्णपादिति (*nabhrāṇṇapāditi*) gives the word a sense that does not fit here, so that the sense is not suitable. ⟨NOTE:14⟩
notes: ವೇತ್ತೀತ್ಯೇತಸ್ಮಿನ್ನರ್ಥೇ printed for Pāṇini's sense; ನ ವೇತ್ತಿ expected from the context; left as printed

en: - कया ऋतेन (*kayā ṛtena*)—by what rite, of the nature of truth

O Agni, you who provide water to all beings and do good to the world, which of our rites can make you know our praise? May Agni, the praiseworthy one, the guardian of the seasons, the shining one, know me as his devotee. Only Agni, the lord of my wealth, I have not yet seen face to face.

Agni, bestower of water, by what (act of) truth may you, who are adorable, be cognizant of our adoration ? may the divine Agni, the guardian of the seasons recognize me : I (know) him not (yet) as the lord of the riches of which I am the possessor.

In this Ṛk also the word ṛtu is used four times. For the first, ऋतुयन् (*ṛtuyan*), the meaning given is water; for the second, ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), a rite of the nature of truth; for the third and the fourth, the words ऋतूनां ऋतुपाः (*ṛtūnāṃ ṛtupāḥ*), the meaning given is the seasons (words denoting time). Here there is a repetition, ऋतुपा ऋतूनां (*ṛtupā ṛtūnāṃ*). Such repeated expressions are specially found in the Ṛgveda: रयिपतिं रयाणां (*rayipatiṃ rayāṇāṃ*); विशां विश्वतिं (*viśāṃ viśvatiṃ*); रयाणां त्वा रयिपतिं (*rayāṇāṃ tvā rayipatiṃ*); वसूनां वसुपतिं (*vasūnāṃ vasupatiṃ*), and so on.

सनितुः अस्य रायः पतिं अहं न—भजमानस्य मम पश्वादिलक्षणस्य धनस्य स्वामिनं तमग्निं नाहं जानामि । (*sanituḥ asya rāyaḥ patiṃ ahaṃ na—bhajamānasya mama paśvādilakṣaṇasya dhanasya svāminaṃ tamagniṃ nāhaṃ jānāmi |*) Agni is the lord of wealth. This wealth is of many kinds, such as cattle, food and houses. The seer says that he (being of little understanding) does not know well the qualities and surpassing powers of Agni, the lord of such wealth, and thus expresses the greatness of Agni and his own smallness.

O Agni, who are those of your people that would be the binders of one's enemy? By reason of their surpassing power no one can know of what kind such men are: this is the meaning. Who among yours are the radiant protectors of people, who give wealth to the poor? Who of yours protect the man who bears untruth? Who are there as guardians of evil speech, such as a curse? None at all: this is the meaning. Or else: whoever are the binders of the enemy; whoever are the protectors who give wealth and are radiant; whoever protect the man who bears untruth by turning him away from the sin born of untruth and giving him the right path; whoever are guardians of evil speech of the nature of curses and the like: all of these are yours, that is, your worshippers.
- ते (*te*)—among the men who belong to you

O Agni, among the company of men who belong to you, who are the good and who are the bad? How many are there who bind enemies and give wealth to the afflicted, who are radiant and protectors of the poor? How many are there who protect the man of untruthful nature and his evil deeds? Who are they?

Who, Agni, among your (followers) are the imprisoners of foes ? who among them are the protectors (of men), the splendid distributors of gifts ? who among them defend the asserter of untruth ? who are the encouragers of evil deeds ?

O Agni, those who conquer and bind the enemy, the protectors of the poor, those who give wealth to the afflicted, those who protect, without seeing, those who have spoken untruth, ⟨NOTE:15⟩ and those who have gained good sense so as not to speak evil words: all such good men are yours, that is, they are those who worship you. This is the main purport.
notes: ಕಾಣದೆ ಅನೃತವನ್ನಾಡಿದವರನ್ನು: sense of ಕಾಣದೆ unclear

en: O Agni, these friends of yours, your praisers, dispersed and spread everywhere, who were formerly inauspicious, reviling others and the like and abandoning your service, and so unfortunate, have now become auspicious and fortunate, rendering you service. Moreover, those who, to me who conduct myself straight and rightly, speak crooked things with words, that is, with evil speech: these my rivals may themselves be harmed. The word अहिंस्यंत (*ahiṃsyaṃta*) is given as the sense of the verb form.
- एते ते सखायः (*ete te sakhāyaḥ*)—these men, friends of yours
- अशिवाः संतः (*aśivāḥ saṃtaḥ*)—(formerly, not worshipping you) being doers of inauspicious acts; (now)
- शिवासः (*śivāsaḥ*)—in the auspicious work of your worship
- ऋजूयते (*ṛjūyate*)—to me, the doer of good acts
- अधूर्षत (*adhūrṣata*)—let them bring harm upon themselves
O Agni, these men, friends of yours, dispersed and settled everywhere, who formerly, not worshipping you, were doers of inauspicious acts, are now engaged in the auspicious work of your worship.
Let these my enemies, who practise deceitful acts upon me, the doer of good acts, by the use of evil words, bring harm upon themselves of their own accord.

These your friends, Agni, everywhere dispersed, were formerly unhappy (in abandoning your worship), but are again fortunate (by its renewal); may they who, with (censorous) words, impute fraudulent (practices) to me who pursue a straight path, bring evil upon themselves.

Those who are now good men were formerly, that is, before worshipping Agni, wicked and used to do evil deeds. All such wicked people, having worshipped Agni and thereby gained good sense, have become good men. But for all those who have not become good in that way by serving Agni, the wicked people who are my enemies and deceive me, may harm come according to the fruit of their deeds. This is the main purport.

O Agni, the man who praises you, the one worthy of worship, with reverent praise; or else, the man who worships you with the oblation in the form of food, offering the sacrifice to you. (The explanation of the verbal form for this second view is a matter of grammar.) He protects the praise belonging to Agni, the shining one, the showerer of desires. The house of that sacrificer becomes extensive, that is, it becomes full of wealth such as cattle. To the man who goes forth in service of you, may a virtuous remnant, one who accomplishes desires, come: what remains is called the remnant, that is, a son; the meaning is "may he come, may he be".
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of the one who has a radiant lustre ⟨NOTE:16⟩
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of Agni, the showerer of desires
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the praise that is a part of the sacrifice
- आ एतु (*ā etu*)—may he be born
notes: ಅರೋಚಕವಾದ ಕಾಂತಿಯುಳ್ಳವನೂ printed (Bhāvārtha ಆರೋಚಕವಾದ); Sāyaṇa ರೋಚಮಾನಸ್ಯ; read here as "radiant"

en: O Agni, the man who praises you, the one worthy of worship, with reverent praise protects the praise, a part of the sacrifice, of Agni, who is radiant and a showerer of desires. The dwelling-house of that same sacrificer grows extensive. To the man who worships you most excellently, may a son of good understanding be born.

May the dwelling of him, Agni, who celebrates your worship with reverence, of him who protects the sacrifice (offered) to the resplendent showerer (of benefits), be well stored and may a virtuous successor of the man who diligently worships you come in his place.

In the two preceding Ṛks the seer told of the troubles that come to those who do not worship Agni; in this Ṛk he describes the fruit that comes to those who praise Agni and offer oblations. The houses of the good men who, offering oblations to Agni, the one worthy of sacrifice, worship with salutation and praise the shining Agni, the giver of what is desired, will prosper. Prosperity in cattle and the like will come to them. A good and worthy son will be born to them: so the seer has described.

O Agni, we who adore you invoke you. Adoring, that is, praising, we kindle you with fuel-sticks, we make you blaze, for our protection or for your satisfaction. The word अर्चंत (*arcaṃta*) stands a third time for the sake of great respect.
O Agni, worshipping you, we pray and call you for our help. Praising you, we make you blaze for our protection.
Adoring you, Agni, we invoke you: adoring you we kindle you, adoring you for protection.
We who desire wealth recite today, on this day, the praise of the shining Agni, who pervades the sky in the form of the sun: a praise that accomplishes the aims of man.
- दिविस्पृशः (*divispṛśaḥ*)—of him who pervades the intermediate space in the form of the sun
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—the praise that is addressed to Agni
- सिद्धं (*siddhaṃ*)—that accomplishes the aims of man
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice

We who desire wealth recite, at the time of this sacrifice, the praise addressed to the shining Agni, who pervades the intermediate space in the form of the sun, the praise that accomplishes the aims of man.
Desirous of wealth, we recite to-day the effectual praise of the divine Agni, (whose radiance) reaches the sky.

It has been explained many times before that Agni pervades in three forms: in heaven in the form of Āditya, in the intermediate space in the form of lightning-fire, and on earth in the form of terrestrial fire (the sacrificial fire, the household fire or the forest fire). In the present Ṛk it is explained that Agni shines in heaven (the intermediate space) in the form of the sun.

सिद्ध्रं-साधनं । (*siddhraṃ-sādhanaṃ |*) Yāska has explained that the word sidhra has the meaning "means" (Ni. 9-38), and as an example has cited the mantra ⟨NOTE:18⟩ द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्स,शं । यज्ञं देवेषु यच्छतां ॥ (*dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ sidhramadya divissa,śaṃ | yajñaṃ deveṣu yacchatāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-20).
notes: ಮಕ್ಕಳನ್ನು printed (ಮಂತ್ರವನ್ನು?)

en: The Hotā, the invoker of the gods, who dwells among men: may that Agni accept our praises, that is, partake of them. May that Agni offer sacrifice to the people connected with the gods.
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words in the form of praise
- दैव्यं जनं (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*)—with reference to people of divine nature
May that Agni who stands in the midst of men partake of our praises, and may he perform the sacrifice with reference to the people of divine nature.
May Agni, who amongst men is the invoker of the gods, accept our praises ; may he offer sacrifice to the divine beings-

यः अग्निः मानुषेषु आ (*yaḥ agniḥ mānuṣeṣu ā*)—the Agni who is among men, that is, the sacrificial fire established on the sacrificial altar in the form of Gārhapatya and the rest. In the preceding Ṛk the Agni who is in heaven in the form of Āditya was praised; in this Ṛk the terrestrial Agni is praised. Although the terrestrial fire has the varieties sacrificial fire, household fire and forest fire, here there is the prayer नः गिरः जुषत (*naḥ giraḥ juṣata*), "may he partake of our praises", and so it should be understood that the praise is addressed to the sacrificial fire alone.
दै व्यं जनं (*dai vyaṃ janaṃ*)—देवसंबंधिनं जनं (*devasaṃbaṃdhinaṃ janaṃ*): people connected with the gods, that is, the gods who are invoked in the sacrifice: such is the purport.

O Agni, you who are ever pleased, who are to be chosen by all, the Hotā, are spread widely everywhere. So Yāska says: सर्वतः पृथुः (*sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) (Ni. 6. 7.). Moreover, all sacrificers extend the sacrifice by you as the means.
- सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—having gained pre-eminence in every way
- वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*)—(the sacrificers) carry out
O Agni, you who are fully satisfied, honoured by all and the accomplisher of the offering, have gained pre-eminence in every way. By your help alone the sacrificers carry out the sacrifice.
You, Agni, are mighty and gracious, the (ministrant) priest, the desired (of all): through you worshippers complete the sacrifice.
जुष्टः (*juṣṭaḥ*)—सर्वदा प्रीतः (*sarvadā prītaḥ*). The purport is: one who is always pleased, who is delighted, with the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice.

वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—सर्वैर्वर्णीयः (*sarvairvarṇīyaḥ*): one who is desired by all. Since a sacrifice cannot be performed without Agni, all people, the sacrificers and the rest, desire Agni; Agni is needed by all. Therefore in the second half of this Ṛk it is said त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते (*tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvate*): all perform the sacrifice by you (with your help).

सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—सर्वतः पृथुः (*sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*). त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असीत्यपि निगमो भवति (*tvamagne saprathā asītyapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-7). Since Agni pervades everywhere (when he burns), he spreads very widely: thus Yāska explained the meaning of the word saprathāḥ and gave this very Ṛk as the example.

O Agni, the wise praisers, the intelligent ones, make you grow with their hymns: you, the giver of food (vāja is food, and you give it), well praised by the great seers of old, thoroughly praised. May you, such as you are, give us excellent strength that is to be praised by all.
O Agni, the wise praisers cause you to grow, you who are the giver of food and are praised by all. May you, such as you are, produce praiseworthy strength for us.
Wise worshippers exalt you, Agni, the bountiful giver of food, the deservedly lauded : bestow upon us excellent strength.

विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—The word vipra is read among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19); it means intelligent people. This word is also used in the sense of the officiating priests who take part in the sacrifice and of the praisers. There is the explanation of Durgācārya: विविधानर्थानस्य प्राप्तुं धातीति विप्रः (*vividhānarthānasya prāptuṃ dhātīti vipraḥ*). Saying that medhāvin means one who possesses intellect, Yāska states the etymology मेधावी कस्मान्मेधया तद्वान् भवति । मेधा मता धीयते । (*medhāvī kasmānmedhayā tadvān bhavati | medhā matā dhīyate |*) (Ni. 3-19). Asking what a medhāvin is, he explains the meaning: the man in whose intellect there is excellent knowledge, a man who possesses such power of intellect.

वाजसातमं सुष्टुतं विप्रा वर्धंति (*vājasātamaṃ suṣṭutaṃ viprā vardhaṃti*)—the people who, praising him with hymns and the like, offer oblations in the sacrifice, this Agni, the giver of food and praised by all, in the sacrifices with fuel and the like
materials, and with oblations of ghee, make to blaze well (to burn brilliantly): such is the purport.

O Agni, you surround the gods, that is, you surpass them by your own brilliance. How? Like the shining outer rim of a wheel, which encloses the spokes fixed in the nave, the fine supports, as it were. Moreover you bring about manifold राधः (*rādhaḥ*), riches: that by which men accomplish their aims is riches. Accomplish them for your praisers. Since the word is read among the names of wealth, it is said that riches means wealth.
- नेमिः (*nemiḥ*)—the outer rim of the wheel
- अरानिव (*arāniva*)—as if encircling all the spokes inside the wheel
O Agni, as the outer rim of a wheel surrounds all the spokes inside the wheel, you surround and pervade all the gods. May you, who have such greatness, fill us, your praisers, with manifold riches.
Agni, you encompass the gods as the circumference (surrounds) the spokes (of a wheel) : bestow manifold wealth upon us.

अग्ने । नेमिः । अरान् इव । देवान् । त्वं । परिभूः । असि । (*agne | nemiḥ | arān iva | devān | tvaṃ | paribhūḥ | asi |*)—As in the wheel of a chariot the outer rim (Rim, or Tyre) surrounds and encloses the spokes (Spokes), Agni stays surrounding all the gods. That is, since he carries the oblation to all the gods, he stays near those gods; the purport is suggested that he goes to all the gods and returns for the carrying of the oblation.

O praiser, awaken Agni, the immortal, who has not the nature of dying, with praise, that is, with a hymn; awaken him thoroughly for the accomplishment of your desired aims. May that Agni, who is well kindled by hymns, that is, shines well, place our oblations among the gods.
- (O praiser) अमूर्त्यं (*amūrtyaṃ*)—who is free from the nature of death
O praiser, awaken with praise Agni, who is free from the nature of death. May Agni, well kindled, take our oblations and place them among the gods.
Waken the immortal Agni with praise, that, being kindled, he may bear our oblations to the gods.

In this Ṛk, the words "awaken Agni, who is free from the nature of death, with praise and the like" are said with reference to the praise. That is, the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, addressing the priests such as the Adhvaryu, says "produce Agni by churning, with mantras"; this

meaning is suggested here. How is Agni free from the nature of death? By offering to Agni fuel and oblations such as ghee, he is always shining without going out: this purport is suggested by the word अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*). Since the churning of fire is one of the rites to be performed at the beginning of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is clearly praying to the Adhvaryu that he should produce Agni by churning; to the Hotṛ that he should recite the mantras prescribed for that churning; to the Udgātṛ that he should sing the Sāma mantras such as the Stoma; to the other priests that they should offer in the fire oblations and the like for the gods; and finally to Agni that he should carry the oblations offered to the gods who are intended.

Mortals, that is, men, praise at the sacrifices with seven strands that Agni, the shining, immortal one, who has not the nature of dying, the best sacrificer in the world of men, that is, among the people connected with men.
- अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*)—free from the nature of death
Men praise in the sacrifices Agni, the shining one, the most worshipful in the human world, who is free from the nature of death.
Mortals worship him, an immortal divinity, at their sacrifices, most adorable among the human race.

मानुषे लोके अध्वरेषु मर्त्याः (*mānuṣe loke adhvareṣu martyāḥ*) praise: in the world of men, that is, on this earth, in the sacrificial rites proceeding on the sacrificial altar, men who are sacrificers praise Agni with various praises: this is the purport.

The many praisers praise that god Agni. What are they like? They are provided with a ladle that pours ghee. For what purpose do they praise him? For the carrying of the oblation, which has the form of cooked rice, cake and the like, to carry it.
- वोढवे (*voḍhave*)—in order to carry (to the gods)
Many praisers, provided with the oblation-vessel that pours streams of ghee, praise that same Agni, who is of divine nature, in order to carry the oblation to the gods.
Numerous (worshippers), pouring out butter from the (sacrificial) ladle, glorify him, the divine Agni, that he may convey their oblation (to the gods).

धृतश्चुता—धृतं क्षरंत्या स्रुचा । (*dhṛtaścutā—dhṛtaṃ kṣaraṃtyā srucā |*) Pouring ghee; that is, when making an offering they fill wooden ladles with ājya (clarified butter) and offer it in the fire. Those ladles are called sruk. Because ghee is poured into the fire from such ladles, they are described by the word धृतश्चुता (*dhṛtaścutā*).

Agni, born, that is, manifested by the churning of the two fire-sticks, slaying the dasyus, the enemies who obstruct the sacrifice, shone, that is, blazed, destroying the darkness by his own light, his own brilliance. Moreover he found गा (*gā*), the waters, and svar, the sun: he made them known. ⟨NOTE:19⟩
notes: ಗಾ ಅಪ ಉದಕಾನಿ: Sāyaṇa glosses only the waters; the Kannada gloss has ಗಾಃ—ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನೂ

en: - जातः (*jātaḥ*)—as soon as he is born
- दस्यून् (*dasyūn*)—the enemies who cause obstruction to the sacrifice
As soon as he is born, Agni shone, destroying the enemies who cause obstruction to the sacrifice and driving away the darkness by his own radiance. He made the cows, the waters and the sun manifest.
Agni, as soon as born, blazes brightly, destroying the Dasyus, and (dispersing) the darkness by his lustre: he has discovered the cows, the waters, the sun.

In the sacrifice, as soon as Agni is brought forth by the act of churning, the darkness is dispelled by his radiance and everything comes to shine with light. The cows, the waters and the sun as well engaged in their respective functions: this is the main import.

Addressing the people: worship Agni, who is ईळेन्यं (*īḷenyaṃ*), praiseworthy; कविं (*kaviṃ*), far-seeing (क्रांतदर्शिनं (*krāṃtadarśinaṃ*)); and धृतपृष्ठं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaṃ*), he whose upper part of the flame. May that Agni desire (कामयतां (*kāmayatāṃ*)) my invocation, that is, my call, and may he hear it.
- धृतपृष्ठं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaṃ*)—having a flame whose base is held (fed) by ghee ⟨NOTE:20⟩
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the praise in the form of an invocation
notes: ಧೃತಮೂಲವಾದ ಜ್ವಾಲೆ in the Kannada gloss; Sāyaṇa has ದೀಪೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ, the upper part of the flame

en: Worship Agni, who is worthy of praise, far-seeing, and has a flame whose base is held by ghee. May that same Agni know my praise, which takes the form of an invocation, and listen and hear it.
Worship the adorable Agni, the sage, whose summit blazes with butter : may he hear and comprehend my invocation.

धृतसृष्टं—दीप्तोपरिभागं (*dhṛtasṛṣṭaṃ—dīptoparibhāgaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:21⟩ Because ghee (ājya, ghṛta) is offered into the fire, Agni is described by the epithet that speaks of ghee at his summit; that is, by the oblations of ghee Agni blazes up well and shines. The meaning is: worship such a resplendent Agni.
notes: ಧೃತಸೃಷ್ಟಂ here against ಧೃತಪೃಷ್ಠಂ in the verse and bhāṣya; ದೀಪ್ತೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ against ದೀಪೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ in the bhāṣya

en: The priests (ऋत्विजो (*ṛtvijo*)) augmented Agni, who is विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*), the beholder of all, and who is accompanied by the gods, who are स्वाधीभिः (*svādhībhiḥ*), of good meditation, and वचस्युभिः (*vacasyubhiḥ*), desirous of praise; they augmented him with ghee and with स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*), praises, that is, hymns of praise.
- वचस्युभिः (*vacasyubhiḥ*)—and desirous of praise, accompanied by the gods
- विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*)—having the power to see all
The priests made Agni grow with ghee and with praises: Agni, who is accompanied by gods worthy of excellent meditation and desirous of praise, and who has the power to see all.
They have augmented Agni, the beholder of all, with oblation and with praises, along with the gods, the objects of pious meditations, desirous of praise.

In the sacrifice the priests caused Agni, who is accompanied by gods worthy of meditation and of praise, and who is able to see everything, to blaze and shine by the oblations of ghee offered with mantras. That is, by the oblations of ghee which the priests offer with mantras, Agni blazed and shone: this is the purport.

The Agni who is घृतप्रसत्तो (*ghṛtaprasatto*), gratified by ghee in the form of the oblation; strong; सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*), one whose शेवं (*śevaṃ*), happiness, is good, since शेव (*śeva*) is read among the names of happiness; रायो (*rāyo*) धर्ता (*dhartā*), the supporter, that is, nourisher, of wealth; धरुणो (*dharuṇo*), the holder of the oblations; and वस्वो (*vasvo*), the bestower of dwelling: that Agni is so. To the वेधसे (*vedhase*), creator; कवये (*kavaye*), far-seeing (क्रांतदृशे (*krāṃtadṛśe*)); वेद्याय (*vedyāya*), worthy of praise (the root विदि (*vidi*) here has the same sense as मनि (*mani*), and मनि (*mani*) denotes the act of praising); to the renowned (यशसे (*yaśase*)), the foremost (पूर्वाय (*pūrvāya*), chief): to that Agni I offer (प्र भरे (*pra bhare*), may I present, प्रणयानि (*praṇayāni*)) praise.
- धरुणः (*dharuṇaḥ*)—the one who holds the oblation
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—the giver of dwelling, he is
- पूर्वाय्य (*pūrvāyya*)—and foremost; addressing such an Agni
- प्र भरे (*pra bhare*)—I produce well and offer

Agni is one who is gratified by ghee, powerful, endowed with excellent happiness, the nourisher of wealth, the one who holds the oblation and the giver of dwelling. Addressing that Agni, who is the creator, of far-reaching wisdom, worthy of praise, famous and foremost, I compose excellent praise and offer it.

I offer praise to Agni, the creator, the far-seeing, the adorable, the renowned, the first (of the gods); he who is propitiated by oblations, the strong, the giver of happiness, the possessor of riches, the receiver of oblations, the bestower of dwellings.

The sacrificers (yajamānas) who, in the sacrifice that is the धरुणे (*dharuṇe*), upholder, of दिवो (*divo*), the world of heaven, reach (अभि ननक्षुः (*abhi nanakṣuḥ*), approach) together with the born men, the priests, the unborn gods, the leaders, who are seated (सेदुष आसीनान् (*seduṣa āsīnān*)) there: those sacrificers uphold (धारयंत (*dhārayaṃta*) is धारयंति (*dhārayaṃti*)) with ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), praise, Agni, who is the upholder of the sacrifice and of the nature of truth, in the excellent place, the व्योमन् (*vyoman*), namely the uttaravedi, in the rite (शाके (*śāke*), the occasion of the rite).
- जातैः (*jātaiḥ*)—with the priests who are human beings
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—and of the nature of truth, Agni
- शाके (*śāke*)—that which is the occasion of the rite
- व्योमन् (*vyoman*)—in the place that has the form of the uttaravedi

The sacrificers who bring together, with the human priests, the gods who are seated in the sacrifice that upholds the world of heaven, the leaders, the unborn: those sacrificers have established and made stand, with praise, Agni, the upholder of the sacrifice and of the nature of truth, in the place that has the form of the uttaravedi, which is the occasion of the rite and excellent.

They are detaining by sacrifice the true recipient (of offerings) in the most eminent place of the ceremony, who brings together the leaders (of the rite), the unborn, with the born (or gods and men), as seated at the solemnity which is the stay of heaven.

The sacrificers who offer to that Agni, the foremost (पूर्वाय्य (*pūrvāyya*), chief), abundant food, वयो (*vayo*), in the form of the oblation, which is great (महदधिकं (*mahadadhikaṃ*), exceeding) and hard for the Rākṣasas to obtain: those sacrificers free their own bodies from sin (तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*) is their own bodies; अंहोयुवः (*aṃhoyuvaḥ*) means separating from sin) and extend them (वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*), they spread them out). May the newly born Agni overcome (तुतुर्यात् (*tuturyāt*), तरतु (*taratu*)) the enemies assembled (संवतः (*saṃvataḥ*), संगतान् (*saṃgatān*)). Moreover, may the enemies who are all around keep away from me and stand apart, as animals keep away from an angry lion.
- दुष्टरं (*duṣṭaraṃ*)—and not to be obtained by the Asuras
- अंहोयुवः (*aṃhoyuvaḥ*)—having made them free of sin
- वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*)—they cause to grow
- सिंहं न (*siṃhaṃ na*)—as all the animals, afraid of a lion, stand in very distant regions!
- स्थुः (*sthuḥ*)—may they come to stand far away

The sacrificers who offer to the foremost god Agni the oblation that is most abundant and cannot be obtained by the Asuras make their bodies free of sin and cause them to grow. May the newly born Agni drive far away the enemies who have gathered round. As all the animals, afraid of an angry lion, stand in very distant regions, so may all the enemies, afraid at the sight of me, not come near me but stand far away.

They who (present) to the chief (of the gods) the great food (of sacrifice, unattainable {by the Rakshasas), enjoy forms exempt from defect: may that new born Agni scatter assembled (hosts): let them stand from around me, as (deer avoid) an angry lion.

When you, पप्रथानः (*paprathānaḥ*), spreading everywhere, sustain every man like a mother; and when, for support (धायसे (*dhāyase*), धारणाय (*dhāraṇāya*)) and for seeing (चक्षसे (*cakṣase*), दर्शनाय (*darśanāya*)), you are prayed to by all; and when you are being held (दधानो (*dadhāno*), धार्यमाणो (*dhāryamāṇo*)), then you bring to maturity (जरयसि (*jarayasi*)) all food, वयो वयः (*vayo vayaḥ*). Moreover, being विषुरूपो (*viṣurūpo*), of manifold form, you go round all beings by yourself (त्मनात्मना (*tmanātmanā*)).
- धायसे (*dhāyase*)—for the support of the world
- चक्षसे च (*cakṣase ca*)—and also for looking graciously (you are prayed to, when)
- परि जिगासि (*pari jigāsi*)—you pervade everything and make it enter into yourself

O Agni, when, having gained increase everywhere, you bear all people like a mother, and are prayed to for the support of the world and for looking on it with a gracious eye, and when, held by all, you cause all food to ripen, then, possessing forms of many kinds, you pervade everything by your own greatness and make it enter into yourself.

When, everywhere predominating, you cherish all men like a mother, and (are implored by all) to behold and to support them : and when, being detained, you mature every kind of food, then, multiform (Agni), you comprise (all beings) in yourself.

O shining Agni: may the food in the form of the oblation, which is उरुं (*uruṃ*), vast, दोघं (*doghaṃ*), the yielder of desires, and धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*), the supporter, of wealth, guard today the end (अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*), completion, fulfilment) of your strength. As a thief (तायुर् (*tāyur*)) guards an article that he keeps hidden in a cave, so you, for great wealth, that is, for the winning of wealth, showing the good path, gratify the seer Atri.
- देव (*deva*)—O Agni, who are of divine nature
- वाजः (*vājaḥ*)—the food in the form of the oblation
- तायुः न (*tāyuḥ na*)—as a thief carefully guards it

O Agni, who are of divine nature, may the food in the form of the oblation, which is abundant, yields desires and supports wealth, protect your strength entirely. For the winning of great wealth, showing us the good path, protect Atri carefully and gratify him, as a thief who has obtained property hidden in a cave guards it with care.

Divine Agni, may the (sacrificial) food, the vast yielder (of benefits to men), the sustainer of riches, support the utmost of your vigour ; and do you, considering (the means of acquiring) great riches, like a thief keeping concealed the article (he has stolen), be propitious to Atri.

In the sacrifice abundant food, बृहद्वयो (*bṛhadvayo*), in the form of the oblation, is given to the radiant (दीप्तिमते (*dīptimate*)) Agni. Therefore you also offer food (अर्च (*arca*), give) to the shining god Agni, whom men set in front, as a friend, with excellent praises (प्रशस्तिभिः (*praśastibhiḥ*), प्रकृष्टाभिः (*prakṛṣṭābhiḥ*)): they place him first.
Addressing Agni, who is divine and radiant, whom men have established in front of them, praising him with excellent praises as they honour their friends, offer abundant oblation.
Offer abundant (sacrificial) food to the brilliant divine Agni, whom mortals have placed before them by praises as a friend.

The Agni who makes the oblation attached (आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)) among the gods, who is possessed of the splendours (द्युभिर् (*dyubhir*)) of strength in his arms (बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)), becomes the invoker (होता (*hotā*)) of the gods for the people, that is, the sacrificers. Like Bhaga, that is, like the sun, he bestows especially (व्यृण्वति (*vyṛṇvati*)) desirable wealth (वारं (*vāraṃ*)) upon men.
- स हि अग्निः (*sa hi agniḥ*)—that same god Agni
- होता (*hotā*)—being in the form of the invoking priest
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—he provides (for the gods) in due succession
- भगः न (*bhagaḥ na*)—(and) like the sun
- वि ऋण्वति (*vi ṛṇvati*)—he gives in a special manner

That same god Agni, endowed with the splendours that are the strength of his arms, and being the invoking priest for the sacrificers, provides the oblation in due order and succession to all the gods. And like the sun he supplies men with the wealth they desire.

For that Agni, (endowed) with the lustre of the strength of his arms, is the ministrant priest of mortals, who (presents) the oblation to the gods in succession, and like Bhaga distributes desirable wealth.
भगो न-सूर्य इव (*bhago na-sūrya iva*). Like the sun. As the sun is needed by everyone, so wealth too is a thing needed by everyone. The meaning is that everyone desires it.

May we be in the praise (स्तोमे (*stome*)) and in the friendship of such an Agni: he is मघोनो (*maghono*), the possessor of wealth, and वृद्धशोचिषः (*vṛddhaśociṣaḥ*), one whose splendours, that is, lustres, are great. He is the lord, loud with much sound, in whom all (विश्वे (*viśve*), all the priests) place strength (शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*), बलं (*balaṃ*)) fully, with oblations and with praises.
- सं आदधुः (*saṃ ādadhuḥ*)—have placed in full: of such
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—and in friendship may we be
notes: ತುವಿಷ್ಟಣಿ here, ತುವಿಷ್ವಣಿ in the Saṃhitā, ತುವಿಸ್ವನಿ in the Pada

en: May we be in the act of praise and in the friendship of this Agni, who is the possessor of wealth and of abundant radiance, who has much sound, who is the lord of all, and in whom all the priests have placed strength.

(May we be assiduous) in the praise, (and cherished) in the friendship, of that very radiant possessor of wealth, on whom, loud-sounding and all-ruling, (his) universal (worshippers) have conferred vigour.
तुविष्टणे बहुशब्दे (*tuviṣṭaṇe bahuśabde*). It is a matter of experience that when a fire is burning it makes a sound such as crackling and so on.

O Agni, then (अध (*adha*) is अथ (*atha*)): for us, the sacrificers, be disposed to giving (मंहना (*maṃhanā*) means दानाय (*dānāya*); the root मंहति (*maṃhati*) is read as a verb of giving) of the excellent strength (सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*)) that is desired by all. Heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)) have encompassed (परिगृह्णीतः (*parigṛhṇītaḥ*)) that very Agni, glory (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)) to be heard by all, as they encompass the great sun (यह्वं न (*yahvaṃ na*)).
- यह्वं न (*yahvaṃ na*)—as they surround the great sun

O Agni, after our time of worship, be of gracious mind to give us, the sacrificers, excellent strength and wealth. Heaven and earth both stand surrounding the renowned Agni, as they surround the great sun.
Now verily, Agni, (be disposed) for bestowing excellent strength on these (your worshippers): heaven and earth have invested him with glory like the vast (sun).

O Agni, being praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*), स्तूयमानः (*stūyamānaḥ*)), come quickly to the sacrifice; and having come, bring us desirable wealth (वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*), वरणेयं (*varaṇeyaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:24⟩), that is, provide it. We who are the sacrificers and those who are the praisers (सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*), स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*)), both together with oblations (सचा (*sacā*)), offer praise (स्वस्ति (*svasti*), स्तोत्रं (*stotraṃ*); धामहे (*dhāmahe*), we make). And be for our increase and prosperity in the battles (पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*), पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)).
notes: ವರಣೇಯಂ printed; ವರಣೀಯಂ expected

en: - ये वयं (*ye vayaṃ*)—we who are the sacrificers
- ये च (*ye ca*)—and we who are
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the praisers, we who worship in both ways
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—the praise that goes to meet you

O Agni, praised by us, come to our sacrifice at once. We who are sacrificers and praisers, worshipping you by both kinds of rites, prepared with the oblations, offer the praise that goes to meet you. Be gracious, so that victory and increase may be ours in the battles.

Glorified by us, Agni, come quickly, and bring us desirable wealth : we who (are your worshippers), we (who are your) adorers, offer you welcome together with oblations: be favourable to us; be (our) success in battles.

O god Agni: a mortal, that is, a man, the priest (ऋत्विगित्थेत्थं (*ṛtvigitthetthaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:25⟩), thus calls with sacrifices, that is, with praises, for his gratification (ऊतये (*ūtaye*), तर्पणाय (*tarpaṇāya*)) you, Agni, who are तव्यांसं (*tavyāṃsaṃ*), grown strong by your own splendours. Moreover Pūru, a man and a praiser, in the sacrifice well performed (कृते स्वध्वरे (*kṛte svadhvare*)), praises that Agni for protection (अवसे (*avase*), रक्षणाय (*rakṣaṇāya*)).
notes: ಋತ್ವಿಗಿತ್ಥೇತ್ಥಂ glued as printed

en: - तव्यांसं (*tavyāṃsaṃ*)—you, who have grown by your own splendour
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—with praises that are parts of the sacrifice

O Agni, of divine nature, the human priest calls and prays to you, who have grown by your own splendour, for protection, in the prescribed manner, with praises that are parts of the sacrifice. Pūru the praiser, at the time of the performance of an excellent sacrifice, praises Agni for protection.
Divine Agni, a mortal thus with sacrifices (calls upon you) who are endowed with lustre for protection : Puru adores Agni for protection when the sacred rite is solemnized.

पूरुः (*pūruḥ*). In this ṛk the seer has spoken his own name. Although the verbs of the doer are in the third person, their use in the sense of the first person is a special usage current in the Ṛgveda.

Sāyaṇa addresses the praiser: "O Vidharman", that is, one whose dharma is distinguished (viśiṣṭa); this is a vocative for the praiser. The praiser is स्वयशस्तरः (*svayaśastaraḥ*), the most renowned among those of good renown. With a mind of excellent understanding, as his means, he praises with his mouth that well-known Agni (the "hi" marks him as famous).
