Agni is of this kind: "nāka" is happiness; "aka" is pain; he for whom there is no pain is nāka. He is of wonderful lustre (चित्रतोभिषं (*citratobhiṣaṃ*) is glossed as "of wonderful radiance"), adorable (मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*) is glossed as "worthy of praise"), and supreme. ⟨NOTE:26⟩
notes: ಪರಃ ಪರಸ್ತಾಶ್ಚಿತಂ — the gloss of ಪರಃ is damaged in the bhāṣya; not construed

en: - विधर्मान् (*vidharmān*)—O praiser, who have faith in various rites
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—him who is free from pain
- परः (*paraḥ*)—who has a power surpassing worldly condition
- तं अस्य हि (*taṃ asya hi*)—that very Agni

O praiser, who with faith perform many rites, you, being of exceeding fame, praise with speech endowed with excellent understanding that very Agni, who is free from pain, of manifold splendour, worthy of praise, and of a power surpassing worldly condition.

Performer of various functions, who are deservedly renowned, you praise by your words that Agni, who is possessed of wonderful splendour ; who is exempt from pain ; who is adorable and supreme in understanding.
नाकं (*nākaṃ*): अकं दुःखं । न विद तेऽकं यस्य सः (*akaṃ duḥkhaṃ | na vida te 'kaṃ yasya saḥ*). "Aka" means pain; the absence of pain is "nāka", that is, happiness. This is the meaning intended.

The Agni who is joined with praise (gir) accompanied by "tuja", that is, a strength able to protect the world, is meant here. Like the shining sun, the whole world is pervaded by the radiance (retas) of whichever Agni it is whose great flames (arcayaḥ, दीप्तयः (*dīptayaḥ*)) shine forth. By the radiance of this Agni the sun becomes radiant. The word "u" is a mere filler. ⟨NOTE:27⟩
notes: ದಿವೋ ನ — Sāyaṇa glosses it as "of the shining sun"; the Kannada gloss reads "like the luminous atmosphere (ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷ)"

en: - तुजा (*tujā*)—accompanied by the capacity to protect the world
- दिवो न (*divo na*)—like the luminous atmosphere
- अर्चिषा वै (*arciṣā vai*)—by the radiance alone

The Agni who joins with praise accompanied by the capacity to protect the world, and by whose radiance all the rays, of great form like the luminous atmosphere, shine: by the radiance of that Agni alone the sun too becomes radiant.
He who is endowed with vigour, is (glorified) by praise, and by whose radiance, like that of the sky, the rays of light shine brightly : by his lustre, verily, (the sun is luminous).

In this Ṛk it is described that the sun shines by the radiance of Agni. In many places it is said that Agni shines in heaven (the atmosphere) in the form of the sun, which is one of his three forms. The same idea is indicated here.

The vicetasaḥ are the priests of good understanding. By the kratu, that is, by the rite such as the sacrifice, of this Agni, who is "dasma", pleasing to see, they place (ā dadhati) wealth in the chariot. That Agni, who is to be invoked for the sacrifice, is then, immediately after his birth, praised among all the people (vikṣu, प्रजासु (*prajāsu*)).
- दस्मस्य (*dasmasya*)—of him who has an attractive form
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—as the fruit of the rite of worship
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—who is worthy of the oblation

As the fruit of worshipping this Agni, who has an attractive form, the priests of excellent understanding fill their chariots with wealth. Agni, who is worthy of the oblation, is praised by all the people.
By the worship of him who is pleasing of aspect, the provident (heap) wealth in their cars : Agni, to whom oblations are due, is then grorified by people.

"O Agni, give us quickly (nu) the desirable (vāryam) wealth"; "id" is a filler. For the praisers (sūrayaḥ) obtain wealth from you by their praise (āsā, "āsyena stotreṇa"). Further, O "ūrjo napāt": son of food, or son of strength, that is, "not letting food fall". अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*) is for one who desires: the sense to be supplied is "give me food". "Protect us from calamities." "Svastaye": for welfare, for the welfare of wealth such as cattle: "be able" (शग्धि (*śagdhi*)), that is, "I ask you"; the second person is used for the first by interchange. Or it may mean "be able". "And, O Agni, in battles (pṛtsu, पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)) be (edhi, "bhava") for our growth." ⟨NOTE:28⟩
notes: ಮೃಧೇ printed in the bhāṣya for the verse's ವೃಧೇ

en: - उर्जो नपात् (*urjo napāt*)—O Agni, son of strength
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—to me, who desire food (give food)
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for the securing of our welfare
notes: ವಿಧಿ printed in the Pratipadārtha; the verse has ಏಧಿ

en: O Agni, grant quickly to us also that same desired wealth which the praisers obtain by their praises. O Agni, son of strength, give food to me, who desire food. Protect me. Be able to secure our welfare. And in battles be a helper for our victory and growth.

Quickly, (Agni, give us) desirable (wealth), such as the devout combining with (pious) praise, (obtain): son of strength, (be favourable) to (my) desires ; protect us (from calamity); be alert for our prosperity ; come for our success in battles.

ऊर्जोनपात् (*ūrjonapāt*): अन्नस्य पातयितः बलस्य पुत्र ना (*annasya pātayitaḥ balasya putra nā*) ⟨NOTE:30⟩. Since the word ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*) has the meanings food and strength, Agni is addressed either as the lord of food, or as the son of strength, that is, one born from the churning done with the use of strength.

शग्गि (*śaggi*): याचे (*yāce*). "I pray." Here the second person singular is used in place of the first person singular. Such usages, and the interchange of case-endings and numbers, are specially employed in the Ṛgveda.
notes: ನಾ printed; the bhāṣya has ವಾ

en: "Puru-priya" is "much loved". विशः (*viśaḥ*) is the one who establishes wealth in the sacrificer. He is the "atithi" (guest): one who comes to the houses of the sacrificers on the lunar days (tithi). So Yāska says: अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान्भवत्य- (*atithirabhyatito gṛhānbhavatya-*) (the passage breaks off at the end of this page and continues in the next window).

Sāyaṇa completes the quotation from Yāska: भ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा (*bhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā*) (Ni. 4-5), that is, one who comes on the lunar days to the families of others or to the houses of others. Such an Agni is praised in the morning (प्रातः (*prātaḥ*), स्तूयते (*stūyate*)). The immortal Agni (one whose nature is not to die) desires (कामयते (*kāmayate*)) all the oblations that are placed among mortals, that is, among the sacrificers.
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—who is free from the nature of death
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—worthy of worship like a guest
The immortal Agni, who desires all the oblations that are with the sacrificers, who is wanted by many and is worthy of worship for the sacrificers like a guest, is praised at the time of dawn.
Let Agni, the beloved of many, the guest of man, be present at dawn; he who, immortal, desires the oblations of mortals.

"O Agni, to Dvita", that is, the son of Dvita, who is "mṛktavāhas": one who carries ("vahati", "prāpayati") pure ("mṛkta", "śuddha") oblation to the gods. To him, for your own ("svasya", "ātmīyasya") "dakṣa", that is, strength or wealth, be of a giving mind (मंहना (*maṃhanā*) is explained as "for giving") ⟨NOTE:32⟩.
"O immortal, eternal Agni": because that Mṛktavāhas, always attached to you, holds the "indu", the Soma, and is also your praiser.
notes: ಧನಸ್ಯ ನಾ ಮುಂಹನಾ — ನಾ and ಮುಂಹನಾ as printed; the block continues on the next page with ಮಂಹನಾಯ್ಕೆ

en: - (O Agni) मृक्तवाहसे (*mṛktavāhase*)—who has pure oblation to offer to you
- मंहना (*maṃhanā*)—be one with a mind to give
- अमर्त्य (*amartya*)—O Agni, free from the nature of death
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to offer, with you in view

O Agni, be of a mind to give your own strength to Dvita, who has pure oblation to offer to you. O Agni, free from the nature of death, that Dvita, the Mṛktavāha, at all times, reciting your praise, holds the Soma in order to offer it to you.
Be (willing to make) a grant of your own strength to Dwita, the bearer of the pure oblations ; for he, immortal Agni, your diligent praiser, brings to you continually the Soma juice.

"O Agni, you whose brightness travels far": वः (*vaḥ*) is a plural used in honour (of the one addressed). I invoke ("huve", आह्वयामि (*āhvayāmi*)) you with praise on behalf of the wealthy ("maghonām"). "O giver of horses": of whichever wealthy men the chariot goes forth (वीयते (*vīyate*), "vigacchatu") unharmed (अरिष्टः (*ariṣṭaḥ*)) by enemies in battles.
- (O Agni) दीर्घायुशोचिषं (*dīrghāyuśociṣaṃ*)—who have been shining for many ages

O Agni, you who have been shining for many ages and are renowned, I praise and call you on behalf of the wealthy. O Agni, giver of horses, may the chariot of those same wealthy men travel happily in battles, not harmed by enemies.
I invoke you bright-shining, through a long life, with praise, (for the benefit) of the affluent, that their chariot, giver of horses, may proceed unimpeded.

Among whichever priests there is ("bhavati") varied (चित्रा (*citrā*), नानाविधा (*nānāvidhā*)) "dīdhiti", that is, action concerning the sacrifice; who guard in their mouths (आसन् (*āsan*), "āsye") the "ukthāni", that is, the hymns: by those priests, upon the strewn ("stīrṇam") sacred grass (बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)), the श्रवांसि (*śravāṃsi*), that is, foods and oblations, are placed ("dadhire", "nidhīyante") in the "svarṇara": "svar" is heaven, and that which leads ("nayati") the sacrificer ("nara") there is the sacrifice, "svarṇara".
- दीधितिः (*dīdhitiḥ*)—actions concerning the sacrifice are performed
- बर्हिः परि (*barhiḥ pari*)—upon the seats of sacred grass
- स्वर्णरे (*svarṇare*)—in the sacrifice that leads the sacrificer to heaven

Those priests who are renowned for performing sacrificial rites of many kinds, who always recite the hymns from their mouths and so guard them, place the oblations, for the sacrificer, upon the widely spread seats of sacred grass in the sacrifices that lead to heaven.

Amongst whom the ceremonial of many kinds is observed ; who perpetuate the sacred hymns by their recital ; by them the sacrificial viands are placed upon the strewn grass (at the sacrifice which) leads (the worshipper) to heaven.

The liberal wealthy men who gave me fifty horses together with praise ("sadhastuti"), that is, immediately after the praise of you: "O immortal Agni", for those wealthy men make (कृधि (*kṛdhi*), "kuru"; the meaning is "give") splendid ("dyumat", "dīptimat"), great ("mahi", "mahat"), abundant (बृहत् (*bṛhat*), "parivṛḍham") food (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), "annam"), accompanied by men who attend (नृवत् (*nṛvat*), "paricārakamanuṣyayukta").
- सधस्तुति (*sadhastuti*)—immediately after (praising you on their behalf)
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—accompanied by sons, grandsons and others

O immortal Agni, for those wealthy men on whose behalf I praised you, and who immediately gave me fifty horses, provide wealth of food that is splendid, great, exceedingly abundant and accompanied by sons, grandsons and others.
Immortal Agni, bestow upon those opulent men, who, upon (my) praise (of you), gave to me fifty horscs, and brilliant, ample, and abundant food, (supporting numerous) dependents.
In this Ṛk the seer says that he has praised Agni on behalf of the wealthy, prays Agni to provide them with wealth such as food, and so praises the generosity of the wealthy.

Of the seer Vanvi (the "vanir"), one after another ("abhi", "uttarottaram") unhappy states (अवस्थाः (*avasthāḥ*), "aśobhanā daśāḥ") arise ("pra jāyante"). Agni, who shares in the oblations, such as he is, is to take full note ("pra ciketa", प्रजानीयात् (*prajānīyāt*)); the sense is that, having known them, he is to remove them. This is the Agni who sees ("vi caṣṭe", पश्यति (*paśyati*)) all that exists near (समीपे (*samīpe*)) the lap ("upasthe") of the mother, the Earth. ⟨NOTE:34⟩
notes: ವನ್ವೇರ್ಖುಷೇಃ printed at the start of the bhāṣya; ವನಿಃ ಹವಿಷಾಂ ಸಂಭಕ್ತಾ read as Agni

en: - वव्रेः (*vavreḥ*)—to the seer named Vavri (to me) ⟨NOTE:35⟩
- वि चष्टे (*vi caṣṭe*)—looks upon everything, of such a kind
- प्र चिकेत (*pra ciketa*)—let him know fully (the distresses of Vavri) and destroy them
notes: ವಪ್ರಿ printed in the gloss and in the Bhāvārtha for ವವ್ರಿ

en: One after another, circumstances of distress befall the seer named Vavri (me). May Agni, who sitting in the lap of his mother, the Earth, looks upon everything, being the receiver of the oblation, know the distresses of Vavri (mine) and avert them.
Unprosperous circumstances affect Vavri: may the accepter (of oblations) become cognizant (of them), as, reclining on the lap of his mother, he beholds all things.

notes: the Pada-pāṭha of this ṛk ends with ೩; the Saṃhitā has ೨

en: O Agni, the people who, knowing ("vi citayantaḥ") your power, invoke you always ("animiṣam", सर्वदा (*sarvadā*)) for the sacrifice, and having invoked you guard your "nṛṣṇam", your strength, with oblations and with praises: they enter ("ā viviśuḥ", "praviśanti") the firm ("dṛḷhām") city that cannot be taken by enemies. As proof, the Nigama: शतं पूर्भिरायसीभिर्नि पाहि (*śataṃ pūrbhirāyasībhirni pāhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-3-7) ⟨NOTE:37⟩.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - (O Agni) वि चितयंतः (*vi citayaṃtaḥ*)—people who fully know (your power)
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect so as to increase it by hymns and the like
- दृळ्हां (*dṛḷhāṃ*)—that cannot be besieged by enemies

O Agni, the people who fully know your power always call you to the sacrifice, performing sacrifice. They protect your strength, increasing it with hymns and the like. They conquer and enter the city that cannot be besieged by enemies.
They who know (your power) invoke you incessantly and nourish (your) strength (by oblations): they dwell in an impregnable city.

"Jantavaḥ" are those who are born ("jāyanta"). कृष्टयः (*kṛṣṭayaḥ*) are men, the priests. "Madhvā na" is "as with honey", with sweet praise. Or else the particle "na" has the sense of "and", and so "and with honey". "Śvaitreyasya": "śvitra" is the atmosphere; of the Agni who is of lightning, born there, they increase the splendid ("dyumat", "dīptimat") strength. What are the kṛṣṭayaḥ like? निष्कग्रीवः (*niṣkagrīvaḥ*): those whose necks are adorned with gold, the niṣka; the singular is by interchange. Then बृह (*bṛha*). ⟨NOTE:38⟩
notes: the bhāṣya is damaged in ಐಸೈನಯಾ, ಕೃಸ್ಟಯಃ, ಶ್ವತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ ಶ್ಶಿತ್ರಮಂತರಿಕ್ಷಂ and ಅದ್ವಲಮಾ; not construed further

en: - निष्कग्रीवः (*niṣkagrīvaḥ*)—those whose necks are adorned with golden ornaments
- मध्वा न (*madhvā na*)—with praises that satisfy like honey
- तैत्रेयस्य (*taitreyasya*)—of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere ⟨NOTE:40⟩
- आ वर्धंत (*ā vardhaṃta*)—they cause to increase
notes: ಕೃಷ್ಣಯಃ printed; the verse has ಕೃಷ್ಟಯಃ
ತೈತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ printed; the verse has ಶ್ವೈತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ

en: The people, priests and others, who have necks adorned with golden ornaments, who have abundant praise, who desire food, and who have been born, cause to increase, with praises that satisfy like honey, the splendid strength of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere.
Living men, with collars of gold, earnest in praise, desirous of food, augment by this laudation the vigour of you abiding in the white firmament.

May Agni, the helper (सचा (*sacā*)) of the two kinsfolk (जाम्योः (*jāmyoḥ*)), heaven and earth, hear our dear praise, which is desirable ("kāmyam", "kamanīyam"), faultless (अजामि (*ajāmi*), "doṣarahitam"), like milk that has been drawn ("dugdham na payaḥ"). Of what kind is this Agni? Like the "gharma", the Pravargya, he is वाजजठरः (*vājajaṭharaḥ*): he in whose belly is "vāja", food; as the gharma is filled with the offering, with ghee and milk, so he is filled with oblation. अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*) is one not hurt by enemies himself; शश्वतः (*śaśvataḥ*) is eternal; दभः (*dabhaḥ*) is the one who harms enemies.
- घर्मो न (*gharmo na*)—as the Pravargya is filled with oblations of many kinds
- वाजजठरः (*vājajaṭharaḥ*)—he who has a belly filled with food
- अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)—he who is not exposed to the harm of enemies
- दभः (*dabhaḥ*)—he who harms enemies, such Agni
- जाम्योः सचा (*jāmyoḥ sacā*)—together with his kinsfolk, heaven and earth
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—this praise of ours; may he hear it

May Agni, who like the Pravargya filled with oblations of many kinds has a belly filled with food, who is not exposed to the harm of enemies and who for ever harms enemies, together with his kinsfolk, heaven and earth, hear this faultless praise of ours, beneficial like milk.

May (Agni) with his two relatives, (heaven and earth), hear this faultless (praise), acceptable as milk : he who like the mixed oblation, is filled with food, and, unsubdued, is ever the subduer of his foes.

"O rays-possessing Agni, playing (क्रीडन् (*krīḍan*)) in the forests, with the ashes (भस्मना (*bhasmanā*), the burnt remains of your own work) and with Vāyu, the impelling Maruts, well (सं (*saṃ*)) known (वेविदानः (*vevidānaḥ*), "samyag jñāyamānaḥ"), be ("ā bhuvaḥ") turned towards us." वक्षणेस्थाः (*vakṣaṇesthāḥ*) are those that stand in the fire ("vahni"); the वक्ष्यः (*vakṣyaḥ*) are the flames that carry the oblation. Those well-sharpened (सुसंशिताः (*susaṃśitāḥ*), "sutīkṣṇāḥ") flames, धृषजः (*dhṛṣajaḥ*), that is, assailants of enemies, are not to be ("na tigmāḥ", "na tīkṣṇāḥ") sharp towards this sacrificer, me ("san" is "santu").
- वायुना (*vāyunā*)—with the help of the wind
- सं वेविदानः (*saṃ vevidānaḥ*)—you who are visible to all
- आ भुवः (*ā bhuvaḥ*)—be turned towards us
- न तिग्माः सन् (*na tigmāḥ san*)—let them not be sharply burning (let them not harm)
notes: ಭಸ್ಮತಾ printed; the verse has ಭಸ್ಮನಾ

en: O Agni, who have rays, you who play in the forest with your ashes and are visible to all with the help of the wind, be turned towards us. May those flames of yours, which stand in the fire, are sharp, are enemy-seeing ⟨NOTE:42⟩ and carry the oblation, not burn sharply in regard to this sacrificer (let them not harm).
notes: ಶತ್ರುದರ್ಶಕ printed in the Bhāvārtha; the Pratipadārtha has ಶತ್ರುಧರ್ಷಕ

en: Radiant (Agni), you are made manifest by the wind, and are supporting amidst the ashes (of the forest); be present with us : and may the fierce fiery flames, destructive of foes, be gentle to this your worshipper.

"O Agni, O Vājasātama", O one who gives food in the highest degree: whatever wealth ("rayim") in the form of oblation, given by us, you approve ("manyase", "budhyase"); ("cit" is a mere filler) that wealth of ours, in the form of oblation, which is worthy to be heard ("śravāyyam", "śravaṇīyam", "śasyam") and is joined ("yujam", "yuktam") with praises (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)), convey ("panaya", "prāpaya") to the gods (देवत्रा (*devatrā*)).
- यं रयिं (*yaṃ rayiṃ*)—which wealth, in the form of our oblation
- मन्यसे (*manyase*)—you approve, of such a kind
O Agni, who give food in abundance, convey to the gods that same oblation of ours, praiseworthy and joined with praises, which is the wealth in the form of oblation that you approve.
That (sacrificial) wealth, Agni, bounteous giver of food, of which you approve, and which deserves to be commended by our praises, convey to the gods

O Agni, those men who are prosperous with wealth in the form of cattle and the like, yet do not offer you oblations, are deprived of strength or food, and so become destitute of strength and food. Further, the Asura whose observance (vrata, rite) is other than the Vedic, set apart from it, incurs your enmity and your violence, that is, severe punishment; they bring these upon themselves.
- वृद्धाः (*vṛddhāḥ*)—even though they have attained increase of wealth
- अन्यव्रतस्य (*anyavratasya*)—those who, leaving the Vedic rite, are performers of non-Vedic rites

O Agni, those men who do not offer you oblations, even though they have attained increase of wealth, become destitute of great strength. And men who have left the Vedic rite and fallen from their duty receive your enmity and violence from you.
May those prosperous men who do not offer oblations to you become destitute of great strength, and may (the followers) of other (than Vaidik) observances incur (your) enmity and punishment.

O Agni, we who are called Prayasvats, that is, possessors of food, choose you as hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, you who are the accomplisher, the one who brings about, of strength. Moreover, you who are foremost, the chief, at sacrifices, we call upon with speech in the form of praise; that is, we praise you.
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—as the one who calls the gods to the sacrifice (as hotṛ)
O Agni, we who are called Prayasvats choose you, the accomplisher of strength, as hotṛ. We pray to you, the chief at the sacrifice, and call upon you with words of praise.
We, Prayasvats, have recourse to you, the invoker (of the gods), the means of strength : we glorify you first at sacrifices with praise.

O Agni, possessor of strength, day after day do so (ittha), act in such a way that we may be in your protection. O doer of good deeds, act so that we may be (devoted) to wealth and to the sacrifice. Moreover, may we rejoice together with cattle, and rejoice together with sons, who are heroes (vīra); act so.
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner it should be
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Agni, performer of excellent works

O Agni, endowed with strength, grant that we may be in your protection every day. O Agni, performer of excellent works, grant that we may be intent on sacrificial rites for the gain of wealth, and as the result of it may rejoice together with cattle and with heroic sons.

Possessor of strength, day by day so (provide), that we may enjoy your protection; doer of good deeds, may we (be deserving) of wealth through sacrifice, and may we be happy with cattle, happy with male descendants.

O Agni, we meditate upon you as Manu did (manuṣvat), like Manu. Like Manu we kindle you; that is, we cause you to blaze with kindling-sticks. O Agni, Aṅgiras, of the nature of coals (aṅgāra), worship the gods for the sacrificer who desires the gods, as for Manu, the descendant of Manu.
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—O Aṅgiras, of the nature of coals
- देवयते (*devayate*)—on behalf of the sacrificer who desires the gods as helpers

O Agni, as Manu meditated upon you, so do we also meditate upon you. As Manu caused you to blaze, so do we also. O Agni, of the nature of coals, for the sacrificer who desires to win the favour of the gods, do you also, like Manu, perform the sacrifice addressing the gods.
Like Manu, we mediate, Agni, upon you ; like Manu, we kindled you : worship the gods on behalf of the (worshipper), devout as Manu.

O Agni, you who are well pleased with praises in the human world (among the human race) are kindled, that is, you shine. The ladles, filled with oblations, come to you, reach you, constantly (ānuṣak, without break). O well-born one, O Agni, to whom clarified butter is poured, possessed of food mixed with ghee.
- सुप्रीतः (*suprītaḥ*)—when you are well satisfied with praises and the like
- मानुषे जने (*mānuṣe jane*)—in the assembly of men
- सर्पिरासुते (*sarpirāsute*)—you who have food in the form of ghee, O Agni

O Agni, when you are satisfied with praises and the like, you blaze forth in the assembly of men. O Agni, of excellent birth and having food in the form of ghee, the ladles filled with oblations continually approach you.
When you are pleased, Agni, you shine upon the human race; well-born, feeder upon clarified butter, the ladles are constantly uplifted to you.

All the gods, being pleased together (sajoṣasaḥ), have made you their messenger (dūta). For this reason, O Kavi, far-seeing one, the sacrificers, serving you who are shining (deva), at the sacrifices praise you; that is, they beseech you in order to summon the gods.

O wise Agni, all the gods, who have equal affection for you, have chosen you as their messenger. Therefore the sacrificers, worshipping at the sacrifices, praise you, who are divine in nature and shining.
All the consenting divinities have made you their messenger ; therefore the pious worship you who are divine, wise Agni, at sacrifices.

The mortal, the man, is fit to praise the shining Agni, the foremost, for the sake of the worship of the gods (devayajyā), that is, in order to sacrifice to the gods. O bright (śukra) Agni, possessed of splendour, kindled, grown strong with oblations, blaze. Of Sasa, the seer, who is truthful (ṛta), take your seat in the place of origin (yoni), the cause of origin, the means of reaching heaven, the place of sacrifice; sit there in the form of a deity. ⟨NOTE:44⟩ The repetition (of आसदः (*āsadaḥ*)) is to show great respect.
notes: ಸಸಸ್ಯ ಋಷೇರ್ಮನು ಯೋನಿಂ: ಮನು after ಋಷೇಃ is unclear in the bhāṣya

en: - अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—and of the nature of Agni
- देवयज्यया (*devayajyayā*)—in order to perform the sacrifice addressed to the gods
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—when you are kindled with oblations and the like

- Or else: ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice; योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the place of origin; आसदः (*āsadaḥ*)—be seated; ससस्य (*sasasya*)—of the seer named Sasa; योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the place of sacrifice; आसदः (*āsadaḥ*)—be seated.

O Agni, a man praises you, who are shining and divine in nature, in order to perform the sacrifice addressed to the gods. O Agni, endowed with radiance, kindled with oblations and the like, shine. Be seated in the place of sacrifice, true in nature, of the seer named Sasa, the follower of truth.
Man praises you, divine Agni, to convey his offerings to the Gods; bright Agni, blaze when kindled : take your seat in the chamber (of sacrifice): in the chamber of the sincere Sasa.

O Viśvasāman: this is an address to the seer. Like Atri, sing forth (prārca, pragāya) to Agni, whose radiance purifies (pāvakaśociṣe). That Agni who is to be praised (īḍya) at the sacrifices by all sacrificers, the hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, is the most praiseworthy among the people (viś).
- होता (*hotā*)—is of the nature of the hotṛ
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—recite an excellent praise

O seer named Viśvasāman, as the seer Atri recited, recite an excellent praise addressed to Agni, who is most worthy of worship at the sacrifices, is of the nature of the hotṛ, is the most praiseworthy among all people, and has a purifying radiance.
Sing, Vishwasaman, like Atri, (a hymn) to the dispencer of purifying light : (to him) who is to be praised at sacrifices, the invoker of the gods, the most adorable by man.

O sacrificers, establish (ni dadhāta) Agni Jātavedas, the one endowed with knowledge or possessor of wealth that has arisen, the shining one, the priest (ṛtvij), the sacrificer at the proper time. Moreover, may the sacrifice, that is, the oblation given by us as the means of sacrifice, which is the dearest (devavyacastama) to the gods, go forth to that Agni today, on this day, continuously (ānuṣak).
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—(O sacrificers) endowed with the power of knowing everything that has arisen
- ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*)—in the form of the chief priest of the sacrifice
- नि दधात (*ni dadhāta*)—establish (on the sacrificial ground)
- देवव्यचस्तमः (*devavyacastamaḥ*)—most dear to all the gods
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—the oblation offered in the sacrifice

O sacrificers, establish on the sacrificial ground Agni, who has the power of knowing everything that has arisen, who is shining and is in the form of the chief priest of the sacrifice. May the oblation offered in the sacrifice, most dear to all the gods, continuously join Agni in this sacrifice.
Cherish the divine Agni, by whom all that exists is known, the priest (of the rite): may the sacrifice most suitable for the gods duly this day proceed to them.

O Agni, you who are cikitvin-manas, one whose mind is knowing. We mortals, men, approaching you, the god, for protection, praise you for the satisfaction of your favour (avas), you who are to be shared in (varenya), worthy of being resorted to.
- चिकित्सत्मनसं (*cikitsatmanasaṃ*)—possessed of mental power that knows everything

O Agni, we men, who approach you for protection, you who are possessed of a mental power that knows everything and are divine in nature, praise you for the satisfaction of you who are worthy of worship and honoured.
Men have recourse to you divine Agni, who are of intelligent mind, for security : we praise you who are most excellent, seeking your protection.

O Agni, O Sahasya, son of strength (sahas), know this our service, this speech, this praise. O Suśipra, the one whose jaws or nostrils (śipra) are handsome; the word is an address to him. O Suśipra, of fine jaws, O Dampati, lord of the house, the sons of Atri make you grow with their stomas, praises; the sons of Atri adorn you with their words.
- सहस्य (*sahasya*)—O you, the son of strength
- इदं वचः (*idaṃ vacaḥ*)—this praise, which is worthy of worship
- दंपते (*daṃpate*)—and who are the lord of the house
- वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)—make you grow strong and increase

O Agni, son of strength, know the nature of this praise of ours, which belongs to this sacrifice and is worthy of worship. The sons of Atri make you, who have excellent cheeks and are the lord of the house, grow strong with hymns. The same sons of Atri adorn you with words of praise. (They praise you.)

Agni, son of strength recognize the words of this our (laudation): handsome-chinned, lord of the dwelling, the sons of Atri exalt you, such (as you are), by their praises : they embellish you by their hymns.

O Agni, bring (ā bhara) to me, Dyumna, a son (rayi) who overcomes his foes with surpassing strength, as wealth. Here the genitive stands in the sense of the dative. He now explains this: the son who, endowed with praise (āsā, by the mouth), subdues in battles all the men, the enemies, who come against him.
- आसा (*āsā*)—having a mouth (filled with your praise)
- अभि (*abhi*)—who has come to meet him
O Agni, provide to me, named Dyumna, such a son of excellent strength as, with a mouth that praises you alone in battles, has the power to slay all the enemies who face him.
Bestow, Agni, upon Dyumna a son, overcoming foes by his prowess ; one who may with glory subdue all men in battle.
O Agni, O mighty one, bring (ā bhara) a son who overcomes armies (pṛtanā), the enemy hosts. For you are true, in truth wonderful, great, the giver of food (vāja) accompanied by cattle.
- पृतनासहं (*pṛtanāsahaṃ*)—having the strength to overcome the enemy army
O Agni, endowed with strength, provide me with a son who has the strength to overcome the enemy army. You are true in nature, great in form, and the giver of food accompanied by cattle.
Mighty Agni, grant us a son able to encounter hosts ; for you are true and wonderful, and the giver of food with cattle.
O Agni, all the people, the priests (ṛtvij), being pleased together (sajoṣasaḥ), with the sacred grass (barhis) cut, at the sacrificial houses (sadman), you, the hotṛ, the summoner of the gods…
…you, who are dear (priya), pleasing to all, they ask for (vyanti) much (puru) choice wealth.
- व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who have prepared the cut darbha grass as seats
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—of the nature of the hotṛ

O Agni, all the priests, who have equal devotion and affection, and who have cut the darbha grass and arranged excellent seats, ask you, who are of the nature of the hotṛ and dear to all, in the sacrificial houses for abundant and desired wealth.
All men concurring in satisfaction, bearing the clipt sacred grass, solicit you, as the kind invoker of the gods, to the chambers (of sacrifice) for infinite wealth.

O Agni, may that well-known sage Viśvacarṣaṇi hold (dadhe) strength (sahas) that destroys enemies. ⟨NOTE:46⟩ O bright (śukra) Agni, possessed of splendour, shine in our houses (kṣaya) in such a way that they are rich in wealth (revat). O Pāvaka, Agni, purifier of sins, shine with brilliance and with glory (dyumat).
notes: ವಿಶ್ವಚರ್ಷಣಿರ್ಯಷಿಃ and ಹಿ ಸ್ಮೃತಿ ಪೂರಣೌ in the bhāṣya are damaged; read here as ಋಷಿಃ and the particles hi, sma as expletives

en: - एषु क्षयेषु (*eṣu kṣayeṣu*)—in these sacrificial houses
- रेवत् (*revat*)—so that there is abundance of wealth

O Agni, may the seer well known by the name Viśvacarṣaṇi obtain strength that destroys enemies. You, endowed with radiance, shine in these our sacrificial houses so that wealth may abound. O Agni, the purifier, spread your rays everywhere and blaze so as to be most brilliant.
May the (sage) on whom all men rely possess foe-subduing strength : radiant Agni, so shine in our habitations that they may abound in riches : shine, purifying Agni, dispensing light.

O Agni, who are to be chosen (*varūthya*), that is, to be resorted to; or else, enclosed by encircling fences (*varūthaiḥ*), be nearest to us. Be also our protector and the giver of welfare. Agni is the dweller (*vasu*), the foremost of all; being rich in food (*vasuśravas*), turn towards us and reach us; give us most brilliant wealth, wealth in the form of cattle and the like; bestow it on us.
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the leader of all, as it were
- वसुश्रवाः (*vasuśravāḥ*)—you who are the distributor of food

O worshipful Agni, be exceedingly near to us, our protector and the bringer of welfare. You, who are the giver of dwellings, the leader of all, as it were, and the distributor of food, be turned towards us and pervade us. Give us most radiant wealth.
Agni, you are to be adored, be ever nigh to us, our protector and benefactor : you, who are the giver of dwellings and dispenser of food, be present with us : bestow upon us most brilliant wealth.

O Agni, that you (*sa*) understand us (*bodhi*, "know us"); hear (*śrudhi*) our invocation. Protect (*uruṣya*) us from all men who wish us harm (*aghāyataḥ*, "who desire evil"). O most radiant (*śociṣṭha*), blazing with your own splendours (*dīdivaḥ*), Agni: to you, for the sake of happiness (*sumna*; "*sumna*" is a name of happiness) and for the sake of our friends (*sakhibhyaḥ*), that is, our sons who share one name with us, we now (*nūnam*) make our petition (*īmahe*, "we beg").
- दीदिवः (*dīdivaḥ*)—O Agni, who shine with those radiances
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—for the sake of our dear sons
notes: ಸಮಸ್ತಾತ್ in the gloss; the Saṃhitā block and the bhāṣya have ಸಮಸ್ಮಾತ್

en: O Agni, renowned as you are, understand our devotion. Hear our invocation made with praise. Protect us from all enemies who wish us harm. O Agni, of exceeding radiance, shining with those radiances, we now praise you for happiness and for the sake of our dear sons.
Understand us, Agni; hear our invocation; defend us from all malevolent (people) : most bright and resplendent Agni, we earnestly solicit you for the happiness (of ourselves) and our friends.

O Vasūyus (you who desire wealth), sing forth (*gāsi*, "praise") to the divine Agni for protection. Agni, the dweller (*vasu*), who makes himself dwell in the houses of the sacrificers for the agnihotra, may he (*sa*) grant (*rāsat*) us our desires. He is the son (*putra*) of the seers (*ṛṣūṇām*): because he is produced by the seers by churning, he is called "son" figuratively. Truthful (*ṛtāvā*), that is, possessed of truth, or possessed of water, that Agni may carry us across (*parṣati*) our enemies (*dviṣaḥ*), that is, ferry us over them.
- वसुः (*vasuḥ*)—dwelling in the house of the sacrifice
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—in the form of a son (born by churning and the like)
notes: the gloss line "ಋತಾನಾಸತ್ಯವಂತನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು" has the word ಋತಾ run together with ನಾ; read as "truthful"; the Pada block has ಋತ್ಯವಾ for ಋತಾವಾ

en: O seers named Vasūyu, sing the praise of Agni, divine in nature, in a commendable manner, for protection. May that Agni, who dwells in the house of the sacrifice, grant us our desires. May Agni, who, being produced by churning and the like, is as a son to the seers, and who is truthful, destroy our enemies.
Celebrate the divine Agni for his protection : may he who presides over dwellings grant (our desires) : may the son of the Rishis, the observers of truth, save us from those who hate us.

The ancient (*pūrve cit*) great seers kindled Agni, the invoker (*hotāra*) of the gods, whose tongue gives delight (*mandrajihva*): his tongue delights the gods by the offering of oblations; or else, "of delighting tongue". So Yāska says: मंद्रजिह्वं मंदनजिह्वं मोदनजिह्वमिति वा (*maṃdrajihvaṃ maṃdanajihvaṃ modanajihvamiti vā*), Ni. 6-23. He is joined with fair radiances (*sudītibhiḥ*) and has light as his wealth (*vibhāvasu*). The gods too (*devāsaś cit*) kindled that Agni (*īdhire*, "kindled"); that Agni is indeed true (*satya*): he is true to his promise. The word *it* is a filler.
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the invoker for the whole sacrifice
- मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*)—he whose flame, in the form of a tongue, gives delight
- सुदीतिभिः (*sudītibhiḥ*)—he who is joined with commendable brilliance
- सत्य (*satya*)—is of the nature of truth

Agni is the invoker for the whole sacrifice; he has a delighting flame in the form of a tongue; he is joined with commendable brilliance; he has radiance as his wealth. The ancient seers and the gods too kindled him; that Agni is truly of the nature of truth.
That Agni is true whom the ancients, whom the gods have kindled, as the bright-tongued invoker of the gods, radiant with holy splendours.

O Agni, praised with fair praises (*suvṛktibhiḥ*, "with hymns") and worthy of being chosen (*vareṇya*): you, with our best (*variṣṭhayā*, "most choice") and most excellent, praiseworthy (*śreṣṭhayā*) service (*dhītī*, our act of attendance), and with our *sumati*, which here means a śastra, being pleased with the śastra, give (*dīdihi*) us riches (*rāyaḥ*, "wealth").
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—he who is praised with excellent praises
- वरिष्ठया (*variṣṭhayā*)—with what is the very best
- सुमत्या च (*sumatyā ca*)—and with praises in the form of śastras (being gratified)

O Agni, praised with excellent praises and greatly honoured, renowned as you are, be gratified with our very best and praiseworthy acts worthy of worship and with our praises in the form of śastras, and give us riches.
Agni, to be propitiated by praises, (gratified) by our choice and most excellent adoration and hymns, bestow upon us riches.

The Agni who shines (*rājati*) among the gods, that is, appears in the form of a deity in their midst; the Agni who has entered (*āviśan*) among mortals (*marteṣu*), that is, men, in the form of the Āhavanīya and the other fires; the Agni who is the bearer of our oblations (*havyavāhana*), that is, the carrier of the oblations to the deities in our sacrifices: O sacrificers, serve (*saparyata*, "attend upon") that Agni with praises (*dhībhiḥ*).
- राजति (*rājati*)—shines in the form of a deity
- आविशन् (*āviśan*)—has entered in the form of the Āhavanīya and the others
- हव्यवाहनः (*havyavāhanaḥ*)—is the bearer of the oblation (to the gods)

The worshipful Agni shines among the gods in the form of a deity. Agni has entered among men in the form of the Āhavanīya and the other fires. That same Agni is for us the bearer of the oblation to the gods. O sacrificers, worship such a worshipful Agni with praises.
Agni shines amongst the gods: Agni is present amongst mortals : Agni is the bearer of our oblations : glorify Agni with praises.

In the Putrakāmeṣṭi (the offering for the wish for a son), the two Ṛks beginning "Agnis tu viśravastamam" are the yājyā and the anuvākyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt. So it is laid down in the sūtra: अग्निस्तुविश्रवस्तममिति द्वे संयाज्ये (*agnistuviśravastamamiti dve saṃyājye*), Ā. 2-10. Agni, who is of exceeding great fame in food (*viśravastama*, "exceedingly abounding in food"), of many praises (*tuvibrahmāṇa*, "of much hymning"), most excellent (*uttama*), unharmed by enemies (*atūrta*), and *śrāvayatpati*: he makes the lords (*pati*) famous (*śrāvayati*), that is, by his own deeds he makes the fathers known, hence *śrāvayatpati*; ⟨NOTE:49⟩ may Agni give such a son to the sacrificer (*dāśuṣe*) who has given oblations.
notes: ಪತೀನ್ ಪಾಲಯಿತ್ಥನ್ಪಿತ್ಯನಿತಿ ಸ್ವಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪಿತ್ಯಣಾಂ: the machine-read words are damaged; the sense is taken from the Kannada gloss

en: - दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- तुविक्रवस्तमं (*tuvikravastamaṃ*)—endowed with very abundant wealth of food ⟨NOTE:50⟩
- तुविब्रह्माणं (*tuvibrahmāṇaṃ*)—who composes praise in great measure
- श्रवयत्पतिं (*śravayatpatiṃ*)—who by his excellent deeds brings fame to all his fathers, grandfathers and the rest
notes: ತುವಿಕ್ರವಸ್ತಮಂ printed; the Saṃhitā and bhāṣya have ವಿಶ್ರವಸ್ತಮಂ

en: May Agni favour the sacrificer who offers the oblation with a son who is endowed with very abundant wealth of food, who in great measure composes praises of the deities, who is possessed of excellent qualities, who is not harmed by enemies, and who by his excellent deeds brings fame to all his fathers, grandfathers and the rest.
May Agni bestow upon the donor (of the oblation) a son, abounding in food, abounding in devotion, excellent, unharmed, conferring honour upon his progenitors.

In the sacrifice called Putrakāmeṣṭi, this Ṛk "Agnis tu viśravastamam" and the Ṛk after it are to be recited as the yājyā and anuvākyā mantras in the Sviṣṭakṛt homa, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: अग्निस्तु विश्रवस्तममिति द्वे संयाज्ये (*agnistu viśravastamamiti dve saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-10).

The son who in battle (*yudhā*), with his men (*nṛbhiḥ*, his retinue), overcomes (*sasāha*) his enemies, the protector of the good (*satpati*): Agni gives such a son; may he give him to us. Further, Agni (may give) a horse that is *raghuṣyada*: *raghu* is light, *syada* is speed, he whose speed is light; a conqueror (*jetāra*) of enemies, unconquered (*aparājita*) by enemies; *atya* is the horse (*atta*), because it goes (*atati*) constantly. May he give that.
- ससाह (*sasāha*)—defeats the enemies, such a one
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—and the protector of the good, such a son
- ददाति (*dadāti*)—may he favour us with and give

May Agni favour us with a son who defeats enemies in battles together with his followers and who is the protector of the good. May that same Agni give a horse that is swift-going, conquering enemies, and unconquered by enemies.
May Agni bestow a son, the protector of the good, who, with his followers, may be victorious in battle : may he bestow a swift-footed steed, conquering, unconquered.

At the Aśvamedha, in the offering to Pūṣan (⟨NOTE:51⟩), the Ṛk "Yad vāhiṣṭham" is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt. So it is laid down in the sūtra: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नय इति संयाज्ये (*yadvāhiṣṭhaṃ tadagnaya iti saṃyājye*), Ā. 10-6. That hymn (*stotra*) which is best at carrying (*vāhiṣṭha*, "most conveying") is made for Agni. Therefore, O Agni, whose wealth is light (*vibhāvaso*; ⟨NOTE:52⟩), give us abundant (*bṛhat*) food or wealth (*arca*, "give"). If it is asked how he can be the giver of food and wealth, he says: because from you
... from you great (*mahiṣī*) wealth (*rayi*) rises up (*udīrate*), and foods (*vājāḥ*) also rise up from you. The word *iva* is a filler.
notes: ಪೌಷ್ಣಾ ಮಿಷ್ಟ printed
ವಿಧಾವಸೋ printed in the bhāṣya

en: - वाहिष्ठं (*vāhiṣṭhaṃ*)—carries our devotion in the highest degree
- विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*)—O Agni, whose wealth is radiance

That hymn which carries our devotion in the highest degree is offered to Agni. O Agni, whose wealth is radiance, give us abundant wealth, for abundant wealth and foods arise from you alone and spread forth.
That (praise) which best conveys (our veneration, is due) to Agni : affluent in splendour, grant us, (Agn'), great (wealth), for from you vast riches and ample food proceed.

In the Pauṣṭa offering (⟨NOTE:53⟩) of the Aśvamedha sacrifice, this Ṛk "Yad vāhiṣṭham" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the smitakṛt homa ⟨NOTE:54⟩, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नय इति संयाज्ये (*yadvāhiṣṭhaṃ tadagnaya iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 10-6).
notes: ಪೌಷ್ಟೇಷ್ಟಿ printed; the bhāṣya has ಪೌಷ್ಣಾ ಮಿಷ್ಟ
ಸ್ಮಿತಕೃದ್ಧೋಮ printed; the bhāṣya has ಸ್ವಿಷ್ಟಕೃತ್

en: O Agni, your rays (*arcayaḥ*) are radiant (*dyumantaḥ*), full of light. You, who are great (*bṛhat*), are praised (*ucyate*) like the pressing stone (*grāveva*, the stone for pressing). And of you, who shine from the sky (*divaḥ*), by your own power (*tmanā*) your sound (*snānaḥ*) rises (*arta*, "goes up") like thunder (*tanyatuḥ*), the rumbling of a cloud.
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—you, who are of great nature
- ग्रावेव (*grāveva*)—like the stone that presses Soma
- तन्यतुः यथा (*tanyatuḥ yathā*)—like the rumbling of a cloud

O Agni, your rays are full of radiance. You, who are of great nature, are praised like the stone that presses Soma. And your sound, shining by your own greatness, arises and spreads like the rumbling of a cloud.
Brilliant, Agni, are your rays : mighty are you termed, like the stone (that bruises the Soma), and your voice spontaneously spreads through the sky like thunder.

We, the Vasūyus (*vasūyavaḥ*, those who desire wealth), have thus praised (*vavandima*, "we praise") in the manner stated Agni, who is *sahasāna*, that is, who acts like our own strength. May that Agni, the doer of fair works (*sukratu*), carry us over (*parṣat*, "take us across") all (*viśvāḥ*) our enemies (*dviṣaḥ*). How? As with a boat (*nāvā*), a means, one crosses a river.
- वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)—we, who desire wealth (the seers named Vasūyu)
- सहसानं (*sahasānaṃ*)—who accomplishes works endowed with strength
- नाना इव (*nānā iva*)—as one easily crosses a river with a boat ⟨NOTE:55⟩
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he carry across
notes: ತ್ರಿವೃಷ್ಟಸ್ಯ in the bhāṣya, but ತ್ರಿವೃಷ್ಣ in the Kannada Anuvāda

en: We, who are named Vasūyu and desire wealth, praise Agni, who can accomplish works endowed with strength. As one easily crosses a river with a boat, may Agni, the doer of excellent works, carry us across all enemies and protect us.
Thus we, Vasuyus, glorify the vigorous Agni : may he, the performer of great deeds, enable us to pass over our enemies as (we cross a river) with a boat.

O purifier (*pāvaka*), O shining (*deva*) Agni, with your own radiance (*rociṣā*) and with your tongue (*jihvayā*) that delights the gods (*mandrayā*), bring (*vakṣi*) the gods for the sacrifice, and sacrifice (*yakṣi*) also. ⟨NOTE:57⟩
notes: ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ಸುತೋ printed in the bhāṣya; ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಸ್ತುತಃ expected

en: - जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—and in the form of tongues
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring to the sacrifice
- यक्षि च (*yakṣi ca*)—and sacrifice to them
O Agni, purifier and of divine nature, with flames that are radiant, delighting and in the form of tongues, bring the gods to the sacrifice. Sacrifice to them.
Divine purifier, Agni, with your radiant and pleasing tongue, bring hither and worship the gods.

O *dhṛtasnu*, impeller of ghee (*dhṛta*); or else, born of ghee. O *citrabhānu*: *citrā* means of many kinds, *bhānu* means rays; he who has these is Citrabhānu; this is the address to him. You who see everything (*svardṛśam*), we beg (*īmahe*, "we ask") you; therefore bring the gods for the eating of the oblations (*vītaye*).
- धृतस्नो (*dhṛtasno*)—he who is kindled by ghee
- चित्रभानो (*citrabhāno*)—O Agni, who has rays of many kinds
notes: ತ್ವಾಶಿರಃ printed in the bhāṣya; Saṃhitā has ತ್ರ್ಯಾಶಿರಃ

en: O Agni, kindled by ghee and having rays of many kinds, we pray to you, who can see everything and are renowned. Bring the gods to eat the oblation.
Feeder upon butter, bright and variegated radiance we solicit you, the beholder of heaven, to bring the Gods hither to (partake of) the (sacrificial) food

O seer (*kave*), O Agni of far-reaching sight, you whose sacrifice is desired (*vītihotra*), radiant (*dyumantam*) and great (*bṛhantam*): we kindle you (*samidhīmahi*), we make you blaze up, with fuel at the sacrifice (*adhvare*).

notes: ವಿಶ್ವವಾರಾ ಎಂಬ ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯು ದೇವತೆಯು; the bhāṣya calls her the ṛṣi
ಛಂದಃ ೧-೩. ತ್ರಿಷ್ಟುಪ್ and ೨. ಜಗತೀ overlap as printed

en: O Agni, of far-reaching wisdom, whose food is the oblation, endowed with radiance and of great nature, we make you blaze up at the sacrifice.
We kindle you at the sacrifice, wise Agni, whose food is the oblation , who are brilliant and vast.

notes: ಸೌಮಿ printed in the bhāṣya; ಸ್ತೌಮಿ?

en: O Agni, come (*ā gahi*) together with all (*viśvebhiḥ*) the gods, to the sacrificer who gives the oblations (*havyadātaye*), for his sake; come to the sacrifice. For we choose (*vṛṇīmahe*, "we pray to") you, the invoker (*hotāra*) of the gods.
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious to come
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who are the invoker of the gods
O Agni, we pray to you, the invoker of the gods, saying: be gracious to come, together with all the gods, to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.
Come, Agni, with all the gods, to the donor (of the oblation) : we have recourse to you as their invoker.

O Agni, bring (*ā vaha*, "cause to reach") fair strength (*suvīryam*) to the sacrificer (*yajamānāya*) who presses the Soma (*sunvate*). Further, sit down (*ā satsi*, "sit") together with the gods on the sacrificial grass (*barhiṣi*), that is, at the sacrifice.
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—cause to be obtained
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seats of darbha grass
notes: ತ್ರ್ಯಯಮಾ in the bhāṣya, ತ್ರ್ಯರ್ಯಮಾ in the Anuvāda; the incipit is printed with a misprint?

en: O Agni, cause the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice to obtain excellent strength. Come with the gods and sit down on the seats of darbha grass.
To the institutor of the rite, pouring out the libation, bring excellent vigour ; sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass.

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni as "victor of a thousand" (the winner of a thousand), kindled with oblations and praiseworthy. As the messenger of the gods, he says, Agni nourishes our *dharmāṇi*, that is, our rites such as the sacrifice; *puṣyasi* means "you cause to thrive".
- सहस्रजित् (*sahasrajit*)—one who has won victory in thousands of situations
O Agni, who have won victory in thousands of situations, kindled with oblations and worthy of praise, you, as messenger of the gods, cause our sacrificial and other good rites to thrive.
Victor over thousands, you favour, when kindled, our holy rites, the honoured messenger of the gods.

Sāyaṇa addresses the sacrificers: "Establish Agni." He is *Jātavedas*, because he knows all beings that are born; the bearer of the *hotra*, that is, the carrier of the sacrifice; the youngest; the god, that is, the shining one; the *ṛtvij*, the one who sacrifices in the proper season. *Nidadhāta* means "establish".
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—him who knows all beings that have come into being
- होत्रवाहं (*hotravāhaṃ*)—who carries the oblations (to the gods)
- ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*)—who is the chief priest of the sacrifice

O sacrificers, establish and worship Agni, who knows all beings that have come into being, who carries the oblations to the gods, who is very youthful and shining, and who is the chief priest of the sacrifice.
Reverence Angi, by whom all that is, is known, the bearer of oblations the youngest of the gods, the divine, the ministrant priest.

Today, on this day, let the sacrifice, which is the means of sacrifice, namely the oblation, most pervaded by the shining praisers of the gods, go forth uninterrupted to the gods. O priests, spread the sacred grass for Agni's seat.
- देवव्यचस्तमः (*devavyacastamaḥ*)—offered with the utmost devotion by the shining praisers ⟨NOTE:63⟩
- प्र एतु (*pra etu*)—let it reach the gods (O priests)
notes: ಸೂಕ್ತ—೨೨ printed; the sūkta is ೨೯

en: In this sacrifice, let the oblation offered with the utmost devotion by the shining praisers duly reach the gods. O priests, spread the seat of darbha grass for Agni.
May the sacrifice most solemnly offered by the devout duly proceed to-day (to the gods) : spread the sacred grass for their seat.
The Maruts are the troops of Maruts; the Aśvins are the physicians of the gods; Mitra is the sun; and Varuṇa. All these gods, together with their entire retinue, are to sit down on this sacred grass.
- सर्वया विशा (*sarvayā viśā*)—with all the attendant gods belonging to them
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—upon these seats of darbha grass
May the Maruts, who are of divine nature, the Aśvin gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, together with all the attendant gods belonging to them, come and sit down upon these seats of darbha grass.
May the Maruts, the Ashwins, Mitra, Varuna, the gods, with all their attendants, sit down upon this grass.

Atri described the gift of the royal seers in the presence of Agni by means of this sūkta. O Vaiśvānara, leader of all men, Agni, you are *satpati*, the protector of the good and the righteous; *cetiṣṭha*, the most knowing; *asura*, the powerful; and *maghonaḥ*, one possessing wealth. Tryaruṇa, the royal seer of that name, son of Trivṛṣṇa, gave (*mamahe*) to me the two oxen *anasvantā* (that is, joined with a cart, *anas*) together with ten thousands of cattle, gold and the like. That royal seer is known (*ciketa*) to all people by this gift. ⟨NOTE:65⟩
notes: ತ್ರೀ ತ್ರೀಣ್ಯರ್ಯಮಾರ್ಯಮಾಣಿ: construction of the words uncertain

en: - दशभिः सहस्रैः (*daśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ*)—those joined with ten thousand pieces of gold
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—he has become known and famous to all

O Agni, in the form of Vaiśvānara, protector of the good, best among the discerning, endowed with strength and wealth: the royal seer named Tryaruṇa, son of Trivṛṣṇa, gave me a pair of cattle (two oxen) joined with a cart and with ten thousand pieces of gold. For that very reason he has become known and famous to all.

Agni, who are the protector of the good, most wise, powerful, and opulent; Tryaruna, the son of Trivrishna, has become renowned, Vaishwanara, in that he has bestowed upon me a pair of cattle with a waggon, and with ten thousands of treasure.

Sāyaṇa explains that Tryaruṇa gives me hundreds of pieces of gold, twenty of cattle (*gonām* means *gavām*), and two horses (*harī*), which are yoked to a chariot and bear the yoke well (*sudhurā*). He then addresses Agni Vaiśvānara, well praised by us (*suṣṭuta*) ⟨NOTE:66⟩ and growing by the oblations (*vavṛdhāna*): bestow (*yaccha*, that is, *prayaccha*) happiness (*śarma*) on that Tryaruṇa.
notes: ಧೇನುಗಳಿರುವ ಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಿಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ: Sāyaṇa has ಗಾ = ಧೇನೂರ್ವೃಷ್ಟಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾನ್ಯುದಕಾನಿ, ಯಜಮಾನಂ ಗಾ ಲಂಭಯತಿ

en: - वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*)—who are of the form of Vaiśvānara
- ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*)—and made to grow by oblations, you who are so
- शता च (*śatā ca*)—and a hundred pieces of gold
- सुधरा (*sudharā*)—those fit to bear a load
- त्रैरुणाय (*trairuṇāya*)—to the royal seer named Tryaruṇa

O Agni, who are of the form of Vaiśvānara, you who are well praised by us and made to grow by oblations: bring happiness to the royal seer named Tryaruṇa, who has given me a hundred pieces of gold, twenty cows, and two horses fit to bear a load and yoked to a chariot.
Agni, Vaishwanara, you are deservedly praised and exalted ( by us ); bestow happiness upon Tryaruna, who gives me hundreds (of Suvarnas), twenty cattle, and a pair of burden-bearing horses.

Tryaruṇa, hearing the many praises (*girah*) of me, who have many children (*tuvijāta*), is pleased; with a concentrated mind (*yuktena*, that is, *abhiyuktena*) he says to me again and again, "Take this, take this." In the same way, O Agni, who are exceedingly worthy of praise (*naviṣṭha*), Trasadasyu too, desiring a praise (*sumati*) that is newest (*navama*, that is, *navatama*) for you, has begged me, "Take this, take this."
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—(praising you), by the praises (being pleased)
- युक्तेन (*yuktena*)—with a mind full of devotion
- नविष्ठाय (*naviṣṭhāya*)—who are worthy of exceeding praise
- त्रसदस्युः (*trasadasyuḥ*)—Trasadasyu too (has begged me to accept these gifts)

O Agni, Tryaruṇa was gratified by the excellent praises composed and recited with you in view, so that your favour might be gained for Tryaruṇa; and he gave me, who have many sons, the most excellent gifts with devotion. In the same way Trasadasyu too, desiring that I compose an excellent praise with you in view for the gaining of your favour for himself, has begged me to accept excellent gifts.
As Tryaruna, pleased by the eulogies of me who have many children, presses with earnest (mind, gifts upon me), so does Trasadasvu. desirous, Agni, of your valued favour through your exceeding praise.

The petitioner who begs says to Aśvamedha, the royal seer, who is *sūri*, that is, the impeller and giver of wealth, "Give to me" (*pravocati*); that is, he begs wealth from Aśvamedha. Aśvamedha gives wealth (*sani*) to that petitioner who comes (*yate*) to him, that is, goes to his presence, with a *ṛc*, a praise of Agni. O Agni, give to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice (*ṛtāyate*), insight (*medhā*), that is, wisdom concerning the sacrifice.
- सूरये (*sūraye*)—who is a giver of wealth
- अश्वमेधाय (*aśvamedhāya*)—to the royal seer named Aśvamedha
- ऋचा (*ṛcā*)—together with a praise (that extols Agni)
- यते (*yate*)—to him who goes to him
- ऋतायते (*ṛtāyate*)—to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice

O Agni, the petitioner who approaches the royal seer named Aśvamedha, the giver of wealth, and begs wealth of him together with a praise that wins your favour and extols you, to such a man he gives wealth, in the faith that good will come to him from that praise. Give good understanding to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice.

When Ashwamedha gives to him who solicits of him as a benefactor, saying (bestow wealth) upon me, and comes (to him) with a verse (in your praise), do you, Agni, grant intelligence to (the Raja) who wishes to offer sacrifice (to you).

The hundred bulls (*ukṣaṇaḥ*, that is, oxen) given by Aśvamedha as gifts, which fulfil desires (*paruṣāḥ*), delight me exceedingly. O Agni, may those bulls, which have the three mixtures (*āśir*) of curds, barley meal and milk as the means of cooking ⟨NOTE:67⟩, be, like Soma, for your gratification.
notes: ಸಂವಿವ್ಯಾನಶ್ಚಿತ್: Kannada gloss ದೃಢಸಂಕಲ್ಪದಿಂದ ಸಂಚರಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವಾಗಲೇ differs from Sāyaṇa's ಸಂವೃಣ್ವಾನಃ ಸಂಗಚ್ಛಮಾನೋ ವೇಂದ್ರಃ

en: - त्रशिरः (*traśiraḥ*)—of the form of the three mixtures, curds and the rest
- उद्धर्षयंति (*uddharṣayaṃti*)—gratify (may they also serve for your gratification)

O Agni, just as the hundred bulls given by this same Aśvamedha, which fulfil desires, gratify me like Soma juices of the three mixtures of curds and the rest, so may the oblations given by him bring gratification to you.
Whose hundred robust oxen yield me delight, as the triple-mixed Soma, the offering of Ashwamedha (gratifies you).

O Indra and Agni, *śatadānni* means in him who gives to petitioners a hundred, that is, immeasurable, wealth (*śatadāvā*). In that Aśvamedha, the royal seer, establish (*dhārayatam*, that is, *nidhārayatam*) *kṣatra*, that is, wealth, endowed with good heroism (*suvīrya*), great and free from old age (*ajara*). How? As the sun in the sky (*divi*, that is, in the atmosphere).
- अश्वमेधे (*aśvamedhe*)—in the royal seer named Aśvamedha
- सूर‍्यं इव (*sūryaṃ iva*)—shining like the sun

O Indra and Agni, fill the royal seer named Aśvamedha, who gives wealth without measure, with wealth that is endowed with excellent strength, abundant, shining like the sun in the atmosphere, and everlasting.
Indra and Agni, bestow upon the munificent Ashwamedha infinite wealth with excellent posterity, undecaying as the sun in heaven.

Agni, fully kindled, spreads (*aśret*, that is, *śrayati*) his lustre in the shining atmosphere; likewise, facing the dawn, he shines widely (*urviyā*) and brilliantly. Viśvavārā, so named because she keeps off every sinful enemy, faces east (*prācī*, that is, *prāṅmukhī*); she praises the gods, Indra and the others, with praises (*namobhiḥ*), and, provided with oblations such as the *puroḍāśa* and with the ghee-ladle (*dhṛtācī*), goes towards Agni who is thus.
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and the rest

Agni, fully kindled, spreads his lustre in the shining atmosphere. Facing the dawn, he shines widely. Praising Indra and the other gods with praises, and holding the ladle furnished with oblations, the seer named Viśvavārā goes towards Agni, facing him.

Agni, when kindled, spreads lustre through the firmament, and shines in widely the presence of the dawn: Vishwavara, facing the east, glorifying the gods with praises, and bearing the ladle with the oblation, proceeds (to the sacred fire).

O Agni, being well kindled, you rule (*rājasi*, that is, *īśiṣe*) over *amṛta*, that is, water. You also attend (*sacase*, that is, *sevase*) the sacrificer who makes oblations such as the *puroḍāśa*, for his welfare (*svastaye*), that is, for his freedom from destruction. Moreover, the sacrificer to whom you come (*invasi*, that is, *gacchasi*) holds all wealth (*dravinam*) of the kind that consists of cattle and the like. And, O Agni, he sets before you, as the guest that you are, the oblation fitting for your hospitality (*ātithya*).
- हविष्कृण्वंतं (*haviṣkṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- आतिथ्यं (*ātithyaṃ*)—the oblation fit for your worship as guest
- पुर इत् (*pura it*)—right in front of you

O Agni, when you are kindled you are lord of all the water. You attend the sacrificer who makes the oblation, so that welfare may come to him. The sacrificer whom you favour and attend obtains all wealth. O Agni, he places the oblation fit for your worship as guest right in front of you.

When about to be kindled, Agni, you rule over ambrosial (water) : you are present with the offerer of the oblation for his welfare: he to whom you repair acquires universal wealth ; he places before you, Agni, the dues of hospitality.

In the Pavitreṣṭi, the verse beginning *agne śardha* is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. It is laid down in the sūtra: जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2. 12). In the Sākamedha offerings too, at the offering "to the sporting Maruts, a *puroḍāśa* on seven potsherds", the Sviṣṭakṛt yājyā is this same verse, and the sūtra says so: जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2. 18).

O Agni, for our great (*mahate*, that is, abundant) good fortune (*saubhaga*, that is, good wealth), *śardha*: overcome the enemies. Let your *dyumnāni*, that is, riches or splendours, be excellent. Moreover, O Agni, make *jāspatya* (*jā* is wife, and the husband too; the pair is *jāyāpatī*) well-regulated, that is, closely joined to one another; make it good. And overcome (*abhi tiṣṭha*, that is, attack) the energies of the rivals who wish for themselves an enemy.
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)—so that blessed wealth may come to us
- जास्पत्यं (*jāspatyaṃ*)—the good rites that point to the mutual relation of husband and wife
- सुयमं (*suyamaṃ*)—joined to one another, as if under one rule
- शत्रूयतां (*śatrūyatāṃ*)—of those who wish us harm
- अभि तिष्ठ (*abhi tiṣṭha*)—check and stand against

O Agni, check our enemies, so that blessed wealth may come to us in abundance. Let your riches be excellent. Perfect the good rites that point to the mutual relation of husband and wife, joined to one another as if under one rule. Check and overcome the energies of those who wish us harm.
Repress, Agni, (our foes to ensure our) exceeding prosperity : may your riches ever be excellent : preserve in concord the relation of man and wife, and overpower the energies of the hostile.

In the Pavitreṣṭi, this verse beginning अग्ने शर्ध (*agne śardha*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the Sviṣṭakṛt offering; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-12). Again, in the Sākamedha sacrifices, when the offering is made with the words मरुद्भ्यः क्रीडिभ्यः पुरोडाशं सप्तकपालं (*marudbhyaḥ krīḍibhyaḥ puroḍāśaṃ saptakapālaṃ*), this verse is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the Sviṣṭakṛt offering; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-18).

O Agni, I, the sacrificer, praise (*stauti*) ⟨NOTE:70⟩ the glory (*śrī*), that is, the brightness, that belongs to you, who are kindled, that is, grown strong, of excellent splendour (*pramahas*). You are the showerer (*vṛṣabha*) of desires and are wealthy (*dyumnavān*). In the sacrifices (*adhvareṣu*) you are well kindled.
notes: ಸ್ವಶ್ವಪುತ್ರೇಣ ಸೂರ್ಯೇಣ: reading doubtful

en: - प्र महसः (*pra mahasaḥ*)—and who have most excellent splendour
- सं इध्यसे (*saṃ idhyase*)—you are well kindled
O Agni, I bow to the splendour of you, who are fully kindled and have most excellent splendour. You, the showerer of desires, are wealthy with brightness. In the sacrifices you are well kindled.
I praise the glory, Agni, of you when kindled and blazing fiercely : you are the affluent showerer ( of benefits ), you are fitly lighted at sacrifices.

In the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, the two verses beginning *samiddho agna āhuta* are the two Sāmidhenī verses. The sūtra says so: समिद्धो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे (*samiddho agna āhuteti dve*) (Ā. 1-2). O invoked one (*āhuta*), called from every side by the sacrificers; O one of good sacrifice (*svadhvara*); O Agni, being fully kindled, worship (*yakṣi*, that is, *yajasva*) the gods, Indra and the other shining ones. For you are the bearer of the oblations (*havyavāṭ*, that is, *havyānāṃ voḍhā*); for that reason, the connection is, worship the gods.

O Agni, called by the sacrificers and having an excellent sacrifice, you are the bearer of the oblation to the gods. Therefore, as soon as you are kindled by the sacrificer, perform the sacrifice for the gods.
Agni, you are kindled and invoked ; worship the gods at the holy rite, for you are the bearer of the oblation.

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, this Ṛk beginning समिद्दो अग्न आहुत (*samiddo agna āhuta*) and the following Ṛk are to be used as sāmidhenī mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, समिद्दो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे (*samiddo agna āhuteti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 1-2).

O priests, when our sacrifice has begun, make offering to Agni, the bearer of the oblations (हव्यवाहनं (*havyavāhanaṃ*)), from every side; likewise serve him, and choose him. That Agni who is named Havyavāhana is connected with the gods, and that he is to be chosen by the sacrificers, is stated plainly in the Taittirīya (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-8-6): there are three Agnis, Havyavāhana of the gods, Kavyavāhana of the fathers, and Sahaṃrakṣas of the Asuras. These now hope, "he will choose me, me"; by saying "choose Havyavāhana" he chooses the one who belongs to the gods.
- प्रयति (*prayati*)—as soon as it has begun
- वृणीध्वं (*vṛṇīdhvaṃ*)—choose (him as the messenger who brings your oblation to the gods)
O priests, as soon as our sacrifice has begun, offer the oblation to Agni, who carries the oblation. Worship him and choose him as the messenger who brings your oblation to the gods.
Offer worship and adoration to Agni, when the sacrifice is solemnized ; select the bearer of the oblation to the gods.

In the sacrifice that belongs to Manu there are three splendours (त्री त्रीण्यर्यमार्यमाणि (*trī trīṇyaryamāryamāṇi*)) ⟨NOTE:74⟩; and the Maruts uphold three shining lights, divine and in the atmosphere, which have the nature of wind, fire and sun, those splendours. The Maruts, of pure strength, praise you, Indra; you, wise one, are the seer of these Maruts, that is, you become their seer.
notes: ಶುಷ್ಕಮೇತನ್ನಾಮಕಮಸುರಂ in the bhāṣya, but ಶುಷ್ಣಂ in the Ṛk and the gloss

en: - त्री रोचना (*trī rocanā*)—three masses of splendour

In the sacrifice that belongs to Manu and is meant for worshipping the gods, three splendours are established. The Maruts uphold three masses of splendour, which are in the atmosphere and have the forms of fire, wind and sun. O Indra, the Maruts, whose strength is pure, worship you. You are the wise seer of those Maruts.

In the adoration of the gods by Manu there are three effulgences, and they, (the Maruts), uphold three luminaries in heaven : the Maruts of pure energy worship you, for you, Indra, are their intelligent Rishi.

When the Maruts praised Indra, who was delighted, having drunk the pressed Soma, then Indra took up the thunderbolt. Then, when he slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra, he let the mighty waters, which Vṛtra had held back, go forth to flow freely, and freed them from their confinement.
- अनु आर्चन् (*anu ārcan*)—praised with devotion, then (Indra)

As soon as the Maruts praised with devotion Indra, who had drunk the pressed Soma and was satisfied, Indra took the thunderbolt in his hand. As soon as Indra destroyed the Asura Vṛtra, he released the abundant waters to flow freely.
When the Maruts worship Indra, exulting and drinking of the effused libation, he grasps the thunderbolt wherewith he destroys Ahi, and sets the abundant waters free to flow.

O Maruts, mighty ones, you and Indra drink this Soma of mine, well pressed; the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative. The oblation drunk by you, consisting of Soma, makes the sacrificer find cows, that is, the waters that take the form of rain; it makes the sacrificer obtain cows. Moreover Indra, having drunk this Soma, slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra.
- तद्धि हव्यं (*taddhi havyaṃ*)—that same oblation, drunk by you
- मनुषे (*manuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice

O Maruts, mighty in form, you and Indra drink this well-pressed Soma juice. That same oblation, drunk by you, makes known to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice the regions where the cows are. Indra, having drunk this Soma, destroyed Vṛtra. ⟨NOTE:75⟩
notes: ಹಿಂಸಿತವಾಗಿಂದ್ರಿಯಾನ್ in the bhāṣya; the Kannada gloss has ಹಿಂಸಾತ್ಮಕವಾದ ವಾಕ್ಕುಳ್ಳ

en: Or, mighty Maruts, and you also, Indra, drink of this my copiously-effused libation : then the offered libation obtains cattle for the offerer, and Indra, drinking of it, kills Ahi.

Indra, endowed with supreme lordship, after drinking the Soma made the two worlds, heaven and earth, most firm; he made them unmoving. Enveloping (or: coming together, or going; Sāyaṇa derives the word from a root meaning to cover or from one meaning to go) ⟨NOTE:76⟩, he made Vṛtra, who fled like a deer, afraid. Indra, freeing from his covering the Dānava, son of Danu, namely Vṛtra, who was concealing himself, panting to cause fear, advanced against him and slew him.
notes: number of the Ṛk not printed after the Pada; read as 12 from the sequence

en: - आत् (*āt*)—as soon as the Soma was drunk
- संविव्यानश्चित् (*saṃvivyānaścit*)—while moving about with firm resolve
- मृगं (*mṛgaṃ*)—Vṛtra, who was fleeing like a deer
- भियसे कः (*bhiyase kaḥ*)—made him be overcome with fear
- श्वसंतं (*śvasaṃtaṃ*)—who was breathing in a hideous way so that others should fear

The lord Indra, as soon as the Soma was drunk, established heaven and earth exceedingly and firmly. While he was moving about with firm resolve to destroy his enemy, he made Vṛtra, who was fleeing like a deer, be overcome with fear. He prevented Vṛtra, the son of Danu, who tried to cover himself and was breathing hideously so that others should fear, from hiding, confronted him and destroyed him.

Thereupon he fixed firmly heaven and earth, and, resolutely advancing filled (Vritra), like a deer, with terror : stripping off his covering, Indra slew the Danava, endeavouring to hide, and panting with affright.

And further, O Maghavan, O wealthy Indra, through your own deed all the shining gods, Agni and the others, have granted you in due order the drinking of Soma for your sake; from then on Indra became greater than all the gods. So it is heard: स महान्भात्वा देवता अब्रवीदुद्धारं म उद्धरतेत्यादि । (*sa mahānbhātvā devatā abravīduddhāraṃ ma uddharatetyādi |*) (Ai. Brā. 3-21) ⟨NOTE:77⟩. Since you, O Indra, made the tawny horses of Sūrya, which were coming on and were in front, slow of pace for the sake of the seer named Etaśa ⟨NOTE:78⟩, that is, Etaśa had competed with Sūrya, the son of his own horse ⟨NOTE:79⟩; and another passage says the same: प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं सौवश्यॆ सुष्टिमावदिंद्रः (*praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ sauvaśyè suṣṭimāvadiṃdraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-15) ⟨NOTE:80⟩.
notes: ಗವ್ಯಂಚಿತ್ ಗೋಸಂಬಂಧಿ…ನಮಷ್ಯಪೂರ್ವಂ ಸಮೂಹಂ: letters damaged
ಉಪಸಂಹಾರವದ್ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾಣಿ: sense of "upasaṃhāravat" in the explanation of the garment comparison not certain
ಆಗಿ ಎಂಬರ್ಥವುಳ್ಳ ಖನ್ ಧಾತು: "ಆಗಿ" for expected "ಅಗೆ" (to dig)? translated "to make into" as printed
ಇಂದ್ರಪ್ರಾಪ್ತ ರ್ಥ೦: damaged in the print; read as "for the sake of attaining Indra"

en: - एतशे (*etaśe*)—(O Indra) for the help of the seer named Etaśa
- पुरः सतीः (*puraḥ satīḥ*)—that were spreading out in front
- उपराः कः (*uparāḥ kaḥ*)—you made slow of pace
- अनु आदुदुः (*anu āduduḥ*)—approved (to you first, before all others)

O Indra, by that greatness of yours by which, for the help of the seer named Etaśa, you made the horses that belong to Sūrya, which were coming against you and spreading out in front, slow of pace, for that very reason all the gods, pleased by your surpassing deed, approved the drinking of Soma for you, O wealthy Indra, before all others.
Then, for this exploit, all the gods gave you, Maghavan, in succession, the Soma beverage ; whence you have retarded, for the sake of Etasa, the advancing horses of the sun.

When the wealthy Indra split with his thunderbolt at one stroke the nine and ninety strongholds of Śambara (the word अस्य (*asya*) here denotes Śambara; भोगान् (*bhogān*) means cities), then the Maruts, in the place of their common abode, that is, in the battle, praised Indra who stood there, with a hymn in the Triṣṭubh metre. Thus praised, Indra oppressed the shining Asura named Śambara by the mantra employed by the Maruts; the verb बाधत (*bādhata*) means he crushed.
- नव नवतिं च (*nava navatiṃ ca*)—ninety-nine in number

As soon as the wealthy Indra split asunder at one time, with his thunderbolt, the ninety-nine cities of Śambara, the Maruts worshipped Indra, who stood in one place, with praises composed in the Triṣṭubh metre. Indra, pleased by the recitation of these very mantras, harmed the shining Śambara.

Whereupon Maghavan has destroyed with his thunderbolt at once his (Shambara's) ninety and nine cities: the Maruts glorifying Indra in a common dwelling with the Trishtubh hymn, he destroyed the bright (city of the Asura).

Agni, the friend of Indra, quickly cooked three hundred buffaloes, that is, animals, for the friend, this Indra, by a deed that served as the cause. And Indra, endowed with supreme lordship, drank at one time, for the slaying of Vṛtra, the pressed Soma that stood in the three सरांसि (*sarāṃsi*) of Manu, that is, vessels; here the word सरः (*saraḥ*) is said to stand for the vessels named Pūtabhṛt, Ādhavanīya and Droṇakalaśa ⟨NOTE:81⟩.
notes: ಅನೇಃ ಅಗಮಃ: ಅನೇಃ unclear

en: - त्रि शतानि (*tri śatāni*)—three hundred in number
- महिषा (*mahiṣā*)—animals in the form of buffaloes
- त्रि सरांसि (*tri sarāṃsi*)—that is in three Droṇakalaśa vessels
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—that was pressed according to the rule
- वृत्रहत्याय (*vṛtrahatyāya*)—to gain strength to kill Vṛtra

Agni, the friend of Indra, cooked three hundred animals in the form of buffaloes to help his dear friend Indra in his enemy-destroying deed. Indra drank at one time the Soma juice offered by Manu, which was in three Droṇakalaśa vessels and had been pressed according to the rule, and gained the strength needed for the slaying of Vṛtra.

To aid (the undertaking of) his friend, Agni, the friend (of Indra), has quickly consumed three hundred buffaloes ; and Indra, for the destruct- ion of Vritra, has at once quaffed three vessels of Sama, offered by Manu. ⟨NOTE:82⟩
notes: ದೇವರುನಿ: read as ದೇವಶುನಿ "divine bitch" (Saramā)?

en: O Indra, when you ate the flesh of three hundred buffaloes, that is, animals (the verb अघः (*aghaḥ*) stands for eating), and when you, the wealthy one, drank three vessels made of Soma, and when Indra slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra, then all the gods summoned Indra for battle, since he was filled by the drinking of Soma and the like. The example is कारं न (*kāraṃ na*): as a master calls his servant.
- त्री शता (*trī śatā*)—three hundred in number
- कारं न (*kāraṃ na*)—as masters call a servant

O Indra, when you ate the flesh of three hundred animals in the form of buffaloes, when you, the wealthy one, drank all the Soma that filled the three Droṇakalaśa vessels, and when you, Indra, slew Vṛtra, then all the gods summoned Indra, who was filled by the drinking of Soma, for battle, as masters call a servant.

When you have eaten the flesh of the three hundred buffaloes, when you who are Maghavan have drunk the three vessels of Soma, and had slain Ahi. then all the gods summoned Indra, full of food, as if he had been a servant, to the battle.

The Ṛk उशना यत्सहस्यै (*uśanā yatsahasyai*) belongs to the Stoma of Uśanas, and in the Marutvatīya rite it is the opening verse of the sūkta. The sūtra says: उशनसः स्तोमेन गरगीर्णमिवात्मानं मन्यमानो यजेतोशना यत्सहस्यैरयातं । (*uśanasaḥ stomena garagīrṇamivātmānaṃ manyamāno yajetośanā yatsahasyairayātaṃ |*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5): one who thinks of himself as if he had swallowed poison should sacrifice with the Stoma of Uśanas. Sāyaṇa explains: when you, O Indra, and Uśanā Kāvya went to the house of Kutsa with swift horses that overcome their foes, then, O Indra, at that time you went, slaying your enemies, in one and the same chariot with Kutsa and the gods; and you also slew the Asura named Śuṣka ⟨NOTE:83⟩.
notes: ನಿ. ೧೮-೧೮ printed as the reference

en: - सहस्यैः (*sahasyaiḥ*)—that have the power to resist enemies

O Indra, when you and Uśanas, joining together, went to the house of Kutsa with horses that have the power to resist enemies and are swift, you went, destroying your enemies, seated in one chariot with Kutsa and the other gods. And you also harmed the Asura named Śuṣṇa.

When, Indra, you and Ushanas, with vigorous and rapid coursers went to the dwelling of Kutsa, then, destroying his foes, you went in one chariot with Kutsa and the gods, and verily you have slain Sushna.

When the Stoma of Uśanas is recited, this ninth Ṛk of the sūkta, उशना यत्सहस्यैः (*uśanā yatsahasyaiḥ*), is to be recited as the first Ṛk among the Marutvatīya śastra mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उशनसस्तोमेन गरगीर्णमिवात्मानं मन्यमानो यजेतोशना यत्सहस्यैरयातं (*uśanasastomena garagīrṇamivātmānaṃ manyamāno yajetośanā yatsahasyairayātaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5).

O Indra, of the two-wheeled chariot of Sūrya you formerly took away one wheel and set it apart; the other wheel you made over to Kutsa, that he might attain wealth (वरिवः (*varivaḥ*) is wealth). Further, the Dasyus, the Asuras, are अनासः (*anāsaḥ*), without a mouth; by the word for mouth, sound is meant, so they are soundless and dumb. These you killed with your weapon, the thunderbolt. In the battle (दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)) you utterly split the Asuras whose organ of speech is harmed ⟨NOTE:84⟩. The doubling of the verbs अमृणः (*amṛṇaḥ*) and न्यवृणगिति (*nyavṛṇagiti*) is for emphasis.
notes: ಹೇ ಸುಘವನ್ಥನವನ್ನಿಂದ್ರ: damaged at the beginning of the bhāṣya; read as address to the wealthy Indra

en: - सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—(O Indra,) of Sūrya (of the chariot with two wheels)
- अनासः (*anāsaḥ*)—who were without a mouth and dumb
- वधेन (*vadhena*)—with the thunderbolt, the means of killing
- मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*)—the Asuras whose speech is harmful
- नि अवृणक् (*ni avṛṇak*)—you have cut through completely

O Indra, of the two wheels of Sūrya's chariot you set one apart; the other you made a help to Kutsa for obtaining wealth. With the thunderbolt, the means of killing, you harmed the Asuras who were without a mouth and dumb. In battle you have cut through completely the Asuras whose speech is harmful.

You have formerly detached one wheel (of the car) of Surya : another you have given to Kutsa wherwith to acquire wealth : with the thunderbolt you have confounded the voiceless Dasyus, you have destroyed in battle the speech-bereft (foes).
