en: Sāyaṇa glosses देवासः (*devāsaḥ*) as "O gods" and वः (*vaḥ*) as "you". Thus, indeed, and quickly, the mortal, the sacrificer, worships (वनते (*vanate*)) for offspring accompanied by cattle (पशुमत्यै (*paśumatyai*) प्रजायै (*prajāyai*)). The repetition in आ देवास (*ā devāsa*) is for the sake of respect. In this sacrifice, may the deity Nirṛti make good food for me, for this body, a son favoured by the gods. And may she swallow up (ग्रसतु (*grasatu*)) old age.
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—for the protection of this body
- शिवां धासिं (*śivāṃ dhāsiṃ*)—the most excellent food

O gods, the human being worships you without fail for the wealth of progeny together with cattle; he is bound to worship you. On this occasion may the god Nirṛti increase the excellent food needed for the nourishment of this body of mine. May she see to it that our body does not waste away through old age.

The mortal (sacrificer) worships you, gods, at all times for progeny and cattle : verily, gods, the mortal worships you: may Nirriti, on this occasion, sustain my body with solutary food, and keep off decay.

In the present mantra Nirṛti is regarded as a particular deity. Sāyaṇa has explained it as meaning a deity. And the sacrificer prays that she should do him a favour. Such contexts are rare. Nirṛti is ordinarily known as a deity who causes harm. In the present case a good result is expected from that deity. It is therefore necessary to know what the true nature of this deity is.
The Nirukta-writers have read the word निर्यति (*niryati*) among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5).⟨NOTE:220⟩ Afterwards, showing the derivation of this word,

इमान्येकविंशतिः पृथिवीनामधेयान्यनुक्रांतानि । तत्र निर्यतिर्निरमणादृच्छतेः कृच्छ्रापत्तिरितरा सा पृथिव्या संदिह्यते । तयोर्विभागः ॥ (*imānyekaviṃśatiḥ pṛthivīnāmadheyānyanukrāṃtāni | tatra niryatirniramaṇādṛcchateḥ kṛcchrāpattiritarā sā pṛthivyā saṃdihyate | tayorvibhāgaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 2-7)

This word may be formed from two roots. If it is formed first from the root *ram*, then निरमणात् (*niramaṇāt*): निविष्टानि रमंते अस्यां भूतानीति निर्ऋतिः पृथिवी (*niviṣṭāni ramaṃte asyāṃ bhūtānīti nirṛtiḥ pṛthivī*); because all beings that rest on the earth experience delight from the earth, the earth has the name Nirṛti. Secondly, from ऋच्छतेः (*ṛcchateḥ*): इतरा कृच्छ्रापत्तिः । दुःखसंज्ञिका । निर्ऋतिः पाप्मा । (*itarā kṛcchrāpattiḥ | duḥkhasaṃjñikā | nirṛtiḥ pāpmā |*); because she causes sorrow, the goddess Nirṛti is a producer of sin. But here, समान नामधेयत्वात् समानश्रुतित्वं पृथिव्या संदिह्यते (*samāna nāmadheyatvāt samānaśrutitvaṃ pṛthivyā saṃdihyate*); having shown in this way the two derivations of this word, he then says that the meaning of the word is to be stated according to the context, that when the meaning "earth" is intended one must not take it as "mother of sin", and when the second purport is intended one must not take it as "earth".

Durgācārya has explained it in two ways: 1) एका निविष्टानां भूतानां रमयित्री (*ekā niviṣṭānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ramayitrī*), one who gives delight to all beings; 2) एका पुनः कृच्छ्रमापादयित्री (*ekā punaḥ kṛcchramāpādayitrī*), another who gives sorrow. In this context the Nirukta-writers

य ईं चकार न सो अस्य वेद य ईं ददर्श हिरुगिन्नु तस्मात् । स मातुर्योना परिवीतो अंतर्बहुप्रजा निर्ऋतिमा विवेश ॥ (*ya īṃ cakāra na so asya veda ya īṃ dadarśa hiruginnu tasmāt | sa māturyonā parivīto aṃtarbahuprajā nirṛtimā viveśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-32)

cite this mantra and explain the meaning of the word *nirṛti*. In the cited mantra, in stating his explanation of the word *nirṛti*, Sāyaṇa first gives his own view, which differs from that of the Nirukta-writers, and explains it as sorrow; afterwards he also gives the view of the Nirukta-writers and explains it as the earth, the means of sorrow. But it appears that the view of the Nirukta-writers is that whenever the meaning "earth" is intended, it must be explained as a means of delight. But the use of the word *nirṛti* appears for the most part to concern an inauspicious deity. One or two of these may be taken as examples and their purport examined.
मो षु णः परापरा निर्युतिर्दुर्हणा वधीत् । पदीष्टतृष्णया सह ॥ (*mo ṣu ṇaḥ parāparā niryutirdurhaṇā vadhīt | padīṣṭatṛṣṇayā saha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.38-6)

Here the word *nirṛti* is explained as a deity of the demon class. The prayer is that this deity of demonic form may not do us harm. In such contexts, powers that cause calamity, such as famine and greed, are indicated as the deity. In sum, it may be explained as the presiding deity of sin.
Showing the purport of this word, the scholar Max Muller has stated his view thus:

"One of the meanings of निर्यति (*niryati*) is sin. It is derived from the same root which yielded ऋत (*ṛta*) in the sense of right. निर्यति (*niryati*) was conceived, it would seem, as going away from the Path of right. It was personified as a power of destruction and evil," (Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 32, p. 88)

Among the many meanings of the word *nirṛti*, the meaning "sin" is the most frequent. The word *nirṛti* is formed from the same root from which the word *ṛta* is formed. The word *ṛta* means the straight path, truth. That which is without straightness and without truth is the meaning of the word *nirṛti*. To conceive the states of sin and destruction as embodied is the knowledge of the nature of the deity Nirṛti.⟨NOTE:221⟩ There is a rule that certain rites must be performed to escape from the influence of this deity, who is full of sin and causes sorrow. When these rules are stated, the nature of this deity is stated along with them. For example, only a few passages may be examined here.

अथातो नैऋतीर्हरंति । एतद्वै देवा गार्हपत्यं चित्वा समारोहन्नयं वै लोको........समारोहंस्ते तम एवानतिदृश्यमपश्यन् ॥ (*athāto naiṛtīrharaṃti | etadvai devā gārhapatyaṃ citvā samārohannayaṃ vai loko........samārohaṃste tama evānatidṛśyamapaśyan ‖*) (Śa. Bhā. 7. 2. 1-1)⟨NOTE:222⟩

These are the mantras recited while the bricks named Nirṛti are laid. When the gods had built the Gārhapatya fire-altar and were ready to ascend it, they were enveloped in pitch darkness on this Gārhapatya, which has the form of the earth, and could see nothing.
तेऽब्रुवन् । उप तज्ञानीत यथेदं तमः पाप्मानमपहनामहा इति तेऽब्रुवंश्चतयध्वमिति ॥ (*te 'bruvan | upa tajñānīta yathedaṃ tamaḥ pāpmānamapahanāmahā iti te 'bruvaṃścatayadhvamiti ‖*)
"We must think how we are to cross this darkness. All of you meditate, seeking a means of destroying it." When this was said, the knowledge came to them that the fire-altar must be built.

ते चेतयमानाः । एता इष्टका अपश्यन्नैर्य्यतीस्ता उपादधत ताभिस्तत्तमः पाप्मानमपाघ्नत पाप्मा वै निर्ऋतिः तद्यदेताभिः पाप्मानं निर्ऋतिमपाघ्नत ॥ (*te cetayamānāḥ | etā iṣṭakā apaśyannairyyatīstā upādadhata tābhistattamaḥ pāpmānamapāghnata pāpmā vai nirṛtiḥ tadyadetābhiḥ pāpmānaṃ nirṛtimapāghnata ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-3)

Meditating, they found the bricks named Nirṛti. Then by building them they destroyed the darkness and Nirṛti, who has the form of sin. Nirṛti is the mass of sin in the form of destruction. By the building of the bricks named Nirṛti this sin is destroyed. In this way and the like the nature of this deity is described. But in order to escape the destructive influence of this deity, worship must be offered even to this deity.

असुन्वंतमयजमानमिच्छेति । यो वै न सुनोति न यजते तं निर्ऋतिऋच्छति स्तेनस्येत्यामन्विहि तस्करस्येति .... .... .... .... यथा स्येनतस्करः प्रलायमेत्यॆ वं प्रलायनि:हि .... .... .... .... नमो देवि निर्ऋते तुभ्यमस्त्विति नमस्कारेणैवैनामपहते ॥ (*asunvaṃtamayajamānamiccheti | yo vai na sunoti na yajate taṃ nirṛtiṛcchati stenasyetyāmanvihi taskarasyeti .... .... .... .... yathā syenataskaraḥ pralāyametyè vaṃ pralāyani:hi .... .... .... .... namo devi nirṛte tubhyamastviti namaskāreṇaivaināmapahate ‖*) (Śa. Prā. 7 2.1.9)⟨NOTE:223⟩

"O goddess Nirṛti, strike the one who does not press the Soma for the sacrifice and does not offer the oblation in the sacrifice. O goddess, follow the very path the thief takes, and hide as he hides. Approach the one who is not a sacrificer and strike him. O goddess, homage to you"; saying this and making obeisance, he sends that goddess out.

नमः सु ते निर्ऋते तिग्मत्तेज इति । तिग्मत्तेजा वै निर्ऋतिस्तस्याएतन्नमस्करोत्ययस्मयं विच्यता बंधमेतमित्ययस्मयेन ह वै तं बंधेन निर्ऋतिर्बध्नाति .... .... .... .... ॥ (*namaḥ su te nirṛte tigmatteja iti | tigmattejā vai nirṛtistasyāetannamaskarotyayasmayaṃ vicyatā baṃdhametamityayasmayena ha vai taṃ baṃdhena nirṛtirbadhnāti .... .... .... .... ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-19)

"Homage to you, O Nirṛti of sharp brilliance. Indeed your power is very keen and radiant. Loosen this bond of mine in the form of an iron rod." For Nirṛti binds the man with whom she is displeased with hard iron rods (pierces him).

यस्यास्ते घोर आसज्जु होमीति । घोरा वै निर्ऋतिस्तस्या एतदासञ्जुहोति यत्तद्देवत्यं कर्म करोत्येषां बंधानामवसर्जनायेति यैर्बंधैर्बद्धो भवति यां त्वा जनो भूमिरिति प्रमंदत इतीयं वै भूमिरस्स्यां वै स भवति यो भवति निर्ऋतिं त्वाहं परिवेद विश्वत इति निर्ऋतिरिति त्वाहं परिवेद सर्वत इत्येतदियं वै निर्ऋतिरियं वै तं निरर्पयति यो निर्ऋच्छति................आमंत्रितो हिनस्ति ॥ (*yasyāste ghora āsajju homīti | ghorā vai nirṛtistasyā etadāsañjuhoti yattaddevatyaṃ karma karotyeṣāṃ baṃdhānāmavasarjanāyeti yairbaṃdhairbaddho bhavati yāṃ tvā jano bhūmiriti pramaṃdata itīyaṃ vai bhūmirassyāṃ vai sa bhavati yo bhavati nirṛtiṃ tvāhaṃ pariveda viśvata iti nirṛtiriti tvāhaṃ pariveda sarvata ityetadiyaṃ vai nirṛtiriyaṃ vai taṃ nirarpayati yo nirṛcchati................āmaṃtrito hinasti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-11)

"O goddess Nirṛti, you are of terrible form": having praised her thus, in performing the rite of the deity he offers the oblation in her mouth. If he offers it saying "O goddess, this is for the release of your bond", the sacrificer is freed from whatever bond he is bound by. "O goddess, the sacrificers address you as the earth; but I know you only as all-pervading." What is said here is also true. The earth rejects and thrusts far away the sacrificer who is blameworthy. If, as said above, worship is offered to Nirṛti, the sacrificer's release from bondage comes about.

नोपस्पृशति । पाप्मा वै निर्ऋतिर्नेत्पास्मना सग्गस्पृशा इति न सादयति प्रतिष्ठा वै सादनं नेत्वाप्मानं प्रतिष्ठापयानीति .... .... .... ॥ (*nopaspṛśati | pāpmā vai nirṛtirnetpāsmanā saggaspṛśā iti na sādayati pratiṣṭhā vai sādanaṃ netvāpmānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayānīti .... .... .... ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-1-12)

The sacrificer does not touch the bricks named Nirṛti. Nirṛti has the form of sin; therefore, if he touches them, contact with sin results. Nor does he set them up; if he set them up, it would be as if he established in his own house Nirṛti herself, who has the form of sin. — In this way and the like, in order to escape the sin-filled and sorrow-causing influence of Nirṛti, who is of an inauspicious nature, he regards her as a particular deity, worships her and sends her out (नमस्कारेणैवैनामपहते (*namaskāreṇaivaināmapahate*)). Thus there is a description of Nirṛti's nature. Even though Nirṛti is said to have the form of the earth, for some people the earth becomes a giver of delight; then the derivation of this word is from the root *ram*. For others the earth is a sharer of sorrow; then the derivation is from the root *ṛ*. Although at times an identity between the earth and this deity is shown, on many occasions she is regarded as a deity different from the earth.

en: Sāyaṇa addresses the gods as Vasus, "those who cause to dwell", and speaks of "that well-known good thought (sumati) of yours", that is, a means of good thinking; growth of thought comes from food, and it is well known in passages such as अन्नेन मतिवृद्धिरन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । (*annena mativṛddhirannamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ |*) (Chā. U. 6. 5. 4) that "the mind, dear one, is made of food". "Invigorating" means strength-giving, and the इषं (*iṣaṃ*) is food, a means of seeking, of the nature of milk, curds and the like. May we obtain it, may we reach it, through praise (शसा (*śasā*)) from the cow. May that goddess come to us for our good, for happiness; गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) means "may she come", "may she approach". The deity is further qualified: सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*), of good gifts; मृळयंती (*mṛḷayaṃtī*), making us happy; द्रवंती (*dravaṃtī*), hastening, coming towards us.
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O you who are of divine nature
- शसा (*śasā*)—as the fruit of our praises
- वः (*vaḥ*)—which is to be (kept) with regard to you
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—conducive to an excellent state of mind
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food of the nature of milk and the like
- प्रति गम्याः (*prati gamyāḥ*)—may she come towards us

O Vasus, divine beings, the food of milk and the like, to be obtained from that cow, is conducive to the pure state of mind that we must keep with regard to you, and is a producer of nourishment for our body. As the fruit of our praise may we obtain that food. And may that goddess, who is endowed with excellent gifts, who is a giver of happiness to us, and who is eager to favour us, come towards us for our good.
Divine Vasus, may we obtain from the adorable cow invigorating and mind-sustaining food : may that liberal and benignant goddess, hastening (hither), come for our felicity.

en: May Iḷā, the earth, the creator of the herd (the host of cows), praise us. Or, as they say, Iḷā is the daughter of Manu, who has taken the form of a cow. Or else Iḷā is the Mādhyamikā Vāc, the creator of the host of Maruts. Or Urvaśī is the Mādhyamikā Vāc. May she praise with the rivers, with the Gaṅgā and the others. The word स्मच्छब्दः (*smacchabdaḥ*) is said to be a word of praise: may she proclaim excellence. Or else Urvaśī, of abundant brilliance, uttering, praising our rite, covering (the sacrificer): whom? Āyu, the man, the sacrificer. By what? By प्रभृथस्य (*prabhṛthasya*), by brilliance or by water, by giving; the Nirukta (11-49) says that प्रभृथस्य तेजसो वोदकस्यॆति (*prabhṛthasya tejaso vodakasyèti*). Or else प्रभृथस्य (*prabhṛthasya*) means "of him who carries offerings forward", covering the sacrifice of Āyu.
- नदीभिः (*nadībhiḥ*)—together with the Gaṅgā and the other rivers

May the goddess Iḷā, the mother of the host of cows, and Urvaśī, together with the Gaṅgā and the other rivers, favour us. Moreover, may Urvaśī, of exceeding brilliance, be gracious, praising our rites and covering the sacrificer by the spreading of brilliance.
May Ila, the mother of the herd, and Urvashi, with the rivers, be favourable to us; may the bright-shining Urvashi (come), commanding our devotion, and investing the worshipper with light.

notes: abbreviation ಕ. printed

en: May she attend upon us, who belong to Ūrjavya of that name, the king, the nourisher. By implication the host of gods is understood; or else Urvaśī or the host of Maruts is taken, since it is the topic.
- पुष्टेः (*puṣṭeḥ*)—who are the cause of (his) increase
May that goddess serve us, who are the cause of the increase of the king named Ūrjavya.
May she cherish us (as the servants) of our patron Urjavya.

May the speech of praise, most happiness-giving, together with the दीधिती (*dīdhitī*), the rite consisting of casting in the oblation, surely and without fail reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi. Moreover, पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) is he who dwells in the middle region of dappled colour; पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) is Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa of the breaths prāṇa, apāna and the rest. Or else पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) is a name of Vāyu, for the śruti says that Vāyu is the five-fold hotṛ and he is the breath. He is अतूर्तपंथाः (*atūrtapaṃthāḥ*), of unharmed course, असुरः (*asuraḥ*), the giver of the breath, मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*), the abode of happiness. May Vāyu, of the nature so described, hear the praise.
- गीः (*gīḥ*)—the speech in the form of (our) praise
- दीधिती (*dīdhitī*)—joined with rites such as the giving of the oblation
- प्र अश्याः (*pra aśyāḥ*)—may it go and reach
- पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*)—he whose own place is the middle region, of variegated colours
- पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*)—Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa consisting of prāṇa, apāna and the rest

May our most happiness-giving praise, joined with rites such as the giving of the oblation, surely go and reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi. May Vāyu, whose own abode is the middle region of variegated colours, whose going is unimpeded, the giver of life, the bestower of happiness, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa consisting of prāṇa, apāna and the rest, hear our praise.
May our most animating praise, together with our offerings, successfully attain Varuna, Mitra, Bhaga and Aditi: may the ministrant
of the five (vital airs, Vayu), the dweller in the dappled (firmament), he whose path is unimpeded, who is the giver of life, the bestower of happiness, hear.

The two words पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) and पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) both describe the nature of Vāyu. Because he dwells in the middle region of dappled hue, Vāyu is called पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*). There is also the synonymous name पृश्निगर्भ (*pṛśnigarbha*). This is the purport of the first epithet. Secondly, for पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*) the explanation पंचविधस्य प्राणापानादिहोमस्य साधको वायुः (*paṃcavidhasya prāṇāpānādihomasya sādhako vāyuḥ*) is given: it is explained as Vāyu, the accomplisher of the fivefold homa in the form of prāṇa, apāna and the rest. It must be examined which natures of Vāyu these two epithets show. First,

पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*):— अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवताः । तासां वायुः प्रथमगामी भवति (*athāto madhyasthānā devatāḥ | tāsāṃ vāyuḥ prathamagāmī bhavati*) (Ni. 10.1). The Nirukta-writers have indicated Vāyu's place thus: among the deities of the middle region the first place belongs to Vāyu; he is the "first-going". There is a difference between merely "dwelling in the middle region" and पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) or पृश्निगर्भ (*pṛśnigarbha*). The epithet पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) also indicates Vāyu's right to enjoy the sacrifice.
अथ नमो नायवेंतरिक्ष्षिते लोकक्षिते (*atha namo nāyaveṃtarikṣṣite lokakṣite*) (Chā. U. 9-24-9)⟨NOTE:228⟩

The enjoyment of the sacrifice stated in such sentences is what is indicated in the present mantra. It is from this very place that he is the one to whom offerings are made, as is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa thus:

तान्वायुरब्रवीत् । उपाहमायानीति केनेति दिग्भिरिति तथेति दिश्याभिर्ह तदुवाच तस्माद्वितीयाय्कॆ स्वयमातृणाया अनंतर्हिता दिश्या उपधीयंते तस्मादंतरिक्षादनंतर्हिता दिशोऽनंतर्हितो वायुरनंतर्हितो हैष एताभिरुपैत् ॥ (*tānvāyurabravīt | upāhamāyānīti keneti digbhiriti tatheti diśyābhirha taduvāca tasmādvitīyāykè svayamātṛṇāyā anaṃtarhitā diśyā upadhīyaṃte tasmādaṃtarikṣādanaṃtarhitā diśo 'naṃtarhito vāyuranaṃtarhito haiṣa etābhirupait ‖*) (Śa. Bā. 6-2-3)⟨NOTE:229⟩

The layer of the second storey itself appeared in the form of the middle region. "I shall ascend there," said Vāyu. Then he joined the bricks of the layer. Then they were not separated from the middle regions. Then

Vāyu too came to have a permanent connection with the middle region, which is of the form of a brick, and so on; thus it is stated that his standing in the middle region itself produced his fitness for the sacrifice. While describing the nature of Vāyu at the time of the brahmodya it is said,
वायुर्गृहपतिरिति हैक आहुः सोंतरिक्षलोकस्य गृहपतिः । (*vāyurgṛhapatiriti haika āhuḥ soṃtarikṣalokasya gṛhapatiḥ |*)

and so on; thus it is stated that the lordship of the household fire (gārhapatya) of the middle world is the office of Vāyu. Although in this way the topic पृषद्योनिः (*pṛṣadyoniḥ*) points out the place of Vāyu, saying that the middle region itself is the womb (the place) of Vāyu, yet in some passages it is clearly stated that heaven and earth, both of them, are the causes of Vāyu's origin. For example:
राये नु यं यज्ञ तू रोदसीमे राये देवी धिषणा धाति देवं ॥ (*rāye nu yaṃ yajña tū rodasīme rāye devī dhiṣaṇā dhāti devaṃ ‖*)

In sentences of this kind, heaven and earth are said to have caused Vāyu to be born, and so the quality of being the womb of Vāyu is a common feature of the two worlds. The sentences प्राणाद्वायुरजायत (*prāṇādvāyurajāyata*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-13), "from the breath of the Supreme Person the birth of Vāyu took place", are sentences that point to the quality of being a "five-fold priest" in Vāyu, which is indicated by the word पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*), the second epithet in the present mantra. The connection that the five breaths, indicated by the word pañcahotṛ, have with Vāyu, and Vāyu's lordship over the middle region, are stated together in one and the same context in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows.
स यः स वैश्वानरः । अंतरिक्षमेव विश्वं । वायुर्नरः ॥ (*sa yaḥ sa vaiśvānaraḥ | aṃtarikṣameva viśvaṃ | vāyurnaraḥ ‖*)

The middle region itself is the universe (viśva). Since Vāyu is the lord of the middle region, he too has the repute of being Vaiśvānara. Moreover, if the influence of Vāyu is to be described further,

इदमेवांतरिक्षं । तस्मादेतदलोमकमलोमकमिव ह्यंतरिक्षं तदेतद्विश्वं प्राण एव वायुः स नरः स मध्येनास्य भवति मध्यॆ न ह्यंतरिक्षस्य वायुः ॥ (*idamevāṃtarikṣaṃ | tasmādetadalomakamalomakamiva hyaṃtarikṣaṃ tadetadviśvaṃ prāṇa eva vāyuḥ sa naraḥ sa madhyenāsya bhavati madhyè na hyaṃtarikṣasya vāyuḥ ‖*)

This middle part of the Universal Person is the middle region itself. It is without hair. For this part of the Universal Self, Vāyu is the form of breath; he is the Man (nara). This Vāyu is the lord of the middle world. Sentences such as these declare the nature and the authority of Vāyu.

अथ विश्वज्योतिषमुपदधाति । वायुर्वै मध्यमा विश्वज्योतिर्वायुर्ह्येवांतरिक्षलोके विश्वं ज्योतिर्वायुमेवैतदुपदधाति तामनंतर्हितां दिश्याभ्य उपदधाति दिक्षु तद्वायुं दधाति तस्मात्सर्वासु दिक्षु वायुः ॥ (*atha viśvajyotiṣamupadadhāti | vāyurvai madhyamā viśvajyotirvāyurhyevāṃtarikṣaloke viśvaṃ jyotirvāyumevaitadupadadhāti tāmanaṃtarhitāṃ diśyābhya upadadhāti dikṣu tadvāyuṃ dadhāti tasmātsarvāsu dikṣu vāyuḥ ‖*)

When the bricks named Viśvajyotis are laid, there is this praise of Vāyu. The Viśvajyotis of the middle part is Vāyu. Vāyu is the light that illumines the world. Since it reflects all the directions and the intermediate directions, it is an all-pervading form of radiance. It also has the power of producing universal vitality. For this Vāyu, who is of the form of the universal light, the middle region is merely the place of origin; the existence of this Vāyu is all-pervading.

वायुर्वाव धर्त्तं चतुष्टोमः स आभिश्चतसृभिर्दिग्भिः स्तुते तद्यत्तमाह धर्त्तमिति प्रतिष्ठा नै धर्त्तं वायुरु सर्वेषां भूतानां प्रतिष्ठा तदेव तद्रूपमुपदधाति स वै वायुमेव प्रथममुपदधाति वायुमुत्तमं वायुनैव तदेतानि सर्वाणि भूतान्युभयतः परिगृह्णाति ॥ (*vāyurvāva dharttaṃ catuṣṭomaḥ sa ābhiścatasṛbhirdigbhiḥ stute tadyattamāha dharttamiti pratiṣṭhā nai dharttaṃ vāyuru sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ pratiṣṭhā tadeva tadrūpamupadadhāti sa vai vāyumeva prathamamupadadhāti vāyumuttamaṃ vāyunaiva tadetāni sarvāṇi bhūtānyubhayataḥ parigṛhṇāti ‖*)

Thus is the praise of Vāyu by the hymn that is a part of the Catuṣṭoma. If the Catuṣṭoma is the supporter of all sacrifices, then Vāyu is this Catuṣṭoma. Therefore Vāyu is the supporter of all sacrifices. Because he keeps bestowing, from all directions, the gift in the form of praise, Vāyu is the supporter of the sacrifice from every direction. Moreover he is the foundation of all beings and their support as well. In this way the importance of Vāyu in the sacrifice is praised.

In the present mantra, one must examine what personal quality is praised by the epithet पंचहोता (*paṃcahotā*), "the accomplisher of the offering in the form of the five breaths". Because he gives vitality to all living beings, Vāyu is praised in many places as the lord of the breath. He is the support, the shelter and the prop even of the primal deities Agni, Āditya and Soma, who give vitality to all beings. He is of the form of the breath of the universe. How is that? Thus:

वायुर्वाव संवर्गो यदा वा अग्निरुद्वायति वायुमेवाप्येति यदा सूर्योऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति यदा चंद्रोऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति ॥ (*vāyurvāva saṃvargo yadā vā agnirudvāyati vāyumevāpyeti yadā sūryo 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti yadā caṃdro 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti ‖*)

In the world Vāyu takes into his own power all things. When fire blazes up and becomes quiet, and after the sun has set, and after the moon has set, they join Vāyu alone and become one with him there.
शौ वा ऐश् द्वै संवर्गौ वायुरेव देवेषु प्राणः प्राणेषु ॥ (*śau vā aiś dvai saṃvargau vāyureva deveṣu prāṇaḥ prāṇeṣu ‖*)

Among the "gatherers" of the world (those that take everything into themselves) there are chiefly only two that draw the breath: among the gods, Vāyu, and among the fivefold breaths, the breath. Vāyu and the breaths are not different principles.
वायुः प्राणो भूत्वा नासिके प्राविशत् । (*vāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat |*)

Thus it is described: Vāyu, becoming breath, entered the nostrils. The following sentences explain that the five breaths too are the five-fold transformations of Vāyu. Moreover, they state the connection that the offering in the form of breath has with Vāyu.

तस्य व्युष्टिवाहनोऽश्वरथो दक्षिणा । त्रयोऽश्वा द्वौ सव्यष्टसारथी ते पंचप्राणा यो वै प्राणः स वातस्तद्यते तस्य कर्मण एषा दक्षिणा तस्मात्पंचवातीयं नाम ॥ (*tasya vyuṣṭivāhano 'śvaratho dakṣiṇā | trayo 'śvā dvau savyaṣṭasārathī te paṃcaprāṇā yo vai prāṇaḥ sa vātastadyate tasya karmaṇa eṣā dakṣiṇā tasmātpaṃcavātīyaṃ nāma ‖*)

This is the explanation of the offering of oblations named Pañcavātīya. Here, what are the five oblations? They are three horses, a warrior, and a charioteer. The five breaths are these three horses, the warrior and the charioteer. These five breaths are the fivefold transformations of Vāyu. Therefore, since he is the accomplisher of the sacrifice by the oblations that are his own five forms, a kind of five-fold priesthood is established through this Pañcavātīya quality. Besides this, the five-fold priesthood has a spiritual meaning as well. The explanation below contains both purports, the one concerning the deities and the one concerning the self, and it also makes clear the five-fold priesthood of Vāyu.
प्राणो वै वायुः । प्राणोग्निस्तस्येमा इष्टका । यः प्राणो व्यानोऽपानः समान उदानः ॥ (*prāṇo vai vāyuḥ | prāṇognistasyemā iṣṭakā | yaḥ prāṇo vyāno 'pānaḥ samāna udānaḥ ‖*)

From one point of view the Gārhapatya fire is in the form of the year, which consists of the five seasons. From another point of view this same Gārhapatya is in the form of Vāyu, which consists of the five breaths. Prāṇa, apāna, vyāna,

udāna and samāna, the five breaths so named, are the bricks of this Vāyu in the form of the Gārhapatya. It is described that Vāyu, the accomplisher of this offering in the form of the five breaths, has the five-fold priesthood.

Besides this, how Vāyu, comprising these five breaths, is the accomplisher of the offering in the sacrifice that consists of the realisation of the Self is thus: the description of this offering of a spiritual nature is as follows.

तस्य ह ना एतस्य हृदयस्य पंच देवसुषयः स योऽस्य प्राज्‌सुषि स प्राणस्तच्चक्षुः स आदित्यस्तदेतत्तेजोऽन्नाद्यमित्युपासीत तेजस्व्यन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tasya ha nā etasya hṛdayasya paṃca devasuṣayaḥ sa yo 'sya prājsuṣi sa prāṇastaccakṣuḥ sa ādityastadetattejo 'nnādyamityupāsīta tejasvyannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

In the heart of a person there are five paths to the sacrifice that is the realisation of Brahman. Among these, the door of the eastern direction is the breath. That is the eye, and that is the sun. One should meditate upon that radiance as food. One who knows this truth becomes radiant and an eater of food.

अथ योऽस्य दक्षिणः सुषिः । स व्यानस्तच्छोत्रं स चंद्रमास्तदेतच्छिश्च यशश्चेत्युपासीत श्रीमान् यशस्वी भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣiḥ | sa vyānastacchotraṃ sa caṃdramāstadetacchiśca yaśaścetyupāsīta śrīmān yaśasvī bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
The path of the southern direction is vyāna. That is the ear and the moon. The worshipper should meditate upon it as fame and as wealth. One who knows this truth becomes wealthy and famous.

अथ योऽस्य प्रत्यज् सुषि: सोऽपानः सा वाक् सोऽग्निस्तदेतद्ब्रह्मवर्चसमन्नाद्य मित्युपासीत ब्रह्मवर्चस्यन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद । (*atha yo 'sya pratyaj suṣi: so 'pānaḥ sā vāk so 'gnistadetadbrahmavarcasamannādya mityupāsīta brahmavarcasyannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda |*)

The path of the western direction is apāna. That is speech and fire. The worshipper should meditate upon it as the knowledge of Brahman, which is the cause of the brilliance of Brahman, and as food. One who knows this truth becomes possessed of the brilliance of Brahman and an eater of food.

अथ सोऽस्योदज्‌सुषिः स समानस्तन्मनः स पर्जन्यस्तदेतत्कीर्तिश्च व्युष्टिश्चेत्युपासीत कीर्तिमान्व्युमान्भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha so 'syodajsuṣiḥ sa samānastanmanaḥ sa parjanyastadetatkīrtiśca vyuṣṭiścetyupāsīta kīrtimānvyumānbhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
Samāna is the path of the northern direction. That is the mind-principle and is of the nature of Parjanya. That is fame and beauty. One who knows this truth becomes famous and powerful.

अथ योऽस्योर्ध्वः सुषिः स उदानः स वायुः स आकाशस्तदेतदोजश्च महश्चेत्युपासीतौजस्वी महस्वान्भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*atha yo 'syordhvaḥ suṣiḥ sa udānaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa ākāśastadetadojaśca mahaścetyupāsītaujasvī mahasvānbhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
Udāna is the door of the upper part. That is Vāyu and that is space. The worshipper should meditate upon it as vigour and as strength. One who knows this becomes vigorous and strong.

ते वा एते पंच ब्रह्मपुरुषाः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपाः एतानेवं पंच .... .... .... .... स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान्वेद ॥ (*te vā ete paṃca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya lokasya dvārapāḥ etānevaṃ paṃca .... .... .... .... svargasya lokasya dvārapānveda ‖*)

These five divisions of Vāyu, of the nature of breath, are the door-keepers of the Person who is Brahman. One who knows this truth attains union with Brahman; thus the spiritual five-fold priesthood is described. Śaṅkarācārya, explaining this in his commentary, has explained it with sentences such as प्राणाय स्वाहेति हुतं हविः सर्वमेतत्तर्पयतीति (*prāṇāya svāheti hutaṃ haviḥ sarvametattarpayatīti*) (Chā. U. Śa. Bhā. 3-13.1)⟨NOTE:239⟩.

en: Sāyaṇa takes the word मे (*me*) as "mine" and says that the deity Aditi is to accept my praise (stoma, stotra). "As a mother her own son": as a mother, having received her son and embraced him, is pleased, so may she be, this is the meaning. What kind of praise is it? It is heart-going (हृद्यं (*hṛdyaṃ*)) and gives good happiness (सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)); these two qualities are common to the praise. Further, the brahma, the mass of mantras, which is pleasing, dear to the gods and attainable by the gods, which is a means of happiness: that I convey to Mitra and Varuṇa, "I convey" being the word to be supplied. Or else: of Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of day and night, there is the brahma of the stated character, the great rite in the form of sacrifice and so on, and that I uphold.⟨NOTE:240⟩
notes: ಹನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಣಾನಾಂ, ಗನಾದಿದಾತಾರಂ, ಪುರೂನಸುಃ printed in the bhāṣya: misprints for ಹವಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಣಾನಾಂ, ಗವಾದಿ…, ಪುರೂವಸುಃ?

en: - सूनं न (*sūnaṃ na*)—as (she) lovingly embraces her own child⟨NOTE:241⟩
- मयोभु (*mayobhu*)—is the giver of happiness, that mantra
notes: ಚೋಹುವಾನಂ printed; Saṃhitā has ಜೋಹುವಾನಂ

en: As a mother lovingly embraces her child, may Aditi lovingly accept my praise, which is pleasing and auspicious. The mantra that is affection-producing, beneficial to the gods and giver of happiness, that mantra I offer, addressing Mitra and Varuṇa.⟨NOTE:242⟩
notes: ಪುರೂನಸುಃ printed; Saṃhitā has ಪುರೂವಸುಃ

en: May Aditi accept my affectionate and devoted praise, as a mother (the endearments of) a son; the pleasing, delightful prayer that is approved of by the gods I address to Varuna and Mitra.

The Ṛk beginning उदीरय कवितमं कवीनां भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिमिति द्वे । (*udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnāṃ bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayaṃtaḥ puraṃdhimiti dve |*) is the vapā-yājyā at the animal sacrifice to Savitṛ in the rite named in the glued word उदीरयेत्येष्टैकादशिने (*udīrayetyeṣṭaikādaśine*)⟨NOTE:243⟩, and the sūtra says so: "'Udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnām' and 'bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayantaḥ puraṃdhim', two verses" (Ā. 3-7). By this Ṛk Savitṛ is praised. O priests, rouse this Agni, or Savitṛ, who stands before you, the most far-seeing (kavitama, "of penetrating vision") of the poets; carry him upward, that is, gladden him. Anoint this god with sweet Soma juice and with ghee; that is, satisfy him. May that god Savitṛ give us wealth (vasūni, fit for dwelling, such as cattle and the like), well offered (prayatā, prayatāni), beneficial, delightful (candrāṇi, āhlādaka) gold; this is the meaning of "may he give" (suvāti).
notes: ರತಾ ದಿ printed for ರತ್ನಾದಿ?

en: - सः सविता (*saḥ savitā*)—that same god Savitṛ
notes: ಹೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಪತೇ in the bhāṣya, while the Kannada gloss addresses Bṛhaspati

en: O priests, gladden the god Savitṛ, the most excellent of poets. Satisfy this god with sweet Soma juice. May that same god Savitṛ give us wealth that is complete, beneficial and delightful.
Celebrate, (priests), the most prophetic of the prophets; imbue him with the sweet libation, and may the divine Savitri bestow upon us ample beneficial, and delightful riches.

This Ṛk beginning with the word उदीरय (*udīraya*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā-offering made in the animal sacrifice to the deity called Ekādaśī Savitṛ⟨NOTE:245⟩, as is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra उदीरय कवितमं कवीनां भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिमिति द्वे (*udīraya kavitamaṃ kavīnāṃ bhagaṃ dhiyaṃ vājayaṃtaḥ puraṃdhimiti dve*) (Ā. 3-7).
notes: ಆಪವ್ರತಾನ್ printed; Saṃhitā has ಅಪವ್ರತಾನ್

en: O Indra, you lead us (सं नेषि (*saṃ neṣi*)) with a mind, that is, with an excellent thought, together with cows; that is, you bring cows to us. In the same way the verb is to be supplied everywhere. O Harivat, that is, Indra, who has the two bay horses, you lead us with the wise (सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)), that is, with sons or with priests⟨NOTE:246⟩; likewise with blessings (स्वस्ति (*svasti*)), that is, with well-being, you lead us. With brahma, that is, with abundant food, you lead us: with the food which is beneficial to the gods. Further, you lead us with the good will (सुमत्या (*sumatyā*)), that is, with the thought of favour, of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice.
notes: ಸೂರನಿಂದ, ಸೂರಜ್ಯೋತಿ printed for ಸೂರ್ಯ-

en: - मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind full of favour
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, who has the horses named Hari

O Indra, with your mind full of favour, unite us with cows, with wise sons, and with abundant food that is beneficial also to the gods. And cause the thought of favour of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice to be upon us.

With a (willing) mind, Indra, you associate us with cattle, with pious (priests) and, lord of steeds, with prosperity, with (sacrificial) food that is agreeable to the gods, and with the favour of the adorable deities.

Here the deities are stated by their gender. Bhaga, the god Savitṛ, the master of wealth, Aṃśa, and स्वष्टा (*svaṣṭā*)⟨NOTE:247⟩, and Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra: these gods are the conquerors of riches, that is, those who rightly conquer them; Ṛbhukṣan, that is, Ṛbhu, and Vāja, and also Purandhi, that is, one of much wisdom, who is called Vibhu. And these gods, Bhaga and the others, being immortal, of the nature of not dying, hastening toward our sacrifice, may protect us.
notes: the Pada ends with ॥ ೧೮ ॥ where the Ṛk number is 10 (printed ೧೦ in the Saṃhitā)

en: - पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—Vibhvan, of many kinds of wisdom
- अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*)—all the gods who are free from the nature of death
- तुरासः (*turāsaḥ*)—being eager to come to our sacrifice

The god Bhaga, Savitṛ the master of wealth, Aṃśa, Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, Ṛbhu, Vāja and Vibhvan, who have obtained mastery over riches, and all the gods who are free from the nature of death, being eager to come to our sacrifice, may protect us.

May the divine Bhaga, Savitri, the lord of wealth, Ansa, Indra (the slayer) of vritra, (all) the conquerors of riches, Ribhukshin, Vaja and also Purandhi, immortals, hastening (to our sacrifice) preserve us.

We, the sacrificers, proclaim, that is, make known, the deeds of Indra, who is possessed of the Maruts (मरुत्वतो (*marutvato*)). What kind of Indra is he? He is unopposed (अप्रतीतस्य (*apratītasya*)), that is, one who has not retreated, who does not run away in battle. And not only that: he is victorious (जिष्णोः (*jiṣṇoḥ*)), that is, by nature a conqueror, and unageing (अजूर्यतः (*ajūryataḥ*)), that is, one who does not grow old, always young. Now it is said directly: O Maghavan Indra, the ancient men did not attain your valour, that is, your prowess; the later ones did not attain it either. What more is there to say? Whoever is new, a marvel, whoever he may be, does not attain valour.
- मरुत्वतः (*marutvataḥ*)—Indra, who is with the Maruts
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, the possessor of wealth
- नूतनः कश्चन (*nūtanaḥ kaścana*)—any among the moderns
notes: ದೇವಾನಾಂ ನೀತಿಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿರ್ಭಕ್ಷಣಂ ನಾ ಯತ್ರ: ನಾ printed, reading doubtful

en: We praise the heroic deeds of Indra, who is unopposed, victorious, undecaying and always in the company of the Maruts. O Indra, possessor of wealth, none of those who came before attained your prowess. None of those who came after attained it. None among the moderns can attain it.

We celebrate the exploits of Marutwat, the unrecoiling, the victorious, the undecaying: neither the ancients, Maghavan, nor their successors, have attained your prowess, nor has any one recent attained it.

O inner self, you praise (उप स्तुहि (*upa stuhi*)) the god Bṛhaspati. He is first (प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)), that is, chief, the most excellent; the giver of delightful wealth (रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*)); the distributor, the one who apportions, of riches that are of the nature of oblations⟨NOTE:249⟩. Or else: by the word ratna jewels, pearls and the like are meant, and here by the word dhana cows and the like; he is the giver of cows and the like. Bṛhaspati is the lord, the master, of the great mantra. Praise that god who praises the sacrificer with the śastras and extols him with the sāmans, who is the greatest producer of happiness (शंभविष्ठः (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*)), and who, being rich in abundant wealth, comes to the sacrificer who calls upon him.
notes: ಸ್ವಿಸು: printed; Saṃhitā has ಸ್ತಿಷುಃ, Kannada gloss ಸ್ವಿಷುಃ

en: - शंसते (*śaṃsate*)—who praises with the śastra mantras
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—to the sacrificer who extols with the sāmans and the like
- शंभविष्ठः (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*)—the giver of happiness; and he who
- चोहुवानं (*cohuvānaṃ*)—to the sacrificer who prays that he may come to his help⟨NOTE:250⟩
- रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*)—the giver of jewels and other riches⟨NOTE:252⟩
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—of the wealth of oblation-food and the like
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ printed
ಉತಾ printed in the gloss where the Saṃhitā has ಉರೌ
ಋಗ್ವೇ printed as the abbreviation of the reference

en: O inner self, praise and extol Bṛhaspati, who gives happiness to the sacrificer who praises with the śastras and the like and extols with the sāmans and the like, who comes bringing abundant wealth to the sacrificer who prays to him for help, who is the best of all, the giver of riches such as jewels, and the distributor of the wealth of oblation-food and the like.

Glorify the first donor of precious treasure, Brihaspati, the distributer of riches, the bestower of great happiness upon him who recites or chants (his praise), who comes laden with ample wealth to his invoker.

O Bṛhaspati, the sacrificers who are united with your protections (तवोतिभी (*tavotibhī*)), who are unharmed, wealthy and have good sons, that is, good heroes. Those who, favoured by you, are givers of many horses; or else givers of cows; and those who are givers of clothing and are fortunate, that is, possessed of good wealth: among all of these let riches, that is, wealth, come to be; "let come to be" is the word to be supplied.
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—and united also with excellent sons and the like
- ये सुभगाः (*ye subhagāḥ*)—whoever have obtained the wealth of your favour

O Bṛhaspati, the sacrificers who are united with your protections are unharmed by enemies, possessed of wealth and endowed with excellent sons and the like. Among all such as, having obtained the wealth of your favour, are givers of horses, givers of cows and givers of clothing, let riches abound.

Associated, Brihaspati, with your protections, (men) are unharmed (by foes), and become opulent and blessed with descendants: may wealth devolve on those who are generous, and givers of horses, of cows, of clothes.

Make the wealth of these who are about to be named (एषां (*eṣāṃ*)) scattering, that is, of a nature to disperse (विसर्माणं (*visarmāṇaṃ*)), O Brahmaṇaspati⟨NOTE:253⟩. Of whom does he say "of these"? Of those who enjoy without giving, that is, without bestowing: on whom? On us, who are distinguished by the ukthas, the śastras which convey praise. Make dispersing the wealth of those who are devoid of rites (अपव्रतान् (*apavratān*)), that is, whose works have gone astray, who are prospering in the world of men, the place of birth, who are haters of brahma, that is, haters of Brāhmaṇas and haters of mantras. Separate them from the sun; put them apart, that is, place them in darkness.
notes: ಮಹೇ in the gloss where the Saṃhitā and Pada have ಮಹಃ

en: - उक्थैः (*ukthaiḥ*)—who praise with the śastra and other mantras
- ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)—those fallen from the rites, who despise the mantras and the like without knowing their greatness
notes: ಖ. ಸಂ. printed

en: O Bṛhaspati, make the wealth of those greedy rich men who, without giving to us, who are distinguished by praise with śastras and the like, enjoy all wealth themselves, scatter and disperse. Those who, while prospering in the world of men, are devoid of Vedic rites and despise the mantras and the like without knowing their greatness, those who have fallen from the rites: separate them from the sun, that is, place them in pitch darkness, where there is no light of the sun.⟨NOTE:255⟩
notes: abbreviation ಬೃ. ವೇ. printed

en: Render transitory the riches of those who partake of enjoyment without giving satisfaction (to those who are eminent) by holy hymns: put apart from the sun, those who perform not sacred rites, and who, though prospering in their posterity, are the adversaries of prayer.

notes: abbreviation ಸಾ. ಭಾ. printed after ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ.

en: The sacrificer who brings (ओहते (*ohate*)) the powerful rākṣasas into the sacrifice called देवनीत् (*devanīt*), that is, the sacrifice in which there is the going of the gods, their arrival, their partaking⟨NOTE:257⟩, and who makes it demoniac by performing it wrongly and the like: that sacrificer, O Maruts, drive down with chariots without wheels (अचक्रेभिः (*acakrebhiḥ*)) into darkness. Or else: अचक्रेभिः (*acakrebhiḥ*) is to be construed with what goes before; by the word "wheel" the limbs of the rite are meant; he brings it again and again with only the principal parts, without the limbs; whereas a rite with its limbs reaches the gods. And whoever of you reviles the rite of praise (शमीं (*śamīṃ*)) belonging to me who am praising, that is, reviles the Vedic rite such as the Jyotiṣṭoma and the like, and himself pursues futile and perishable desires, enjoyments born of ploughing and the like, sweating, that is, tormenting himself. Or else: he makes the desirable enjoyments among you worthless.
notes: abbreviation ಇ. ಬ್ರ. printed

en: - देवनीत् (*devanīt*)—in the sacrifice that proceeds for the satisfaction of the gods
- शमीं (*śamīṃ*)—while performing a rite accompanied by praise
- शशमानस्य (*śaśamānasya*)—me, who praise (you) (or those who belong to me)
- सिष्टिदानः (*siṣṭidānaḥ*)—exposing himself to affliction and pouring out sweat

O Maruts, the sacrificer who brings demons into the sacrifice that proceeds for the satisfaction of the gods, push that sacrificer into darkness with chariots without wheels. The one who reviles me, who offer praise to you by performing a rite directed to you, or those who belong to me, he, exposing himself merely to affliction and pouring out sweat, imagines these desires for enjoyment that are of no worth.

Send, Maruts, into darkness, with (cars) devoid of wheels, the man who invites the Rakshasas to the food of the gods; (him also) who reviles me when offering praise to you : whilst sweating, he toils (to realize) vain desires.

O self, praise that very Rudra; make praise. He who has a good arrow (स्विसु: (*svisu:*))⟨NOTE:258⟩ and a good bow; his praiseworthiness is due to his killing of opponents. And he who is lord of all medicine, that is, of all herbs: for the allaying of bodily or worldly ailment, since there is no remedy apart from the Lord and since he is the best of physicians, his lordship over medicine is established, as the śruti says, भिषक्तमं त्वा भिषजां शृणोमि । (*bhiṣaktamaṃ tvā bhiṣajāṃ śṛṇomi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2.33-4)⟨NOTE:259⟩, and so on. Further, worship that Rudra, the god who delivers from suffering or from the evil that causes it, for great (महे (*mahe*)) good-mindedness; peace of mind from worship of the Lord is well known. Further, with salutations or with oblations, attend upon the shining god, the asura, that is, one of excellent life, the mighty one; or else: attend upon Rudra, the giver of breath.
notes: abbreviation ಪ್ರ. ಪ್ರ. printed
abbreviation ಚ. ಬ. printed

en: - सुधन्वा (*sudhanvā*)—and has a bow that is effective
- क्षयति (*kṣayati*)—is the lord; such a one
- सौमनसाय (*saumanasāya*)—for the gain of an excellent state of mind

Praise that Rudra who has an excellent arrow and an effective bow, who is the lord of all herbs. Perform the sacrifice addressed to that same Rudra for the gain of a great and excellent state of mind, and worship that same mighty god with salutations.
Praise him who has the sure arrow, the strong bow, who presides over all sanitary drugs; worship Rudra for a comprehensive and sound understanding; adore the powerful divinity with prostrations.

Here the deities are named by their gender. The word दमूनसो (*damūnaso*) means those of a giving mind or of a controlled mind; or else those who are अपसः (*apasaḥ*), doers of good work in making cups, chariots, cows and the like; the suffix of possession is dropped. For that very reason they are सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*), skilful of hand,

those who are such, the Ṛbhus; and the wives, that is, the protectresses, of the showerer, that is, of Indra the rain-giver; the rivers, those that roar, Gaṅgā and the others, made by the middle one of the Ṛbhus; Sarasvatī, the river of that name or the goddess of speech; Bṛhaddivā, of abundant radiance; and also the goddess Rākā; they who grant desires, the radiant; and may they favour us, that is, wish wealth for us.
- अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—possessed of excellent work such as the making of cups
- सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)—possessed of hands fit for skilful work
- वृष्ण (*vṛṣṇa*)—of Indra, the showerer of desires
- वरिवस्यंतु (*varivasyaṃtu*)—may they bless us that we may gain wealth

The Ṛbhus who are of giving mind, who are doers of excellent work such as the making of cups, who have hands fit for skilful work; the wives of Indra, the showerer of desires; the rivers fashioned by Vibhu; Sarasvatī; and the goddess Rākā, who shines exceedingly: may they too, supplying our desired objects and being radiant, bless us that we may gain wealth.

May the dexterous-handed, humble-minded artisans (of the gods, the Ribhus; may the wives of the showerer (Indra); may the rivers carved out by Vibhu; may Saraswathi and the brilliant Raka, the illustrious granters of desires, be willing to grant us riches.

I bring forth well, that is, I prepare excellently, for the great one, the good protector, Indra or Parjanya, or the giver of good happiness, a praise held in the mind (मेधां (*medhāṃ*)), a hymn. Of what kind? New, that is, very recent, or very praiseworthy, and being born, that is, produced now: new, that is the meaning. Indra or Parjanya, who is the striker, that is, the sprinkler, for the good of the daughter, that is, the earth, who stands in the place of a daughter, making forms in the rivers, has made this water for us.
- आहनाः (*āhanāḥ*)—as the one who pours out rain
- दुहितुः (*duhituḥ*)—of this earth, his daughter (for her good)
- सुशरणाय (*suśaraṇāya*)—and the giver of an excellent refuge, to such Indra
- मेधां (*medhāṃ*)—and of the nature of meditation
- प्र भरे (*pra bhare*)—I fashion, to offer

The Indra who, pouring out rain, for the good of the earth, his daughter, and producing forms of streams in the rivers, has made this water for our good: to offer to that great one, the giver of an excellent refuge, I fashion exceedingly a praise that is new, just now born, and of the nature of meditation.

To the great protector, (Indra), I offer devoutly pious praise, new and originated (at this time): to him, the showerer, who for his daughter (earth). giving form to the rivers, has provided this water for our (use).

Here Parjanya is praised. Sāyaṇa takes the verse thus: O worshipper, let your excellent praise surely reach, that is, attain in full measure, Parjanya, who thunders and roars, making the sound that is produced by raining, the lord of Ilā, that is, of food and of water. And that Parjanya who possesses the abbimān, the waters, that is, the clouds, and is full of water, goes forth sprinkling the two worlds, heaven and earth, with lightning.
- अब्दिमान् (*abdimān*)—who keeps the clouds under his own control
- रुवंतं (*ruvaṃtaṃ*)—producer of the sound that sprinkles rain

O worshipper, may your excellent praise go quickly and reach that Parjanya, the lord of food, who keeps all the clouds under his own control, who is full of water, who by his lightning makes heaven and earth shine, and who moves about thundering.

May your pious praise, oh worshipper, assuredly reach the thundering, roaring lord of Ila, who, impelling the clouds and distributing the rain, proceeds, illuminating the heaven and earth with lightning.

May this hymn, produced by me, reach the Maruts' might, turning towards it. Having praised them as a group, he now speaks of them as individuals: they are the sons of Rudra (their sonship to Rudra has been stated again and again), and they are youthful, or else desirous of union. The word for "up" is to be taken as "exceedingly": reach, O mind, exceedingly. Desire, that is, resolve, calls me, that is, impels me, towards wealth and towards imperishable well-being. Since this is so, approach and praise the Maruts who have spotted horses, that is, spotted in colour, and who go to the sacrifice.
- उत् आश्याः (*ut āśyāḥ*)—may it go and reach, so as to be pleasing
- पृषदश्वान् (*pṛṣadaśvān*)—those who ride horses of variegated colour
- आयासः (*āyāsaḥ*)—and who are going to the sacrifice, the gods

May this hymn, produced by me, go and reach the host of the Maruts, the sons of Rudra and very youthful, turning towards them and so as to be pleasing to them. My mental resolve, being desirous of wealth, impels me on an auspicious path alone. Approach and praise the gods who ride variegated horses and are going to the sacrifice.
May this hymn reach up to the presence of the might of the Maruts, the youthful sons of Rudra: the desire of riches incites me to holiness : glorify those who go to sacrifice on spotted steeds.

May this hymn, this praise, reach the deities beginning with Earth. For what purpose? For wealth. May every god, each and every deity, be easily invoked for me, that is, readily called. May Earth, the mother, the maker of all (or else, since Atri is earth-born, in a special sense the mother), not place us in ill-thought, that is, not establish us there.
- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise made by me
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the deity presiding over the mid-region
- वनस्पतीन् (*vanaspatīn*)—the deities of the forest trees
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the presiding deities of the herbs
- प्र अश्याः (*pra aśyāḥ*)—may it go and reach in an excellent manner
- सुहवो भूतु (*suhavo bhūtu*)—may be prayed to and called in an excellent manner
- मा धात् (*mā dhāt*)—may she not place
This praise, made by me, for the sake of wealth, may go and reach in an excellent manner the deity Earth, the deity of the mid-region, the deities of the forest trees and the deities of the herbs.
May every single deity be prayed to and called by me in an excellent manner. May Earth, the maker of the world, not join us with ill-thought.

May this hymn attain (the divinities) of earth and heaven, the trees, the herbs, for (the sake of) wealth: may each individual deity be successfully invoked by me : let not mother earth take us into unfavourable thought.
O gods, may we, the Atris, be in your great happiness that is wholly without obstruction.

notes: abbreviation ಕೃ. ಸಂ. printed

en: O gods, may we be in happiness that is exceedingly great and free from hindrance.
May we ever, gods, enjoy great and uninterrupted felicity.

We would come together with the Aśvins' protection, which is new, that is, not experienced before by others; which is joy-producing, that is, brings about happiness; and which is well-leading, that is, has good guidance. O immortals, deathless Aśvins, bring us wealth, that is, make it reach us; bring also sons of good valour; bring also all good fortunes.
- सं गमेम (*saṃ gamema*)—may we be joined
- अमृता (*amṛtā*)—O Aśvin deities, free from the nature of death

Together with protection that is new, never experienced before by anyone, joy-producing and excellent, may we always be possessed of them. O Aśvin deities, free from the nature of death, bring us wealth, heroic sons and all good fortunes.
May we ever be participant of the unprecedented, joy-conferring and well-guided protection of the Aswins: bring to us, immortal (Aswins,) riches, male progeny, and all good things.

The dhenus, the nourishing ones, are the rivers, accompanied by sweet milk, that is, sweet essence; they are swift in motion, for Yāska says that artha means going (Ni. 1. 18). Being unharming, may they come near to us. For the sake of great wealth they are the great ones, the seven, seven in number and of a flowing nature: the Gaṅgā and the others spoken of in the mantra इमं मे गंगे (*imaṃ me gaṃge*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 75. 5)⟨NOTE:261⟩, where seven only are mentioned as the principal ones. They are mayobhuvaḥ, bringers of happiness. The vipra, the one who especially gratifies, the worshipper, the praiser, invokes them, calls them.
notes: ನವಸಾ printed; the Saṃhitā has ನಮಸಾ

en: - अमर्धंतीः (*amardhaṃtīḥ*)—and not harming in any way
- आ यंतु (*ā yaṃtu*)—may they flow and come
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number, the Gaṅgā and the rest
notes: the printed text breaks off at ಯಜ್ಞತತ್ತ್ವವನ್ನರಿ at the end of the page, the rest of the gloss is missing

en: May the rivers, which give satisfaction to all men, come flowing near to us together with sweet water, flowing swiftly and not harming in any way. I, who am wise and a praiser, invoke with prayer the rivers, which are of great nature, seven in number, the Gaṅgā and the rest, and givers of happiness.
May the milch cows, quick-moving, doing no harm, come to us, (laden) with their sweet fluid; the wise worshipper invokes the seven-vast and joy-diffusing (rivers) for the sake of ample riches.
Rākā: Sāyaṇa has said earlier (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2.32-4)⟨NOTE:263⟩ that Rākā means the full-moon day, which has a complete moon. The author of the Nirukta, explaining this word, says:
राका रातेर्दानकर्मणः (हविदाननिमित्तं हि सा) (*rākā rāterdānakarmaṇaḥ (havidānanimittaṃ hi sā)*)
that is, the name Rākā is well known as formed from the root rā, which has the meaning of giving.
राका वाक् सरमाप्ताश्च भृगवोऽघ्ना श्य सरस्वती । (*rākā vāk saramāptāśca bhṛgavo 'ghnā śya sarasvatī |*)

From the Bṛhaddevatā text it is known that the particular deities Rākā, Vāc and the like belong to the Indra-world, the atmosphere. This deity is praised as one whose gift is accompanied by an exceedingly generous mind. Some statements show also that she is the sister of the gods and is as worthy of worship as the gods. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, at the time of laying down the worship of Rākā, a doubt arises and there is also an answer to it. On that occasion Sāyaṇa has explained as follows:

संपूर्णचंद्रमंडलयुक्ता पौर्णमासी राका । तदभिमानिदेवतायाः प्रतिपादिका ऋगपि राकेत्युच्यते । सेयं राका देवानां जामी नाम भगिनी ॥ (*saṃpūrṇacaṃdramaṃḍalayuktā paurṇamāsī rākā | tadabhimānidevatāyāḥ pratipādikā ṛgapi rāketyucyate | seyaṃ rākā devānāṃ jāmī nāma bhaginī ‖*)

The full-moon day that has the complete lunar disc is designated by the name Rākā. The Ṛk that praises the deity presiding over her is also well known by the name Rākā. He has explained the sense of the Brāhmaṇa sentence thus: this deity is worshipped as the sister of all the gods. In this connection a doubt arises about the order of worship of this deity. It is this:
तदाहू राकां पूर्वां शंसेच्चा मै वै पूर्वपेयमिति ॥ (*tadāhū rākāṃ pūrvāṃ śaṃseccā mai vai pūrvapeyamiti ‖*)

In this sentence the idea is expressed that to Rākā, the sister of the gods, worship that comes before that of the wives of the gods should be offered. But this injunction is the sentence of the prima facie view. पूर्वपेयं प्रथमतः सोमपानं युक्तमिति पूर्वपक्षः (*pūrvapeyaṃ prathamataḥ somapānaṃ yuktamiti pūrvapakṣaḥ*) (Sā. Bhā.). The next sentence refutes this prima facie view and states the established conclusion that the drinking of Soma that comes before is prescribed for the wives of the gods, rather than for Rākā.
तत्तन्नादृत्यं देवानामेव पत्निः पूर्वाः शंसेत् । (*tattannādṛtyaṃ devānāmeva patniḥ pūrvāḥ śaṃset |*)

It states the answer, to the effect that the drinking that comes before belongs to the wives of the gods, and that the wife, rather than the sister, is the first one worthy of worship. Therefore, since Rākā is the sister of the gods, she does not get the first place that falls to the wives of the gods.
समानोदर्रा स्वसा अन्नोदरय्यै जायाया अनुजीविनी जीवति ॥ (*samānodarrā svasā annodarayyai jāyāyā anujīvinī jīvati ‖*)

It states clearly that, although a sister is born of the womb of one and the same mother, she lives following the wife, who is of another womb, and therefore hers is the second place. Afterwards, while praising Rākā, he enjoins that the worship of Rākā be offered, reciting the mantras beginning राकामहं यास्ते राके (*rākāmahaṃ yāste rāke*), after the passage
राकां शंसति राका ह वा एतां पुरुषस्य सेविनीं सीव्यति यैषा ...... ...... ॥ (*rākāṃ śaṃsati rākā ha vā etāṃ puruṣasya sevinīṃ sīvyati yaiṣā ...... ...... ‖*)

He also states that the mantra that praises Rākā too has the name Rākā. He also praises this same goddess Rākā as one who, taking a most prominent place in the work of the sacrifice, becomes a helper of the sacrificer. At sacrificial times the help of the metres is indispensable. He states this deity to be of the form of a metre.

अनुमत्यै चरुं यानुमतिः सा गायत्री । राकायै चरुं या राका सा त्रिष्टुप् । सिनीवालै चरुं या सिनीवाली सा जगती । कुह्वै चरुं या कुहूः सा अनुष्टुप् । एतानि वाव सर्वाणि च्छंदांसि गायत्रं त्रैष्टुभं जागतमानुष्टुभमन्वन्यान्येतानि हि यज्ञे प्रतमामिव क्रियंते । (*anumatyai caruṃ yānumatiḥ sā gāyatrī | rākāyai caruṃ yā rākā sā triṣṭup | sinīvālai caruṃ yā sinīvālī sā jagatī | kuhvai caruṃ yā kuhūḥ sā anuṣṭup | etāni vāva sarvāṇi cchaṃdāṃsi gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatamānuṣṭubhamanvanyānyetāni hi yajñe pratamāmiva kriyaṃte |*)

Since the help of the metres is indispensable to the series of sacrificial acts, the deities beginning with Anumati themselves reflect those metres. Anumati is of the form of the Gāyatrī; the goddess Rākā is of the nature of the Triṣṭubh. Sinīvālī is of the form of the Jagatī. The goddess Kuhū is of the nature of the Anuṣṭubh. These are praised as the ones that attain abundance and excess in the sacrifice. Because these, being of the form of metres, are helpful to the sacrifice, they also assist in the works of Prajāpati in regulating the universe. How is that? It is thus:

स यः स धातायमेव स धात्रः । द्वादशकपालः पुरोडाशो द्वादशकपालो द्वादशमासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापतिर्धाताथ यत्तद्दिशां परमं त्रांतमेतानि तानि पूर्वाणि हवींष्यनुमत्यै चरू राकायैचरुः सितीनाल्यै चरुः कुह्वै चरुः .... .... .... ॥ (*sa yaḥ sa dhātāyameva sa dhātraḥ | dvādaśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo dvādaśakapālo dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatirdhātātha yattaddiśāṃ paramaṃ trāṃtametāni tāni pūrvāṇi havīṃṣyanumatyai carū rākāyaicaruḥ sitīnālyai caruḥ kuhvai caruḥ .... .... .... ‖*)

The offering of oblation follows that work of Prajāpati which is of the form of the Creator (Dhātṛ) and the Supporter. Since Prajāpati is of the form of the year, cakes are to be baked on twelve potsherds, following the twelve divisions that are the parts of the year. On this occasion the deities named Anumati, Rākā, Sinīvālī and Kuhū are always to be worshipped and satisfied with oblations. These deities, Rākā and the rest, give stability in the various regions to the works of Prajāpati that support the universe.

ता ना एता देव्यः । दिशो ह्येताश्चंदागांसि वै दिशश्चंदागांसि देव्योऽथैष कः प्रजापतिस्तद्यद्देव्यश्च कश्च तस्माद्देविकाः पंच भवंति पंच हि दिशः ॥ (*tā nā etā devyaḥ | diśo hyetāścaṃdāgāṃsi vai diśaścaṃdāgāṃsi devyo 'thaiṣa kaḥ prajāpatistadyaddevyaśca kaśca tasmāddevikāḥ paṃca bhavaṃti paṃca hi diśaḥ ‖*)

Rākā, Sinīvālī and these deities are the four regional deities of the universe. Therefore they are the regulators of the universe. They themselves are of the form of metres. Therefore they are helpers of the sacrificial work that is useful for the business of the universe. They assist the world-nourishing work of Prajāpati, who is called Ka. These are goddesses. Since these goddesses are joined together with Prajāpati, who is of the form Ka, the usage Devikāḥ for all of them together is stated, so the praise of Rākā and the other deities runs. Therefore, although in the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa the deity Rākā has a somewhat lower place than the wives of the gods, in other places the influence of this deity is celebrated to the highest degree. That the help of these goddesses is quite necessary for the continuous growth of the progeny of the world is praised in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The very goddesses whom it addresses as Devikāḥ because of their world-nourishing power are the ones whom a man desiring offspring should worship.

देविकाः ऎंब व्यवहारवु ऎंबुदागि राका मुंताद देवतॆगळ प्रशंसॆयिदॆ. आदुदरिंद, ऐतरेय ब्राह्मणवाक्यदल्लि राका देवतॆगॆ, देवपत्नियरिगिंतलू कॊंच अपकृष्टवाद स्थानविद्दरू उळिदॆडॆ गळल्लि ई देवतॆय प्रभाववन्नु अत्यतिशयवागि कॊंडाडिदॆ. विश्वद प्रजासंततियु अनुसूतवागि वृद्धियागलु ई देवियर सहायवु अत्यावश्यवॆंबंशवन्नु तैत्तिरीयसंहितॆयल्लि प्रशंसिसिदॆ. याव ई देवियरन्नु अवर जगत्पोषकशक्तिगागि देविकाः ऎंदु संबोधिसिदॆयो, अवरन्ने संतति कामनाद पुरुषनु आराधिसबेकु. देविका निर्वपेत्सजाकामश्चंदाग्‌ंसि वै देविकाश्चंदाग्ंसीव खलु वै प्रजाश्चंदोभिरेवास्मै प्रजाः प्र जनयति प्रथमं धातारं करोति मिथुनी एव तेन करोत्यन्वेवास्मा अनुमतिर्मन्यते राते राका प्र सिनीवाली जनयति .... .... .... देविकाश्चंदाग्ंसिवि ॥ (*devikāḥ èṃba vyavahāravu èṃbudāgi rākā muṃtāda devatègaḷa praśaṃsèyidè. ādudariṃda, aitareya brāhmaṇavākyadalli rākā devatègè, devapatniyarigiṃtalū kòṃca apakṛṣṭavāda sthānaviddarū uḷidèḍè gaḷalli ī devatèya prabhāvavannu atyatiśayavāgi kòṃḍāḍidè. viśvada prajāsaṃtatiyu anusūtavāgi vṛddhiyāgalu ī deviyara sahāyavu atyāvaśyavèṃbaṃśavannu taittirīyasaṃhitèyalli praśaṃsisidè. yāva ī deviyarannu avara jagatpoṣakaśaktigāgi devikāḥ èṃdu saṃbodhisidèyo, avaranne saṃtati kāmanāda puruṣanu ārādhisabeku. devikā nirvapetsajākāmaścaṃdāgṃsi vai devikāścaṃdāgṃsīva khalu vai prajāścaṃdobhirevāsmai prajāḥ pra janayati prathamaṃ dhātāraṃ karoti mithunī eva tena karotyanvevāsmā anumatirmanyate rāte rākā pra sinīvālī janayati .... .... .... devikāścaṃdāgṃsivi ‖*)

A man desiring offspring should offer oblation to Rākā and the other goddesses. These deities are of the form of metres. Offspring too grows in the form of metres. Therefore Rākā and the others, who are of the form of mothers, are the cause of the origin of the metres, who are of the form of sons. Dhātṛ alone is the husband. After conjugal relation has been entered into with Anumatī, Rākā,

these (goddesses), the birth of offspring takes place. Therefore the worship of these Devikās is prescribed. Not only the wealth of progeny, but also he who wishes for wealth of cattle should follow this order of worship.
This point is stated by sentences of this kind. Stating that these four Devikās are four forms of the moon, it describes their forms in this way.
पूर्वपक्षो राकापरपक्षः कुहूरमावास्या सिनीवाली पौर्णमास्यनुमतिच्चंद्रमा धाता .... । (*pūrvapakṣo rākāparapakṣaḥ kuhūramāvāsyā sinīvālī paurṇamāsyanumaticcaṃdramā dhātā .... |*)

The goddess Rākā is the first fortnight. The goddess Kuhū is the second fortnight. Sinīvālī is the night of the new moon. Anumati is the night of the full moon. Dhātṛ is the moon. In the form of wives of this moon, who is of the form of Dhātṛ, they are helpers in the manifestation and nourishment of the works of the world's business. In the present mantra the praise of Rākā, who has such influence, is recited, and the order of worship of this deity is laid down.
notes: ಸಂಪ್ರತ್ಯರ್ಥೀಯಃ, ಅಸ್ತು ಪಮಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ ಸಂಪ್ರತ್ಯರ್ಥೇ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಃ: machine-read Sanskrit damaged; sense of Sāyaṇa's remark on "na" not settled

ಪರಿವೃಢಸ್ಯ ಕರ್ಣಣಃ: sense not clear; ಕರ್ಮಣಃ?
