पूषा (*pūṣā*), भगः (*bhagaḥ*), अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—पूषा पोषकः (*pūṣā poṣakaḥ*): one who nourishes by giving food and the like. भगः भजनीयः (*bhagaḥ bhajanīyaḥ*): the deity worthy to be worshipped. आदितिः अखंडनीयः (*āditiḥ akhaṃḍanīyaḥ*): one who pervades everywhere. These three words are explained as epithets of Agni. Or else the commentator says that they may be explained as three separate deities, Pūṣan, Bhaga and Aditi. When it is explained as referring to Agni, the verb दयते (*dayate*): दयते । दयतिरनेककर्मात्र दहने वर्तते (*dayate | dayatiranekakarmātra dahane vartate*); the root has many meanings, and here it is used in the sense of burning. That is, the intention is that Agni burns the oblations and other substances. Or else दयते ददाति यजमानाय (*dayate dadāti yajamānāya*): he gives food and other substances to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice; thus the sense of giving may also be stated for the root. The act of burning applies to Agni alone. The act of giving applies to Agni and also to the other deities, Pūṣan and the rest.

वस्ते (*vaste*), उस्रः (*usraḥ*)—The word उस्र (*usra*) is formed from the root meaning "to spread"; since he spreads everywhere with his rays, उस्रः (*usraḥ*) means the sun. Here the commentator explains that this sun covers, that is, envelops, everything with his radiance.
अहानि (*ahāni*)—सर्वाण्यागंत्यणि (*sarvāṇyāgaṃtyaṇi*): he has explained it as all the works that may come in future, that is, that will be attained.
In this Ṛk the deities Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, the sun, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni are prayed to, that in what follows, that is, in succession, they may bring about all welfare for us.
notes: ಸಪಿತೃವೇ printed for ಸವಿತೃವೇ

en: That well-known wealth which we desire and which is worth choosing, may the unopposed god Savitā, whom nobody has repelled, bestow on us: this is to be supplied. The rivers, which flow, going along, follow after that wealth; the sense is that they go to give wealth. Since I, the Hotṛ, the one who brings about the oblation of the sacrifice, approach and speak, therefore may they bestow it. And may we, the Ātreyas, be lords of wealth of many kinds, delightful through food or strength. Or else: since I speak, therefore may Savitā come to our desired wealth, and therefore may the rivers too follow the sacrifice, our desired wealth: so it is to be construed. ⟨NOTE:346⟩
notes: printed English "des res" for "desires"; opening bracket missing before "Divine leader"

en: - तत् (*tat*)—that same wealth (to give to us)
- अनु ग्मन् (*anu gman*)—may they come toward us
- उप वोचे (*upa voce*)—approach them and praise
- वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*)—and possessed of delightful wealth of food
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we become (may the gods grant it)

May the unopposed god Savitṛ give us that well-known and desired wealth. May the flowing rivers come toward us, so as to bring us that same wealth. I, the Hotṛ in the sacrifice, approach them for that very reason and praise them. May the gods grant that we become lords of wealth and possessed of delightful wealth of food.

May the irreproachable Savitri (grant) us that desirable (wealth); may the flowing rivers hasten to (convey) it to us; for which purpose I, the ministering priest of the sacrifice, repeat (pious praises): affluent in food, may we be the lords of (manifold) riches.

In this Ṛk the god Savitṛ and the rivers are praised. The word वरूथ (*varūtha*) used here can be given two kinds of meaning. वरूथं । वरणीयमस्मदभिमतं धनं (*varūthaṃ | varaṇīyamasmadabhimataṃ dhanaṃ*): wealth that we desire, this is one meaning. The meaning is that the god Savitṛ and the rivers should give us the wealth that we desire. As regards the rivers, wealth may mean money and material goods. Since the rivers supply water for agricultural work and food and the like is obtained from agriculture, wealth may also be understood as wealth in the form of food and other nourishment. The prayer that they give us these is stated here. In the second meaning, if the word वरूथ (*varūtha*) is taken to mean sacrifice, then, as the Hotṛ prays in the second half of this Ṛk with the sentence उप यद्योचे अध्वरस्य होता (*upa yadyoce adhvarasya hotā*), a petition is stated that the god Savitṛ and the rivers come to this sacrifice that we are performing and give us wealth and the like. This is another kind of meaning. ⟨NOTE:347⟩
notes: ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾಕಮೃತ್ತಿಜಾಂ ನನ್ನೇತ್ಥಾನತಿಥೀನ್ looks damaged in the block; the Kannada gloss has ನ್ಯನ್—ನೇತೃಗಳಾದವರೂ

en: The sacrificers who gave to the Vasus, that is to the gods who have their dwelling at the sacrifice, food in the form of animals, food that is able to move about, and who are good speakers of praise toward the god Mitra and toward Varuṇa: to us, such sacrificers, may great wealth and splendour come near; he explains the verb as "may it approach". O gods, make for them wider, that is more spacious, happiness. By the protection of heaven and earth may we rejoice, that is, be glad. ⟨NOTE:348⟩
notes: ನ್ಯೂನ್ ಅಥಿತೀನ್ / ನ್ಯೂನ್ in the Special Topics against ನ್ಯನ್ in the Pratipadārtha

en: - नमः (*namaḥ*)—food (food in the form of animals)

May great wealth come to us, the sacrificers, who offered food in the form of animals to the Vasus and who offered excellent praises to Mitra and Varuṇa. O gods, bring about the greatest happiness for us, who are devoted in this way. May we be happy through the protection of heaven and earth.

May ample wealth devolve upon those who have presented victims to the Vasus, and upon those who have repeated praises to Mitra and Varuna : confer upon them, (gods), felicity, and may we rejoice in the protection of heaven and earth.

वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*): यज्ञनिवासेभ्यो देवेभ्यः (*yajñanivāsebhyo devebhyaḥ*). Explaining the word vasu as "dwelling", the commentators have taken the word वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*) to mean: to the gods who come to the sacrificial ground to receive the oblations and the like and who dwell there until the sacrifice is completed. सूक्तवाचः (*sūktavācaḥ*) means those who praise the gods such as Mitra and Varuṇa with excellent words. This word is an adjective of the word ये (*ye*) (the sacrificers).

Every mortal should choose the friendship of the leading god, that is, of Savitṛ; "choose" is Sāyaṇa's gloss of the verb. Every man, for the sake of wealth, should be lord of wealth, so Sāyaṇa glosses इषुध्यति (*iṣudhyati*) with ईशीत (*īśīta*). By his favour every person should choose wealth, wealth that is sufficient for nourishment. ⟨NOTE:350⟩
notes: ವೀರಪತ್ನ್ಯಃ printed; Sāyaṇa's block has ವೀರಪಸ್ತ್ಯಃ

en: - इषुध्यति (*iṣudhyati*)—may he look for favour (from Savitṛ)
notes: printed English "saerificial" for "sacrificial"

en: May every man pray for and obtain the friendship of the leading god Savitṛ. May every man gain wealth through Savitṛ's favour alone. For a well-nourished life let him desire wealth from him alone.
Let every man solicit the friendship of the divine leader (of heaven, the sun); let every man desire (of him) riches: let him request affluence (wherewith) to nourish (his descendants).

Although the Viśvedevas are said to be the deity of this sūkta, in all the Ṛks of the sūkta it is the god Savitṛ in particular who is praised. Since Savitṛ is ordinarily invoked in the morning, the time when the sacrifice begins, the seer prays that Savitṛ himself, as guide of this sacrifice which we perform, may see that the sacrificial rite is carried out completely, and that as the fruit of that sacrifice he may bestow on us things that bring happiness, such as a house together with sons and grandsons, wealth, food and the like.

O leader, O god: we the sacrificers are yours, belong to you, and so are those others who are able to praise these (the Hotṛ priests and the rest); they too are yours. Or else, those who are able to praise in turn these others, Indra and the rest, are yours as well. Only one great Self is the deity, namely Sūrya; he is the Self of all beings, and the other deities are included in him; this is the sense. The meaning is that they are not only your praisers. Both of these groups, we, are to be united with wealth: this is the connection. Those indeed are the ones to be connected (with wealth). With all desires may we be united, may we come together. ⟨NOTE:352⟩
notes: ಶಂ ಕರೋಶ್ವಿತಿ ಶೇಷಃ printed in the block

en: - इमान् (*imān*)—the other gods, Indra and the rest
- अनुशसे (*anuśase*)—praise and worship (they too are yours)
- राया (*rāyā*)—may they be joined with wealth
notes: ನೇತೃನಾದ printed
ರಾಯೀ printed for ರಾಯೇ

en: O leader, O Savitṛ, we, these sacrificers, belong to your protection. Not only we, but those here who praise and worship Indra and the other gods are also yours. May both these groups of ours be possessed of wealth; may we be united with all our desires, for the fulfilment of our wishes and for our satisfaction.
Divine leader of heaven), these (worshippers) are yours, and (so are they) who praise these (other gods): these (both) we associate with opulence, we (seek) to unite with (our) des res. ⟨NOTE:355⟩
notes: ಷಳುಷ್ಠಿ ಹಸ್ತಿಸ್ರೋ and ಷಡುಷ್ಟಿಹ in the block read as "six Uṣṇih" following the Anuvāda ಉಷ್ಣಿಕ್; the printed words look damaged

en: इंद्रादीन् शंसितुं प्रभवंति तेऽपि त्वदीयाः (*iṃdrādīn śaṃsituṃ prabhavaṃti te 'pi tvadīyāḥ*). In this Ṛk the god Savitṛ is praised. Therefore the seer says that the people, such as the priests and sacrificers, who praise Savitṛ are dear to Savitṛ. But it may be asked whether it is right, addressing the god Savitṛ, to say that likewise the people who praise Indra and the other gods are also yours. To this the commentator says that Savitṛ dwells in the other gods as their inner self, and that therefore, if the other gods are worshipped, it is as though Savitṛ or Sūrya himself were worshipped, and in support of this he has quoted the sentence एकैन वा महानात्मा देवता स सूर‍्यः स हि सर्वभूतात्मा । (*ekaina vā mahānātmā devatā sa sūryaḥ sa hi sarvabhūtātmā |*). In this way he has made clear that Savitṛ has the feeling that even those who praise Indra and the other gods are his own.

"Therefore", that is, in this sacrifice: for us, the priests, the leaders (न्नेत्थानतिथीन् (*nnetthānatithīn*)), the gods who are honoured like guests, worship all around, serve them. Therefore, in this sacrifice, serve also the wives of the gods, with offerings of oblations and the like. Or else: for us, serve here these three, namely sons, servants and the like as guests, and the wife; O gods, grant them. Far away, at a distance, let him drive every enemy who stands in the path, and the other haters as well; let him separate them, either the company of the gods or Savitṛ, the discriminator who separates all that is mingled. ⟨NOTE:356⟩
notes: ಹವ್ಯಾದಾತಯೇಽಸ್ಮಾಕಂ ಹನಿರ್ದಾನಾಯ printed in the block

en: - अतिथीन् (*atithīn*)—the gods who are to be honoured like guests
- पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*)—the wives of the gods also (worship)
- यूयुविः (*yūyuviḥ*)—Savitṛ, who separates the good from the bad
- पथेष्ठाः (*patheṣṭhāḥ*)—who stand as thorns in our path
- आरे युयोतु (*āre yuyotu*)—may he separate and push far away

Worship exceedingly the gods who are our leaders and who are to be honoured like guests. For that same reason worship also the wives of the gods. May Savitṛ, who separates the good from the bad, separate all the enemies who stand as thorns in our path and push them far away.
Worship, therefore, the leaders (of our rites), our guests, (the gods) and the wives (of the deities): may the (divine) discriminator drive to a distance every adversary, (and all our) enemies.

In this Ṛk the gods are praised together. The commentator has said that the sentence in the first half, अतः नः न्यून् अतिथीन् पत्निः आ दशस्यत (*ataḥ naḥ nyūn atithīn patniḥ ā daśasyata*), can be explained in two ways. For the words न्यून् (*nyūn*) and अथितीन् (*athitīn*) he gives नेत्यन् अतिथिवत्पूज्यान् देवान् (*netyan atithivatpūjyān devān*): the gods who carry out the sacrificial rites or are guides in performing them and who are honoured like guests; so one meaning is: attend, in this our sacrifice, on such gods and on their wives, the wives of the gods. For the words न्यून् (*nyūn*) अतिथीन् (*atithīn*) the ordinary meaning is taken, that is: entertain with worship and the like the human guests who come, or have come, to our sacrifice; this is another kind of meaning. Both these meanings are possible here. ⟨NOTE:357⟩
notes: ವಿಶ್ವೈತಿ printed for ವಿಶ್ವೈಃ

en: In which sacrifice Agni, the carrier of the sacrifice, has been brought to the post, and the animal fit for the post runs toward the post, there Savitṛ, whose mind is on the sacrificer, is "of the house of heroes"; heroes are the priests, the sacrificers, sons, servants and the like, and the house is such as has them; or else, he who has impelled a house; that is, the giver of a house furnished with sons and the like. He is the distributor. He is like a woman skilled in अर्णारणकुशला (*arṇāraṇakuśalā*). Or else: with regard to the oblations (अर्णानि हवींष्यभिलक्ष्य (*arṇāni havīṃṣyabhilakṣya*)) he is the distributor. ⟨NOTE:358⟩
notes: ಸತ್ಯಸ್ತು ತಯೋಽಬಾಧ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ in the block looks damaged; read as ಸತ್ಯಸ್ತುತಯೋ

en: - वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—Agni, the manager of the sacrifice
- दुद्रवत् (*dudravat*)—is carried to the neighbourhood of the post (there)
- नृमणाः (*nṛmaṇāḥ*)—Savitṛ, favourably minded toward the sacrificer
- वीरपत्न्यः (*vīrapatnyaḥ*)—houses furnished with sons and the rest ⟨NOTE:359⟩
notes: ವಿವಿಧಕಾನಾನಾಂ ವಾ ಪೂರಕ in the block looks damaged

en: In which sacrifice Agni, the manager of the sacrifice, has been established and the sacrificial animal fit for the post is carried to the neighbourhood of the post, there Savitṛ, favourably minded toward the sacrificers, like a wife skilled in giving, is the distributor of houses furnished with sons and the rest.

When the victim fit to be bound, the subject (of the sacrifice), has been stationed (at the saerificial post) : he, (Savitri), with mind well disposed towards the worshipper, the donor of dwellings and descendants is like a clever wife, the bestower (of wealth). ⟨NOTE:360⟩
notes: ಸೋಮಪಿತಯೇ printed for ಸೋಮಪೀತಯೇ

en: In this sacrifice that we are performing, Agni stands kindled, established in the Āhavanīya fire-pit on the upper altar. The animal prepared for the sacrifice has also been brought to the post to which it is bound and consecrated with mantras. In such a sacrifice the god Savitṛ, satisfied with the oblations and the like that we offer and with our praises, to show favour to the sacrificer, as a clever woman serves the people of the house, dividing food and other nourishment properly (serving it out), may provide a house made prosperous by sons and the rest and by other kinds of comfort; this is the main intention stated here.

O leader, O god Savitṛ, this lord of the chariot of yours, the protector of all, and the one rich in wealth to be given (the possessive suffix is dropped), "may he make happiness" is to be supplied. And we, for wealth, for happiness, for well-being, that is, for freedom from destruction, praisers of the desirable Savitṛ, we glorify him, we praise. Praisers of the gods, or of the god Savitṛ, we glorify, we praise. ⟨NOTE:361⟩
notes: the Kannada has "Bṛhaspati" for the Ṛk's ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಪತಿ; the list in the Kannada paraphrase reads ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಪತಿ, translated as Brahmaṇaspati in the Ṛk

en: - एषःरथस्पतिः (*eṣaḥrathaspatiḥ*)—this chariot, which is also the protector
- शं (*śaṃ*)—may it be a bringer of happiness (to us)
- इषः स्तुतः (*iṣaḥ stutaḥ*)—we who are praisers of the honoured Savitṛ
- देवस्तुतः (*devastutaḥ*)—we who are praisers of Savitṛ, the god in essence
notes: ಚನ್ನೋರತ್ರ್ಯೋರಧಿಷವಣಫಲಕಯೋಃ in the block looks damaged
ಅನತ್ರೇ printed for ಅಮತ್ರೇ

en: O leader, O Savitṛ, may this chariot of yours, filled with wealth and a protector, bring us happiness. We, the praisers of the god Savitṛ, praise him for wealth, for happiness and for well-being.

Leader (of heaven), may this your protecting chariot, laden with riches, (come for our) happiness : praisers of the honoured (Savitri), we glorify him for felicity through well-being : praisers of the gods, we glorify (them).

In this Ṛk, which forms the conclusion of the sūkta, the seer who saw the sūkta prays that the chariot of the god Savitṛ, the guide, and Savitṛ himself also, may provide us with happiness, wealth and well-being, and says that for this we praise this god.

O Agni, for the drinking of the pressed Soma, that is, for the Soma-drinking, come together with all the protecting gods, Indra and the others, to the one who gives oblations, that is, to the sacrificer, the giver of them; आ गहि (*ā gahi*), come. ⟨NOTE:365⟩
notes: ಋ. ಸ printed for ಋ. ಸಂ.; ಷಶ್ಯನ್ in the quotation as printed

en: - विश्वैति देवेभिः (*viśvaiti devebhiḥ*)—with all the gods ⟨NOTE:366⟩
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations
notes: ಇ. ಚಾ. ೯-೨೫ printed; abbreviation looks misread, probably ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ.; the quotation has damaged words, e.g. ಸತ್ವನಾಂ ನಿತ್ತಿಂ

en: O Agni, for the drinking of the pressed Soma juice, come graciously, together with all the protecting gods, to the sacrificer who gives oblations.
Come, Agni, with all the protecting deities, to drink the libation : come with the gods.

O Ṛtadhītayaḥ, gods whose praises are true or whose deeds cannot be obstructed, come to our sacrifice. And having come, O Satyadharmāṇaḥ, upholders of truth, drink with the tongue of Agni the ghee, the Soma and the rest. ⟨NOTE:367⟩
notes: ಪ್ರಲುಗಶಸ್ತ್ರೇ printed here; elsewhere ಪ್ರಉಗಶಸ್ತ್ರ

en: - ऋतधीतयः (*ṛtadhītayaḥ*)—O gods who have truthful works
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with the mouth of the flame, which is like a tongue
O gods who have truthful works and are upholders of truth, come graciously to our sacrifice and drink the Soma with the mouth of the flame, which is like the tongue of Agni.
(Gods who are) devoutly praised and worshipped in truth, come to the sacrifice, and drink the libation with the tongue of Agni.

ऋतधीतयः (*ṛtadhītayaḥ*)—सत्यस्तु तयोs बाध्यकर्मणो वा (*satyastu tayos bādhyakarmaṇo vā*). Those who are praised with true sentences: the qualities that the praising people have described and extolled in the gods are all true. In the hymns they sing or the descriptions they make there is no exaggeration; this is the intention. Or else अबाध्यकर्माणः (*abādhyakarmāṇaḥ*): no one can obstruct the deeds or the heroic acts that these gods perform; that is, no one is able to hinder or put an obstacle in the way of the gods or of the works they do; this other kind of meaning is also stated here. More or less the same meaning applies to the word सत्यधर्माणः (*satyadharmāṇaḥ*) in this same Ṛk. Or else, the main intention is that they uphold truth alone, that they impel and regulate good people so that they do good works, or that their rules and works always rest on truth alone, and therefore they are called सत्यधर्माणः (*satyadharmāṇaḥ*).

O wise one, O विप्र (*vipra*), who fulfils the various (desires), O Agni who is to be shared, come, together with the gods who come in the morning, with the wise ones of the kind described: आ गहि (*ā gahi*), come. For what purpose? For the drinking of Soma. ⟨NOTE:368⟩
notes: ನಾವರ್ತ್ಯ printed; the sūtra says one of the two twice, so ಆವರ್ತ್ಯ?
ಆ. ೭-೧೮ printed here; ಆ. ೭-೧೦ in the Special Topics

en: O wise and adorable Agni, come graciously, together with the wise gods who come in the morning, to drink the Soma.
Sage and adorable Agni, come with the wise and early-stirring divinities to drink the Soma libation.

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the sacrificial ground together with the gods who come in the morning and to drink Soma with them. Who are the gods who come to the sacrificial ground in the morning? Namely—

प्रातरग्निं प्रातरिंद्रं हवामहे प्रातर्मित्रावरुणा प्रातरश्विना । प्रातर्भगं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं प्रातस्सोममुत रुद्रं हुवेम ॥ (*prātaragniṃ prātariṃdraṃ havāmahe prātarmitrāvaruṇā prātaraśvinā | prātarbhagaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ prātassomamuta rudraṃ huvema ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-1). In this Ṛk the seer Vasiṣṭha says that Agni, Indra, Mitra and Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Soma and Rudra are invoked in the morning. Besides, among these gods it is the custom to invoke chiefly Agni, the Aśvins, Uṣas and Savitṛ in the morning. प्रातर्हि यज्ञमश्विना दधाते प्र शंसंति कवयः पूर्वभाजः । प्रातर्यजध्वमश्विना हिनोत न सायमस्ति देवया अजुष्टं ॥ (*prātarhi yajñamaśvinā dadhāte pra śaṃsaṃti kavayaḥ pūrvabhājaḥ | prātaryajadhvamaśvinā hinota na sāyamasti devayā ajuṣṭaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-77-1,2). In this Ṛk the matter of invoking the Aśvins in the morning is stated. Because Agni is absolutely necessary for sacrificial rites, and because the sacrificial rite begins in the morning, it is well known that Agni too is churned and invoked in the morning, the time when the sacrifice begins. In the same way, since the dawn appears before sunrise, the goddess Uṣas also is a deity of the morning; and since Savitṛ is the rising sun himself, Savitṛ too is a deity of the morning. Therefore Agni is prayed to come to the sacrificial ground in the morning with these gods and to drink Soma. ⟨NOTE:370⟩
notes: ವಸವೋಃ ರಂತ printed in the first line; text possibly damaged

en: This Soma, present before us, pressed between the two चमू (*camū*), that is, the two pressing-boards, is poured around into the vessel; that is, it is filled. And it is dear to Indra and to Vāyu. To drink it, O Indra and Vāyu, come: this is to be supplied. ⟨NOTE:371⟩
notes: ನಾ printed; ವಾ?
reference ೩. ೨-೧೩ printed; ನಿ. ೨-೧೩?

en: This Soma, dear to Indra and Vāyu, is pressed between the two wooden boards (चमू (*camū*)) that are used for pressing out the Soma juice, and is filled into the Soma vessel.
The Soma juice, effused into the ladles, is poured out into the vase, acceptable to Indra and Vayu.

चन्नोः (*cannoḥ*): अत्रोः अधिषवणफलकयोः (*atroḥ adhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ*), "of the two pressing-boards". The Soma plants are crushed with stones and the juice is pressed out. Those stones are called ग्रावा (*grāvā*). In some places they are called अद्रि (*adri*). Some say that अद्रि (*adri*) is a stone broad at the bottom and hollow in the middle like a mortar, and that ग्रावा (*grāvā*) is another stone with which the Soma plants, placed on the stone called अद्रि (*adri*), are crushed. This stone called ग्रावा (*grāvā*) is thick at the base and shaped like a round stone so that it is convenient to hold in the hand. These stones may be compared, more or less, with the pestle and mortar (Pestle & Mortar) that physicians use for grinding medicines and the like. Ordinarily the use of such stones is the more common for crushing the Soma plants and pressing out the Soma juice, and it is their description that is found especially. But in place of these stones wooden boards or pieces are also used. The lower board is somewhat broad and hollow in the middle. Another piece of wood, thick and long, with which the Soma plants placed on it are crushed. These two kinds of wooden pieces are what is indicated here by the word चन्नोः (*cannoḥ*). In this Ṛk and in the next three Ṛks, Indra and Vāyu are prayed to come to the sacrificial ground to drink Soma. In the next Ṛk Vāyu alone is prayed to.

For it is well known that in the sacrifice Vāyu is the first to be entitled to drink Soma, and that for another reason Indra joins Vāyu and the two drink Soma together. In this matter, that is, on how the god Vāyu is entitled to the first drinking of Soma, there is an ancient story in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa. देवा वै सोमस्य राज्योऽग्रपेये न समपादयन्नहं प्रथमः पिबीयमहं प्रथमः पिबीयमित्येवाकामयंत ते संपादयंतोऽब्रुवन् हंताजिमयाम स यो न उज्जॆष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पास्यतीति तथेति त आजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिसृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेंद्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विन् । (*devā vai somasya rājyo 'grapeye na samapādayannahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamityevākāmayaṃta te saṃpādayaṃto 'bruvan haṃtājimayāma sa yo na ujjèṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāsyatīti tatheti ta ājimayusteṣāmājiṃ yatāmabhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyurmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātheṃdro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāvathāśvin |*) (Ai. Brā. 9-25). In ancient times all the gods wished to drink Soma together, and when a dispute arose as to who among them should drink Soma first, a discussion began, each saying that he himself should drink first. Since the matter could not be settled in any way, they all met, deliberated and came to an agreement: "Let us all arrange a contest; whoever wins in it will be entitled to drink Soma first." Everyone agreed to this, and the contest was fixed thus: running from one place to another place far away, whoever first reaches a rock or a tree there is to be considered the winner. When all agreed to the pact that the winner among them should first drink Soma as the victor, all the gods began to run at the same moment. Of all the gods who were running, Vāyu reached the appointed place ahead of all. Indra came right behind Vāyu and was second. Afterwards Mitra and Varuṇa ran behind Indra, and behind them the Aśvins, and they reached the appointed place. Therefore among these gods Vāyu ran ahead of all and became the victor.

सोऽवेदिंद्रो वायुमुद्वै जयतीति तमनु परापतत्सह नावथोज्जयावेति स नेत्त्वब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तृतीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति नेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तुरीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति तथेति तं तुरीयेऽत्यार्जत तत्तुरीयभागिंद्रोऽभवत्रिभाग्वायुः ॥ (*so 'vediṃdro vāyumudvai jayatīti tamanu parāpatatsaha nāvathojjayāveti sa nettvabravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti tṛtīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti neti haivābravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti turīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye 'tyārjata tatturīyabhāgiṃdro 'bhavatribhāgvāyuḥ ‖*). While Vāyu was running, and Indra behind him, the following conversation took place between them. Seeing Vāyu running swiftly, Indra, who was behind him, thought: "This Vāyu will run ahead of all and be the victor. I must somehow run along with him and win", and, using all his strength, ran close to Vāyu.

Yet there was no sign that he would leave Vāyu behind and go forward. Then Indra said to Vāyu: "O Vāyu, we two are ahead of everyone. Therefore let us consider that we have both won, and let us share the first drinking of Soma, half for me and half for you. Let us win the victory together, helping each other." Hearing this, Vāyu said: "O Indra, I am ahead of you, if only by a little. Therefore I alone shall be the victor. In the first drinking of Soma everything must belong to me. I cannot give you half." Then Indra said: "Very well, then I do not want half. Take two of three parts and give me only one part." Vāyu did not agree even to that: "Whatever happens, I shall win. All of it will belong to me, and I do not wish to give you even one part in three." Then Indra again entreated Vāyu: "I do not want even one in three. Still less; it is enough if you give me one in four. Agree at least to that." Vāyu said, "So be it", and agreed. Therefore it was arranged that in the Aindravāyava cup (that is, the vessel in which Indra and Vāyu drink Soma together) Indra should have one part and Vāyu three parts.

तौ सहैवेंद्रवायू उदजयतां सह मित्रावरुणौ सहाश्विन् श एषामेते यथोज्जि तं भक्षा इंद्रवाय्वोः प्रथमोऽथ मित्रावरुणयोरथाश्विनो 8 स एष इंद्रतुरीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते यद्यैंद्रवायवः । (*tau sahaiveṃdravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇau sahāśvin śa eṣāmete yathojji taṃ bhakṣā iṃdravāyvoḥ prathamo 'tha mitrāvaruṇayorathāśvino 8 sa eṣa iṃdraturīyo graho gṛhyate yadyaiṃdravāyavaḥ |*). In this way Indra and Vāyu, helping each other, won the contest and first reached the appointed place. Behind them Mitra and Varuṇa came and arrived. Behind them the Aśvins came. Therefore, among these gods, in the order of the places they obtained in the contest, they became entitled to drink Soma. That is, an arrangement was made that first Indra and Vāyu, then Mitra and Varuṇa, and after them the Aśvins should drink Soma. In this way the order of the cup of two deities (the order in which two deities together drink Soma) came into use. Therefore in the Aindravāyava cup only a fourth part of the Soma-drinking is assigned to Indra. ⟨NOTE:373⟩

तदेतदृषिः षश्यन्नभ्यनूवाच नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिरिति (*tadetadṛṣiḥ ṣaśyannabhyanūvāca niyutvā iṃdrasārathiriti*). The seer, knowing by divine sight that in the Aindravāyava cup Indra has one part in four, expressed this matter in the following Ṛk, that is, in the Ṛk शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*śatenā no abhiṣṭibhirniyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*) (Ṛ. Sa 4-46-2) by the sentence नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*niyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*). ⟨NOTE:374⟩ Here, according to the Nirukta statement नियुतो वायोः (*niyuto vāyoḥ*) (Ni. 2-28), the horses called नियुत (*niyuta*) are well known as the vehicle of the god Vāyu.

Therefore the word नियुत्वच्छब्द (*niyutvacchabda*) indicates a connection with Vāyu. In the Ṛk above the word नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*) indicates Indra together with Vāyu. Mantras such as अधा वायुं नियुतः सश्चतस्वाः (*adhā vāyuṃ niyutaḥ saścatasvāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-1-1) support this. The meaning of the word इंद्रसारथिः (*iṃdrasārathiḥ*) is: Indra, who is the charioteer of Vāyu. Since Indra stands in the place of charioteer to Vāyu, this indicates that Indra has only a fourth part in the first drinking of Soma.

तस्माद्वाप्येतर्हि भरताः सत्वनां नित्तिं प्रयंति तुरीये हैव संग्रहितारो वदंतेऽमुनैवानूकाशेन यदद इंद्रः सारथिरिव भूत्वो दजयत् । (*tasmādvāpyetarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ nittiṃ prayaṃti turīye haiva saṃgrahitāro vadaṃte 'munaivānūkāśena yadada iṃdraḥ sārathiriva bhūtvo dajayat |*) (I. Cā. 9-25). ⟨NOTE:375⟩ The matter stated above is made clear by an example from worldly practice. Warriors in battle sit in chariots and, with the help of their charioteer, win in the battle and seize the wealth and other possessions of the enemies. When they seize them in this way, they give one part of that wealth and so on, that is, one part in four, to the charioteers who helped them. This custom is current in the world. In the same way, in this contest arranged by the gods Indra acted as charioteer to Vāyu and, since Vāyu was the victor, a fourth part of the first Soma-drinking won in the contest became Indra's share. The main meaning is that Indra gained his fourth part as charioteer to Vāyu.

en: This Ṛk, beginning वायवा याहीत्येषा (*vāyavā yāhītyeṣā*), is the first Ṛk of the tṛca addressed to Vāyu in the Praüga-śastra of the third day of the Pṛṣṭha rite. ⟨NOTE:376⟩ The sūtra is cited: the Āśvalāyana text (Ā. Sū. 7-10) prescribes वायवा याहि नीतय इत्येका वायो याहि शिवा दिन इति द्वे । (*vāyavā yāhi nītaya ityekā vāyo yāhi śivā dina iti dve |*). Sāyaṇa explains: O Vāyu, come with regard to the food called Soma, for partaking of it, delighting in it, for the sacrificer who offers the oblation, and on his behalf; and drink the pressed Soma, the food.
notes: abbreviation ಅ. ವೇ, printed

en: - जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—one who bears a mind of favour towards the sacrificer
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—looking to the oblation
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the food in the form of Soma
O Vāyu, who bear a mind of favour towards the sacrificer, deign to come to the sacrificer who offers the oblation, looking to the oblation, for its partaking. Drink the pressed Soma.
Come, Vayu, propitious to the offerer of the libation, to partake of the sacrificial food, and drink of the effused juice.

This Ṛk, वायवा याहि (*vāyavā yāhi*), is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the tṛca (a group of three Ṛks) addressed to Vāyu, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Praüga-śastra on the third day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, वायवा याहि वीतय इत्येका वायो याहि शिवा दिव इति द्वे (*vāyavā yāhi vītaya ityekā vāyo yāhi śivā diva iti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 7-10). For the detailed account we have written on the invitation, in this Ṛk, to Vāyu to be the first of all the gods to drink Soma, see the Special Topics of the preceding Ṛk.

In the Praüga-śastra of the third day of the Pṛṣṭha rite, in the Aindra-Vāyava tṛca, the two Ṛks beginning इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*) are to be recited. The tṛca is to be completed by repeating one of the two, the first or the second. ⟨NOTE:377⟩ The sūtra is cited accordingly (Ā. Sū. 7-18). ⟨NOTE:378⟩ Sāyaṇa explains: O Vāyu, you and Indra are worthy of drinking these pressed Soma juices, those taken in the first place. Since this is so, enjoy and partake of those Soma juices, being free from harm to others. For that purpose come, looking to the food called Soma; the words "come" are to be supplied. Or else the food-like Soma juices are the object of "enjoy".
notes: abbreviation ಆ ವೇ. printed
ವಿವಸ್ಪಂತರೂ printed in the Kannada; the quoted Sanskrit has another form

en: - प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—come looking to the food in the form of juice

O Vāyu, you and Indra as well are worthy of drinking these Soma juices that have been pressed and prepared. Being free from harm, partake of these juices. For that very reason, come looking to this food in the form of juice.
Indra and Vayu, you ought to drink of these libations: be gratified by them, benevolent (divinities), and partake of the sacrificial food.

On the third day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha, for the Aindra-Vāyava tṛca among the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, this Ṛk इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*) and the Ṛk that follows it, सुता इंद्राय (*sutā iṃdrāya*), are to be recited. That is, of these two Ṛks, either the first or the second is to be taken again as the third and the tṛca (a tṛca is three Ṛks) is recited. This matter is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra on repeating one of the two Ṛks (Ā. Sū. 7-10).
For Indra and for Vāyu the Soma juices mixed with curds have been pressed and prepared. O Indra and Vāyu, like rivers to a hollow place, these food-like juices flow towards you.
- वायवे च (*vāyave ca*)—and for Vāyu as well
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—have been prepared (O Indra and Vāyu)
- निम्मं न (*nimmaṃ na*)—as they flow swiftly in low-lying places
- प्रयः (*prayaḥ*)—this food in the form of juice
- अभि यंति (*abhi yaṃti*)—come hastily towards you
For Indra and Vāyu, Soma juices mixed with curds have been prepared. O Indra and Vāyu, as rivers flow swiftly in low-lying places, these Soma juices flow swiftly and come towards you.
The Soma juices mixed with curds are poured out to Indra and to Vayu : the sacrificial viands proceed to you as rivers flow downwards.

दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*)—Soma juice mixed with curds. The Soma juice pressed from the Soma plant is well strained and drunk. This kind of Soma is called pure and sharp. To enhance the taste of the Soma juice it is also drunk after mixing milk, curds or barley flour into the juice. The things mixed into the juice, such as milk, are called आशिर (*āśira*) substances. Therefore it is the custom to speak of Soma juice mixed with milk by one name, Soma juice mixed with curds by another (the one used here), and Soma juice mixed with barley flour by yet another. In the present Ṛk Indra and Vāyu are prayed to drink the Soma juice mixed with curds.

In the Praüga-śastra of the third day, the tṛca beginning सजूर्विश्वेभिरिति (*sajūrviśvebhiriti*) is the one addressed to the Viśvedevas; the sūtra is cited (Ā. Sū. 7-10). Sāyaṇa explains: O Agni, come, united with all the gods, and in equal love with the Aśvins and Uṣas. Like Atri: just as Atri delights in the sacrifice, so delight in the pressed Soma. Or else, as Atri rejoices in the sacrifice, so likewise rejoice in the pressed Soma.
O Agni, united with all the gods, with the Aśvin gods and with the goddess Uṣas, joined in equal love, deign to come. With this prepared juice take delight, like Atri.
Accompanied by all the gods, accompanied by the Aswins, and by Ushas, come, Agni, and, like Atri, delight in the libation.

On the third day of the sacrifice, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, the tṛca beginning सजूर्विश्वेभिः (*sajūrviśvebhiḥ*) (the 8th, 9th and 10th Ṛks of this sūkta) is a tṛca to be recited addressed to the Viśvedevas. This matter is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra on this tṛca (Ā. Sū. 7-10).

सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—For this word Yāska has given the etymology सजूः सहजोषण (*sajūḥ sahajoṣaṇa*) (Ni. 9-15), समानप्रीतिः (*samānaprītiḥ*), "one having equal love"; that is, the sense is: accompanied by the deity who is with him, with mutual love (friendship) and co-operation. In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the place of sacrifice together with the Viśvedevas, the Aśvin gods and the goddess Uṣas.
The ninth and the tenth, two Ṛks, are clear.
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come to this sacrifice
O Agni, united with Mitra and Varuṇa, with Soma and with Viṣṇu, deign to come to this sacrifice. With this prepared juice take delight, like Atri.
Accompanied by Mitra and Varuna, accompanied by Soma and Vishnu, come, Agni, and like Atri, delight in the libation.

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the place of sacrifice together with the deities Mitra and Varuṇa, the Soma deity, and Viṣṇu. The latter half of the preceding Ṛk is recited again in this Ṛk and in the next Ṛk. Saying that the meaning is clear, the bhāṣya-writer has not written a bhāṣya for this Ṛk and for the next Ṛk.
Sāyaṇa has not written a bhāṣya for this Ṛk either.
O Agni, joined with the Ādityas, with the Vasus, with Indra and with Vāyu, deign to come to this sacrifice. With this prepared Soma take delight, like Atri.
Accompanied by Aditya and the Vasus, accompanied by Indra and by Vayu, come, Agni, and, like Atri, delight in the libation.

In this Ṛk Agni is praised, that he should bring along as companions the deities Ādityas, Vasus, Indra and Vāyu. Ordinarily the group of deities called Rudras too ought to have joined the deities called Vasus and Ādityas. But the name of the Rudras is not recited here.

वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—As it is said, अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्या: (*aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityā:*), the Vasus are famed as eight deities, the Rudras as eleven, the Ādityas as twelve. Since the Rudras are not spoken of in this Ṛk, their matter will be explained in another context. Therefore here the matter of the Vasus and the matter of the Ādityas will be explained. Concerning the Vasus Yāska says—

वसवः । वसवो यद्विवसते सर्वमग्निर्वसुभिर्वासन इति समाख्या तस्मात्पृथिवीस्थानाः । इंद्रो वसुभिर्वासन इति समाख्या तस्मान्मध्यस्थानाः । वसव आदित्यरश्मयो विवासनात्तस्मद्दुस्थानाः ॥ (*vasavaḥ | vasavo yadvivasate sarvamagnirvasubhirvāsana iti samākhyā tasmātpṛthivīsthānāḥ | iṃdro vasubhirvāsana iti samākhyā tasmānmadhyasthānāḥ | vasava ādityaraśmayo vivāsanāttasmaddusthānāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 12—42)

Who are the Vasus? Their nature can be known from the meaning of the word Vasu. वसवो यद्विवसते (*vasavo yadvivasate*): those called Vasus clothe themselves with everything, as one puts on a garment; that is, they pervade everywhere. Therefore, because they are deities pervading everywhere, that is, in the three stations called earth, atmosphere and heaven, they are called Vasus. How this is so, he shows through examples. Agni too is called Vāsava, that is, one of the Vasus. Since Agni, that is the sacrificial fire or the terrestrial fire, is established on earth, these Vasus can be called deities of the earth-station. In the same way Indra too is Vāsava, that is, one of the Vasus. Since Indra is a deity of the middle station (the atmosphere), the Vasus can also be called deities of the middle station. Since the rays of the sun are renowned as Vasus, and these rays of the sun are in the heaven-station, the Vasus are also renowned as deities of the heaven-station. In this way the Vasus pervade all three stations (worlds): earth, middle (atmosphere) and heaven. To support this the Nirukta-writer has cited the passage of the Vājasaneya-saṃhitā (Śukla-Yajurveda)—

सुगा वो देवाः सुपथा अकर्म य आ जग्मुः सवनमिदं जुषाणः । जक्षिवांसः पपिवांसश्च विश्वेऽस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि ॥ (*sugā vo devāḥ supathā akarma ya ā jagmuḥ savanamidaṃ juṣāṇaḥ | jakṣivāṃsaḥ papivāṃsaśca viśve 'sme dhatta vasavo vasūni ‖*) (Vā. Saṃ. 1-18)
In this mantra the Vasus are praised as deities of the heaven-station.

ज्मया अत्र वसवोः रंत देवा उरावंतरिक्षे मर्जयंत शुभ्राः । अवाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य । (*jmayā atra vasavoḥ raṃta devā urāvaṃtarikṣe marjayaṃta śubhrāḥ | avākpatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-3) ⟨NOTE:379⟩
In this Ṛk the Vasus are praised as deities of the atmosphere or middle station and of the earth-station.
आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—Yāska has stated the etymology of the word Āditya in this way—
आदित्यः कस्मादादत्ते रसानादत्ते भासं ज्योतिषामादीपो भासेति वादितेः पुत्र इति वा ॥ (*ādityaḥ kasmādādatte rasānādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāmādīpo bhāseti vāditeḥ putra iti vā ‖*) (Ni. 2-13)

(1) आदत्त इति आदित्यः (*ādatta iti ādityaḥ*). The meaning of the word is: one who accepts, grasps or attracts. What does he grasp? He attracts the waters through his rays. The water thus attracted produces rain in the form of clouds. Therefore, because he attracts water through his rays from the ocean and other reservoirs, he is named Āditya.

(2) Or आदत्ते भासं ज्योतिषां (*ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ*). When the sun rises, his light lowers the light of all other things (the moon and the rest) and draws that light to himself; therefore he is named Āditya.
(3) Or आदीपो भासेति वा (*ādīpo bhāseti vā*). Because he envelops and shines in all places or all around (through his rays), he is named Āditya.

(4) Or आदितेः पुत्र इति ना (*āditeḥ putra iti nā*) ⟨NOTE:380⟩. Because he is the son of the goddess Aditi, the mother of the gods, he is named Āditya. This is the main import of the etymology. Whenever the word Āditya is a synonym of the Sun, any of these meanings may be given. But since the plural form आदित्यै (*ādityai*) is used in this Ṛk, here the word Āditya applies not only to the Sun but also to other deities. On this matter the Nirukta-writer himself says—

एवमन्यासामपि देवतानामादित्यप्रवादाः स्तुतयो भवंति । तद्यथैतन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्यार्यण्णो दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति । (*evamanyāsāmapi devatānāmādityapravādāḥ stutayo bhavaṃti | tadyathaitanmitrasya varuṇasyāryaṇṇo dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti |*) (Ni. 2-13)
Praises directed to the Ādityas apply also to the deities Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryamā, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa. That is, having said that these deities too are called Ādityas, he gives as an example—

इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । शृणोतु मित्रो आर्यमा भगो नस्तु विजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*imā gira ādityebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi | śṛṇotu mitro āryamā bhago nastu vijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1)
This Ṛk is given. In this Ṛk Mitra, Aryamā, Bhaga, Dhātā, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa are explained as the Ādityas, and it is stated that they are seven. Besides this—
अथापि मित्रावरुणयोः । आदित्या दानुनस्पती (*athāpi mitrāvaruṇayoḥ | ādityā dānunaspatī*) (Ni. 9-13)
Mitra and Varuṇa too are reckoned as Ādityas. For example—
ता सम्राजा धृतासुती आदित्या दानुनस्पती । सचेते अनवह्वरं ॥ (*tā samrājā dhṛtāsutī ādityā dānunaspatī | sacete anavahvaraṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-6)
In this Ṛk Mitra and Varuṇa are called Ādityas. Besides this—

अथापि मित्रस्यैकस्य । प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् यस्य आदित्य शिक्षति व्रतेन इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*athāpi mitrasyaikasya | pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān yasya āditya śikṣati vratena ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*)
In many contexts, even where only Mitra alone is indicated in the mantra, he is called Āditya. For example—

प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान्यस्त आदित्य शिक्षति व्रतेन । न हन्यते न जीयते त्वोतो नैनमंहो अश्नोत्यंतितो न दूरात् ॥ (*pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvānyasta āditya śikṣati vratena | na hanyate na jīyate tvoto nainamaṃho aśnotyaṃtito na dūrāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-2)
In this Ṛk only Mitra is praised, and he too is addressed as Āditya.
अथापि वरुणस्यैकस्य । अथा वयमादित्य व्रते तव । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम वृणोतीति सतः ॥ (*athāpi varuṇasyaikasya | athā vayamāditya vrate tava | vratamiti karmanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ ‖*) (3. 2-13) ⟨NOTE:381⟩
Just as Mitra is indicated, so even when the single deity Varuṇa is praised in a mantra, in that context too Varuṇa is called Āditya. For example—

उदुत्तमं वरुण पाशमस्मदनाधमं वि मध्यमं श्रथाय । अथा वयमादित्य व्रते तवानागसो अदितये स्याम ॥ (*uduttamaṃ varuṇa pāśamasmadanādhamaṃ vi madhyamaṃ śrathāya | athā vayamāditya vrate tavānāgaso aditaye syāma ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-15)

In this Ṛk Varuṇa is indicated as Āditya. Next, it is necessary to discuss here carefully how many the Ādityas are in number. In the Ṛk इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यः (*imā gira ādityebhyaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2.27-1) given above as an example, there are the names of six deities: Mitra, Aryamā, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa. These are said to be the Ādityas. But the Nirukta-writers have explained the word तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*) as Dhātā: बहुजातश्च धाता (*bahujātaśca dhātā*) (Ni. 12-26). How? They have explained it thus—
तुवीति बहुनाम । सर्वविधातृत्वादबहुजन्मा धाता यावदधिकारं जन्मेति । (*tuvīti bahunāma | sarvavidhātṛtvādabahujanmā dhātā yāvadadhikāraṃ janmeti |*)

The word तुवि (*tuvi*) means many, numerous. Janman means office. The meaning of तुविजात (*tuvijāta*) is Dhātā, the maker of all, who has many kinds of offices. Since the word has been explained in this way, it must be said that in this Ṛk there are seven Ādityas, Dhātā being included. And in the mantra सप्त दिशो नाना सूराः (*sapta diśo nānā sūrāḥ*) the number of the Ādityas is indicated as seven (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3). But the names are not given; only देवा आदित्या ये सप्त (*devā ādityā ye sapta*) is stated. Earlier, when speaking of Aditi, taking up the mantras 10-27-8, 9, it was explained that Aditi had eight sons, that she offered seven of them to the gods, and that she kept the eighth, Mārtāṇḍa, herself and nourished him.

Here too the names of the others besides Mārtāṇḍa are not given. In the Atharva-veda mantra Ath. Saṃ. 8-9-21 ⟨NOTE:382⟩ it is stated that Aditi had eight sons. When explaining the import of the mantra 2-27-1, Sāyaṇa quoted a passage of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka to state their number—

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः............ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वागंश्चेत्येते । (*aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ............tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgaṃścetyete |*) (Tai. Ā. 1-13-3)

As is there, the eight sons of Diti ⟨NOTE:383⟩ are stated. In places such as उदगादयमादित्यः (*udagādayamādityaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.50-12) and उदपप्तदसौ (*udapaptadasau*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.191.9), the identity of Sūrya with Āditya is stated. It is also described that Agni, the son of Aditi, has been established by the gods in the atmosphere in the form of the Sun—
यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्जियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं (*yadedenamadadhuryajjiyāso divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11)

Having stated the nature of the path of the Ādityas with अनर्वाणो ह्येषां पंथा आदित्यानां (*anarvāṇo hyeṣāṃ paṃthā ādityānāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8.18-2), in तत्सु नः सविता भगो वरुणो मित्रो अरमा (*tatsu naḥ savitā bhago varuṇo mitro aramā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8.18-3) the name of Savitṛ is added to the four Ādityas. In some places the seventh place among the Ādityas is assigned to the deity Sūra or Savitṛ (A. Me. 8.2.9; 37 ⟨NOTE:384⟩). In some places Indra too, together with Varuṇa, is counted as an Āditya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-85.4).
तत्र त्वादित्या रक्षतां सूराचंद्रमसावुभा (*tatra tvādityā rakṣatāṃ sūrācaṃdramasāvubhā*)
In such places both the Sun and the Moon are included in the group of the Ādityas.
मात्यादित्यानां दुहिता वसूनां हिरण्यवर्णा मधुकशा (*mātyādityānāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ hiraṇyavarṇā madhukaśā*)

Madhukaśā, who is of golden colour, is called the mother of the Ādityas and the daughter of the Vasus. Thus in each context the relation between Aditi and the Ādityas is shown in a different way. Their relation is explained in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa in this manner.

अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मादनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यॆ धाता चार्यमा चा जायेतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् ॥ सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यॆ मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अगंंशश्च भगश्चाजा- (*aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmādanamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyè dhātā cāryamā cā jāyetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt ‖ sā reto 'dhatta | tasyè mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agaṃṃśaśca bhagaścājā-*)

येतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विविस्वाग्‌श्चाजायेतां ॥ (*yetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivisvāgścājāyetāṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1, 2, 3)

Aditi, desiring sons, cooked an oblation in the form of Brahma's food, addressed to the gods and the Sādhyas. They ate that oblation themselves and gave her the remainder. When she ate it, by its power two sons were born, Dhātṛ and Aryamā. When the same procedure was performed a second time, Mitra and Varuṇa, a third time Aṃśa and Bhaga, and a fourth time Indra and Vivasvat ⟨NOTE:387⟩ were produced. The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa describes these as the Ādityas. Explaining the same matter, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa states it thus—

स मनसा एव वाचं मिथुनं समभवत्स द्वादशद्रप्सान्गर्भ्यभवत् । ते द्वादश आदित्या असृज्यंत तान् दिक्षपादधत् । (*sa manasā eva vācaṃ mithunaṃ samabhavatsa dvādaśadrapsāngarbhyabhavat | te dvādaśa ādityā asṛjyaṃta tān dikṣapādadhat |*) (P. Prā. 6-1-2-8) ⟨NOTE:388⟩

(Prajāpati) had a mental union with Vāk (speech). Then he conceived a womb consisting of twelve drops. Its fruit was the manifestation of the twelve Ādityas. Then he placed them as guardians of the directions, it says. In the same way other śruti passages that tell of the Ādityas may also be studied.

कतम आदित्या इति । द्वादश नै मासाः संवत्सरस्यैत आदित्या एते हीदं सर्वमाददाना यंति ते यदिदं सर्वनाददाना यंति तस्मादादित्या इति ॥ (*katama ādityā iti | dvādaśa nai māsāḥ saṃvatsarasyaita ādityā ete hīdaṃ sarvamādadānā yaṃti te yadidaṃ sarvanādadānā yaṃti tasmādādityā iti ‖*) (Śa. Cā. 11-6-3-8) ⟨NOTE:389⟩

How many are the Ādityas? The Ādityas are twelve in number. There are twelve months in the year. These are the Ādityas; because those months, taking in everything, go forward, they are called Ādityas, it says. The story of the Ādityas is told in this way in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa—

आदित्याश्चांगिरसश्च सुवर्गे लोकेऽस्पर्धंत । तेऽंगिरस आदित्येभ्यः। अमुमादित्यमश्वग्ग् श्वेतं भूतं दक्षिणामनयन् । तेऽब्रुवन् । यन्नोऽवेष्ट । स वर्ज्योऽभूदिति । तस्मादश्वग्ं सवरेत्याह्वयंति । तस्माद्यज्ञॆ वरो दीयते। यत्प्रजापतिरालब्दोऽश्वोऽभवत् । तस्मादश्वो नाम । यच्छ्वयदरुरासीत् । तस्मादर्वा नाम । यत्सद्यो वाजन्थमजयत् । तस्माद्वाजी नाम । यदसुसाराणां लोकानादत्त । तस्मादादित्यो नाम ॥ (*ādityāścāṃgirasaśca suvarge loke 'spardhaṃta | te 'ṃgirasa ādityebhyaḥ| amumādityamaśvagg śvetaṃ bhūtaṃ dakṣiṇāmanayan | te 'bruvan | yanno 'veṣṭa | sa varjyo 'bhūditi | tasmādaśvagṃ savaretyāhvayaṃti | tasmādyajñè varo dīyate| yatprajāpatirālabdo 'śvo 'bhavat | tasmādaśvo nāma | yacchvayadarurāsīt | tasmādarvā nāma | yatsadyo vājanthamajayat | tasmādvājī nāma | yadasusārāṇāṃ lokānādatta | tasmādādityo nāma ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-9.21-1, 2)

In heaven the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases vied with one another. The Aṅgirases offered the Āditya who had the form of a white horse to the Ādityas as a sacrificial gift. Then the Ādityas said to the Aṅgirases, "This Āditya whom you have brought is of the most excellent form." Because the Ādityas said of the horse-formed Āditya स वरः (*sa varaḥ*) (he is excellent), the horse too came to be called सवर (*savara*) in the world. Therefore a boon came to be given in the sacrifice. Prajāpati, offered in the sacrifice, became famed under the horse-names: the first because he is all-pervading, the second because he suffered pain of the eyes, the third because he brought all wealth under his sway; and he became famed as Āditya because he seized (ādatte) from the Asuras all their worlds. Thus the etymology of the word Āditya is stated. Explaining this same etymology, the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka says—
योऽसौ तपन्नु देति । स सर्वॆषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेति । (*yo 'sau tapannu deti | sa sarvèṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyodeti |*) (Śrī. Ā. 1-14-1) ⟨NOTE:390⟩

The Sun who rises takes away (ā+dā) the life-breaths of all beings and rises. Therefore he is Āditya. Thus both circumstances are described: that they are Ādityas by being sons of Aditi, or that they are Ādityas by being distinguished by the act of taking (ādāna). For this word the Nirukta-writers have given an explanation in this way—

आदित्यः कस्मात् । आदत्ते रसान् । आदत्ते भासं ज्योतिषां । आदीप्तो भासेति वा । अदितेः पुत्र इति वा । .... .... ....सूरमादितेयं । एवमन्यासामपि देवतानामादित्यप्रवादाः स्तुतयो भवंति । तद्यथैतत् । मित्रस्य वरुणस्यार्यन्नो दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति ॥ (*ādityaḥ kasmāt | ādatte rasān | ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ | ādīpto bhāseti vā | aditeḥ putra iti vā | .... .... ....sūramāditeyaṃ | evamanyāsāmapi devatānāmādityapravādāḥ stutayo bhavaṃti | tadyathaitat | mitrasya varuṇasyāryanno dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti ‖*) (Ni. 2-13)

As described in सहस्रगुणमुत्सृष्टुमावत्ते हि रसं रविः (*sahasraguṇamutsṛṣṭumāvatte hi rasaṃ raviḥ*) and so on, the name Āditya is famed because he takes in the juice. Not only the juice, he takes in all brilliance. This name is famed either because he is kindled by light or because he is the son of Aditi. But in the Ṛk-saṃhitā the Sun is called the son of Aditi only in one or two places. In places such as दिवि देवाः सूर आदितेयं (*divi devāḥ sūra āditeyaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11) there is this kind of descriptive statement. Besides the Sun, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryama, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa too are indicated as Ādityas. Thus, if the import of the word Āditya is the description of one's own quality, it applies to the Sun alone. If it is to show being a son of Aditi, it applies also to Mitra, Varuṇa and the rest. If the second meaning is given, then how many sons of Aditi there are is not a settled matter. There are statements of number such as six, eight, twelve and so on. Some śruti passages showing this number have been cited above.

In the highest atmosphere the deities famed as Ādityas shine by their own lordship. To know the original form of those deities described in the Vedic literature, the descriptions should not be mixed with the accounts in the Purāṇas and the like. (According to that tradition the twelve Ādityas are those who reflect the twelve months of the year.) They are ageless, immortal, eternal revealers of the principle. Aditi, who is immortal and ageless, is the support of their existence. The dwelling-place of these Ādityas too is immortal light. Therefore whatever forms of brilliance there are in the world-order that is of practical use, revolving, and having the forms of rising and setting, they cannot reflect these eternal Ādityas. The Sun, the Moon and the stars: none of these can reflect this Āditya principle. The import of the opinion of the scholar Roth is that the Āditya principle is the principle that transcends all the masses of brilliance belonging to the practical world.
The epithets that are useful chiefly when Mitra and Varuṇa are indicated are applied also to the Ādityas.
- अनिमिषाः (*animiṣāḥ*) (those who do not move their eyelids)
- दीर्घधियः (*dīrghadhiyaḥ*) (far-sighted, or possessing the power to know the future)
By such epithets and others the Ādityas are described.

en: In the Vaiśvadeva-śastra on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭha rite there is a tṛca beginning "Svasti naḥ". The sūtra is cited, which prescribes it as the Vaiśvadeva tṛca (Ā. 8. 1). Likewise, in the Bṛhaspatisava this tṛca serves as the nivid-dhāna of the Vaiśvadeva, as the sūtra cited (Ā. 9.5) shows. Sāyaṇa explains: may the two Aśvins make welfare, that is, safety from destruction, for us; may Bhaga make welfare; so may the goddess Aditi. Pūṣan, who is unassailed, an Asura in the sense of the remover of enemies and the giver of life-breaths and strengths, may bestow welfare on us. May Heaven and Earth, distinguished by good understanding, make welfare for us.
